Under the totals, where the court has always written the weather and the roads, she writes that coal was sold that year by the cart, by the sack and by the lump, and a new fuel once, from the north.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0005"><em>The last coal sale at the fair</em>, 22 am Faoilleach, DE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1041"><em>Black cake entered at Cùirt na Fèille</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1043"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, DE 3** — *A bough hung on a dark lamp-post* (Cathair dhearg). On the evening of the crowning someone hangs a green bough from the feast of Lùnastal on one of the unlit lamp-posts below the tannery in Cathair dhearg.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0004"><em>The lamp-houses of the capital</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1042"><em>The foot of Cùirt na Fèille's year</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1044"></a>**30 an t-Samhain, DE 3** — *Cùirt na Fèille's winter sitting* (Muileann òg). Cùirt na Fèille at Muileann òg sits its winter day with three cases of short weight in lamp-fuel and none in coal, the first year the book shows it so.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0005"><em>The last coal sale at the fair</em>, 22 am Faoilleach, DE 3</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1043"><em>A bough hung on a dark lamp-post</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1045"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, DE 3** — *Jugged buffalo dearer at Doire shean* (Doire shean). Am Buabhall Fortanach at Doire shean puts the price of its jugged buffalo up by a third, the pot needing a day's slow fire and the coal for it dearer every quarter; the harbour's shipmasters eat it all the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1044"><em>Cùirt na Fèille's winter sitting</em>, 30 an t-Samhain, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1046"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 3** — *Carp steamed over wood at Cuan chrom* (Cuan chrom). The kitchen of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr above Cuan chrom goes back to steaming its carp over wood from the old coal road's thorn hedges, the cook saying the fish never knew the difference.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1045"><em>Jugged buffalo dearer at Doire shean</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1047"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 3** — *Fewer carts past An Taigh-seinnse Reòta* (Muileann fhada). The ostler of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta above Muileann fhada counts through the year a third fewer coal carts on the north road than the year before, and the landlord shuts one of his two stable yards.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1046"><em>Carp steamed over wood at Cuan chrom</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 3</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0008"></a>**20 an Gearran, DE 4** — *The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). A company of shipmasters sets up a works for the making of dubhan at Seann Skell on the southern coast, the first on the island outside the north. On what terms they had the making of it is not told.
- <a id="ev-VI-0009"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 4** — *The high custodian's letter* (Seann Skell). The Àrd-choimheadaiche at Seann Skell writes to every house of the Rite that the new fuel is not forbidden, since it is not coal, and not blessed, since it is not coal. The letter is read in the houses and argued in the druid schools for years.
- <a id="ev-VI-0010"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The Seann Skell works' first year* (Seann Skell). The dubhan works at Seann Skell on the southern coast sell their first year's making to the fishing boats of the south coast and the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg. The works' chimney is the tallest thing on the coast.
- <a id="ev-EVII-1048"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Comann nan Sciobairean leases the salt-sheds at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The company of shipmasters takes a lease of the old salt-sheds on the east side of the harbour at Seann Skell on the southern coast. The sheds have stood empty since the humans' time, the salt trade having gone east, and the town takes the rent gladly. The company brings slack and spoil down the coast in its own hulls and stacks it in the first shed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1049"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Peigi nic Ascaill sees the works at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Peigi nic Ascaill, engineer to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais, comes down from Cathair dhearg to see the dubhan works at Seann Skell on the southern coast. She is shown the heaps, the retorts and a lamp burning the new fuel, and the making-shed is kept locked. When she asks where the company learned the making, its master gives her wine.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0003"><em>The Board's inquiry</em>, 28 an t-Sultain, DE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1048"><em>Comann nan Sciobairean leases the salt-sheds at Seann Skell</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1050"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Tuathaich hands at the southern works* (Seann Skell). The dubhan works at Seann Skell on the southern coast keep Tuathaich hands at the retorts, among them Joe Ashby of Caol mhòr. Five work there in the spring and nine by midsummer. It is rare to see Tuathaich working in the south, and the town's foremen say only that the northern hands know the stuff.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1049"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill sees the works at Seann Skell</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1051"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Peigi nic Ascaill's first report on the new fuel* (Cathair dhearg). Peigi nic Ascaill reports to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais that the new fuel burns clean enough for a lamp and may serve for the five lights, and that the works at Seann Skell will not say how it is made. The report is filed. No answer is written.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1050"><em>Tuathaich hands at the southern works</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1052"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The chimney of Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell finished* (Seann Skell). The brick chimney of Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell is finished at the end of the row of salt-sheds. Its smoke lies along the shore on windy days, and the fishwives of the harbour say the herring taste of it. The town petitions the maor against the reek; the maor answers that the company pays its harbour-due, and the petition goes no further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1051"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's first report on the new fuel</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1053"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *A retort bursts at the southern works* (Seann Skell). In the summer a retort of the dubhan works at Seann Skell on the southern coast splits along its lower seam, and a hand of the town is scalded on the arm. Peigi nic Ascaill, in the town for the lantern-glass of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, draws a baffle for the furnaces and sends it to the works unsigned. The company fits it to every furnace in the row.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1052"><em>The chimney of Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell finished</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1054"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *New glass set in the lantern at Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The lantern of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg on the southern cape is fitted with new glass blown at Seann Skell from the white sand of its own shore, at half the price of the capital's glass. Peigi nic Ascaill orders it in an t-Ògmhios and sees it set in an t-Samhain. The tower still burns the island's coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1053"><em>A retort bursts at the southern works</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1055"><em>Alasdair mac Ìomhair reads his letter in Brìde's house</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1055"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Alasdair mac Ìomhair reads his letter in Brìde's house* (Seann Skell). At Seann Skell on the southern coast Alasdair mac Ìomhair, Àrd-choimheadaiche, reads Litir an Àrd-choimheadaiche himself at the evening lamp in the great house of Òrd Bhrìde, on the day it is sent to every house of the order. The hall is full. Many of those who hear it already burn dubhan lamps at home, bought off the works' carts that summer.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0009"><em>The high custodian's letter</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1054"><em>New glass set in the lantern at Tobar dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1056"><em>The school at Caol shean disputes Litir an Àrd-choimheadaiche</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1056"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The school at Caol shean disputes Litir an Àrd-choimheadaiche* (Caol shean). The school of Feallsanachd an Fhèidh at Caol shean writes that a fuel made from the vein's own waste cannot be called wholly not coal, since the spoil has lain against the seam for a thousand years. The houses of Òrd an t-Seabhaig round Cnoc bheag write that they did not ask the Àrd-choimheadaiche's opinion and are glad to have it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0009"><em>The high custodian's letter</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1055"><em>Alasdair mac Ìomhair reads his letter in Brìde's house</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1057"><em>The south-coast boats buy dubhan at Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1057"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The south-coast boats buy dubhan at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The fishing boats of the south coast come in to Seann Skell from Tobar dhearg and the coves along the shore to load the works' dubhan for their galley-stoves and riding-lamps. It is cheaper than coal by a third. For five years they have burned driftwood and fish-oil, and more than one boat has gone on the rocks for want of a lamp that would stay lit in a gale.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1056"><em>The school at Caol shean disputes Litir an Àrd-choimheadaiche</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1058"><em>The first dubhan barrels go to the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1058"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The first dubhan barrels go to the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg* (Seann Skell). Eleven carts of six barrels each leave the works at Seann Skell on the southern coast for the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg, bought on the lamp-houses' account. They are the first dubhan landed at the capital's lamp-houses, for the poorer streets that have been left dark three winters to save coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0004"><em>The lamp-houses of the capital</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1057"><em>The south-coast boats buy dubhan at Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1059"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's twenty barrels</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1059"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Peigi nic Ascaill's twenty barrels* (Seann Skell). Peigi nic Ascaill buys twenty barrels of dubhan at the works of Comann nan Sciobairean at Seann Skell, entered in the company's ledger to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais on account, without her masters' leave. Joe Ashby chalks a lantern on each barrel. That night she writes asking leave to run a trial of the fuel in a spare lamp below one of the lights for a hundred nights.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1058"><em>The first dubhan barrels go to the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1060"><em>The black ring of the shipmasters</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1060"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The black ring of the shipmasters* (Seann Skell). The hulls of Comann nan Sciobairean bring spoil down the coast to the southern Seann Skell with a black ring painted on their bows, the company's mark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1059"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's twenty barrels</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1061"><em>The locked making-shed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1061"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The locked making-shed* (Seann Skell). At the works at the southern Seann Skell the shed where the dubhan is finished is kept under a padlock the size of a man's fist, opened only for a man with a lamp to go in and out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1060"><em>The black ring of the shipmasters</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1062"><em>Joe Ashby chalks the lights' mark</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1062"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Joe Ashby chalks the lights' mark* (Seann Skell). At the southern works Joe Ashby rolls out twenty barrels held for the engineer of the lights and chalks on each head a square with a flame inside it, the first mark Comhairle nan Taighean-solais ever had.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1061"><em>The locked making-shed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1063"><em>The salt-boilers of Caol ìseal try the cake</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1063"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The salt-boilers of Caol ìseal try the cake* (Caol ìseal). The salt-boilers of Caol ìseal try a cart of the northern black cake under one pan of the low strait; it boils the brine as well as coal and fouls the pan less, and two masters of the pans send north for more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1062"><em>Joe Ashby chalks the lights' mark</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1064"><em>Watch kept from the Cnoc bhàn harbour</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1064"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *Watch kept from the Cnoc bhàn harbour* (Cnoc bhàn). The Tuathaich of Cnoc bhàn keep the pirate watch from their harbour wall through the dark months with fires of the black cake, which burn longer on the wall than driftwood and need less carrying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1063"><em>The salt-boilers of Caol ìseal try the cake</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1065"><em>The ferry of Àth gharbh loses its coal cargo</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1065"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4** — *The ferry of Àth gharbh loses its coal cargo* (Àth gharbh). The ferry at the walled ford of Àth gharbh, which had carried coal across for the eastern farms every week since its making, carries none after the spring; its ferryman takes grain and passengers and raises his fare.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1064"><em>Watch kept from the Cnoc bhàn harbour</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0011"></a>**4 am Màrt, DE 5** — *Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Peigi nic Ascaill, engineer to the Lighthouse Board, fits a dubhan burner to a spare lamp in the yard below Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and runs it for a hundred nights. Murchadh mac Coinnich, retired from the light, keeps the log of the trial for her.
- <a id="ev-VI-0012"></a>**7 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich on the south-west coast fit dubhan engines to the first fishing boats. The Shipwrights' Guild calls the work unlawful for its members. The boatwrights leave the guild and keep the work.
- <a id="ev-EVII-1501"></a>**9 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *Comhairle nan Taighean-solais allows a trial in the yard at Baile ìseal* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The secretary of Comhairle nan Taighean-solais writes to its engineer Peigi nic Ascaill that the Comhairle sees no objection to a trial of her burner in the yard of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, at her own charge, so long as the light is not touched and the keeper not hindered. The letter asks under what head twenty barrels of fuel were entered to the Comhairle's account at Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1502"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *The twenty barrels landed at Baile ìseal* (Baile ìseal). A salt-boat of Àth bheag, coming home empty from Seann Skell of the south, lands twenty barrels of dubhan on the slip at Baile ìseal for the engineer of Comhairle nan Taighean-solais. Her skipper complains of the smell. A carter of Baile ruadh carries the barrels out along the cape to the yard below Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, at twice his rate.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1501"><em>Comhairle nan Taighean-solais allows a trial in the yard at Baile ìseal</em>, 9 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1503"></a>**16 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *The keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal keeps the new fuel off her stair* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Seonag nic Thòmais, keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal, tells the engineer Peigi nic Ascaill that the yard is hers for the trial and the tower's stair is not, and that the new fuel shall not come past the tower door. She names the old keeper Murchadh mac Coinnich to keep the trial's log.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1502"><em>The twenty barrels landed at Baile ìseal</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1504"></a>**20 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *Murchadh mac Coinnich rules the log of the trial lamp* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Murchadh mac Coinnich, seventy-one, keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal for thirty-one years, rules a log-book at his cottage by the yard wall for the engineer's trial, one line to a night, with headings of his own: wind, weather, lit, out, wick, smoke, and what the boats said. He takes an under-keeper's wage for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1503"><em>The keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal keeps the new fuel off her stair</em>, 16 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1505"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *The trial lamp's chimney-glass cracked in a squall* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). On the eleventh night of the trial at Baile ìseal a squall of cold rain off the sea cracks the hot chimney-glass of the trial lamp from top to foot. The flame holds. The engineer puts in a new glass in the rain, and the tinsmith of Àth bheag makes a hood of sheet iron for the lantern, after which the glasses hold.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1504"><em>Murchadh mac Coinnich rules the log of the trial lamp</em>, 20 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1506"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *Calum mac Iain comes home by the trial lamp in the haar* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). On the forty-first night of the trial a haar lies high on the eastern cape and hides the light of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal from the sea. Calum mac Iain, last of the Baile ìseal boats home from the lines, steers in under it by the trial lamp in the yard and finds the slip. He asks the log-keeper not to write it; it is written.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1505"><em>The trial lamp's chimney-glass cracked in a squall</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1507"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, DE 5** — *The trial lamp lit from the Bealltainn fire* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). On the feast of Bealltainn a girl of Baile ìseal carries a pail of the dunes' fire out to the tower, as the town has done for its keepers since the light was lit. At the old keeper's word the engineer lights the trial lamp that night from a spill kindled at the Bealltainn coals, and the log records it so.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1506"><em>Calum mac Iain comes home by the trial lamp in the haar</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1508"></a>**5 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *The coal flame of Baile ìseal fails in a gale and the trial lamp holds* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). On the seventieth night of the trial a south-easterly gale lifts the roof of the coal-store at Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and wets the coal. A down-draught drives the smoke back into the lantern, and the tower's light fails from the second hour after midnight to the fourth while the keeper Seonag nic Thòmais fights the grate. The trial lamp in the yard burns through the night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1507"><em>The trial lamp lit from the Bealltainn fire</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1509"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *Two boats of Baile ìseal come home by the trial lamp* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Two boats of Baile ìseal, caught far out at their lines by the south-easterly gale, come round the eastern cape in the small hours while the tower's light is dark, and steer in by the trial lamp in the yard. One comes in with a torn sail and a man with a broken arm. Both reach the slip.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1508"><em>The coal flame of Baile ìseal fails in a gale and the trial lamp holds</em>, 5 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1510"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *The coal-store at Taigh-solais Baile ìseal new-roofed* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). A roofer of Baile ruadh puts the coal-store at Taigh-solais Baile ìseal to rights after the gale. The secretary of Comhairle nan Taighean-solais answers the keeper's report of the night with a request for particulars of the wet coal and the down-draught, and says nothing of the trial in the yard.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1509"><em>Two boats of Baile ìseal come home by the trial lamp</em>, 14 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1511"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *The hundredth night of the trial lamp* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The trial of the dubhan lamp in the yard below Taigh-solais Baile ìseal ends on its hundredth night, fair with a light west wind. Eleven barrels of the twenty and part of a twelfth have been burned. Murchadh mac Coinnich writes the last line of the log: the boats have said nothing about the lamp, being used to it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1510"><em>The coal-store at Taigh-solais Baile ìseal new-roofed</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1512"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *Peigi nic Ascaill's report to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Peigi nic Ascaill, engineer to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais, sends the Comhairle her report of the hundred nights at Baile ìseal, with Murchadh mac Coinnich's log. It sets the fuel burned against the tower's coal night by night, at the works' price and the pit-head's, and gives the seventieth night in full.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1511"><em>The hundredth night of the trial lamp</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1513"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, DE 5** — *The spare lamp of Baile ìseal fitted with a burner* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Peigi nic Ascaill takes the grate out of the storm-lantern of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and sets in its place a burner of two wick-rings with a coil round the chimney foot to warm the fuel.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1512"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's report to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1514"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *The haar on the forty-first night* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). A haar lies high on the eastern cape; the tower's coal light is lost in it from the slip while the trial lamp below shows plain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1513"><em>The spare lamp of Baile ìseal fitted with a burner</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1515"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *Seonag nic Thòmais asks an engineer's questions* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). On the ninety-sixth night of the trial the keeper of Taigh-solais Baile ìseal comes to the foot of the stage for the first time and asks how the burner is made and what the fuel does to brass. The stair, she says, is still hers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1514"><em>The haar on the forty-first night</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1516"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *Hay stored in the old barracks at Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). The barracks at Inis mhòr, empty of soldiers since An Dealachadh, are let by the maor to the farmers of Seann Vell for hay, the long rooms dry and the rent small.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1515"><em>Seonag nic Thòmais asks an engineer's questions</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1517"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *Sorcha nic Dhùghaill buys a launch's engine at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). Sorcha nic Dhùghaill, boatwright of Caol fhiadhaich, finds in a chandler's yard behind the coal quay at Ros dhomhain the engine of a harbour launch, laid up eight years because its coal cost more than the launch earned. She buys it for the price of old iron, and it is carried down the coast road to her yard on an ox-wain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1518"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *The smith of Caol fhiadhaich makes a dubhan burner* (Caol fhiadhaich). Seonaidh Bàn, smith of the harbour at Caol fhiadhaich, makes a burner of iron with a pipe and a cock to feed dubhan to the engine in Sorcha nic Dhùghaill's rope-shed. He copies it from the stove of a coaster out of Seann Skell on the southern coast, made larger. The south-coast boats have burned dubhan in their stoves and lamps since the works' first year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1517"><em>Sorcha nic Dhùghaill buys a launch's engine at Ros dhomhain</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1519"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, DE 5** — *The keel of An Ròn Dubh bored* (Caol fhiadhaich). At the asking of her skipper Lachann mac Neacail, Sorcha nic Dhùghaill hauls the decked boat An Ròn Dubh up her slip at Caol fhiadhaich and bores the sternpost and deadwood below the water for a shaft, against the guild's first rule, Cha tollar an druim. The other three yards of the town watch from the head of the slip.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1518"><em>The smith of Caol fhiadhaich makes a dubhan burner</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1520"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *An Ròn Dubh crosses the harbour under engine* (Caol fhiadhaich). On a calm evening of an Lùnastal the fishing boat An Ròn Dubh, her engine fed by dubhan, crosses the harbour of Caol fhiadhaich to the wolf-stone and back with her sails furled and her oars shipped. Half the town watches from the wall. It is the first fishing boat of the island moved by an engine.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1519"><em>The keel of An Ròn Dubh bored</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1521"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich return their papers* (Caol fhiadhaich). The four yards of Caol fhiadhaich meet in the net-loft over the fish-store, hear the master's letter read, and answer it in writing: they hold the work lawful and will go on with it, and since the guild holds it unlawful for its members, they are members no longer. Their papers of binding go back to Ros dhomhain with the letter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1520"><em>An Ròn Dubh crosses the harbour under engine</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1522"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes and fines the yards of Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes the four yards of Caol fhiadhaich from its roll and lays a fine on each, the heaviest on Sorcha nic Dhùghaill's yard. None of them pays. The maor of the shire, written to by the guild, answers that a guild's fine is the guild's business.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1521"><em>The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich return their papers</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1523"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *A pilot takes an engine-boat through the strait* (Caol fhiadhaich). After the season's offering at the harbour wolf-stone, Ailig Mòr, eldest of the strait pilots of Caol fhiadhaich, takes An Ròn Dubh out through the skerries under her engine, the first hull the pilots have brought through the strait without sail or oar. At the second skerry she drives across the tide.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1522"><em>Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes and fines the yards of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1524"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *An Ròn Dubh comes home against a south-westerly* (Caol fhiadhaich). Late in an Dàmhair a south-westerly gale catches the fleet of Caol fhiadhaich on the herring banks off the south coast. The sailing boats run for the lee of a headland to the east and lie there five days. Lachann mac Neacail brings An Ròn Dubh home into the wind under her engine and lands the only fresh herring on the coast, sold at Doire shean at dawn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1523"><em>A pilot takes an engine-boat through the strait</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1525"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5** — *All four yards of Caol fhiadhaich fitting engines* (Caol fhiadhaich). By an Dùbhlachd all four yards of Caol fhiadhaich are boring keels and fitting engines to the town's fishing boats, and there are more skippers asking than there are slips. Donnchadh Ruadh, the oldest boatwright of the town, fits his first engine before the year is out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1524"><em>An Ròn Dubh comes home against a south-westerly</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>

## The Years DE 6 – 10

- <a id="ev-VI-0013"></a>**23 an Giblean, DE 6** — *The shipwrights' guild court* (Ros dhomhain). The court of the Shipwrights' Guild at Ros dhomhain rules that the fitting of an engine is no shipwright's work and so outside its charter. The boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich are readmitted to the guild. They decline.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-1522"><em>Comann nan Saor-luinge strikes and fines the yards of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0014"></a>**22 an Cèitean, DE 6** — *The lights turned to dubhan* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). The five beacons of the coast, which have burned coal-lit flame for more than a century, are the first works of the kingdom turned by order to dubhan.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-1512"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's report to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0015"></a>**19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6** — *The last coal flame* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The coal flame of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg is borne in a closed lantern to the Rite's house at Seann Skell and let burn out on the altar. Custodians from four shires attend, and Ciorstaidh nic Artair, keeper of the light, carries the lantern.
- <a id="ev-EVII-1526"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, DE 6** — *Three yards of the south-west coast follow* (Inis chrom). In the first months of the year the yards of Inis chrom, Doire shean and a third harbour of the south-west coast send to Caol fhiadhaich to learn how the engines are fitted, and begin the same work. They too leave Comann nan Saor-luinge or are struck from it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0013"><em>The shipwrights' guild court</em>, 23 an Giblean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1525"><em>All four yards of Caol fhiadhaich fitting engines</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 5</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1527"></a>**8 an Lùnastal, DE 6** — *Launch engines dear at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). No one on the island makes engines for boats, and the yards of the south-west buy the engine out of every laid-up launch in the harbours of the capital country. The chandlers of Ros dhomhain, who sold such engines for old iron the summer before, ask three times the price by am Màrt and five times by an Giblean.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1526"><em>Three yards of the south-west coast follow</em>, 26 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1528"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, DE 6** — *The guild summons the boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich* (Caol fhiadhaich). Early in an Giblean Comann nan Saor-luinge summons the boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich to its court at Ros dhomhain to hear its ruling on the matter of the engines. The four yards send Sorcha nic Dhùghaill to answer for all of them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0013"><em>The shipwrights' guild court</em>, 23 an Giblean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1527"><em>Launch engines dear at Ros dhomhain</em>, 8 an Lùnastal, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1529"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, DE 6** — *Sorcha nic Dhùghaill declines readmission* (Ros dhomhain). In the guild hall above the slips at Ros dhomhain, when the master Pàdraig mac an t-Saoir has read the ruling and remitted the fines, Sorcha nic Dhùghaill answers for the four yards of Caol fhiadhaich that they bored the keels as shipwrights and have no need of a shipwrights' guild that disowns the work. The clerk writes that they decline.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0013"><em>The shipwrights' guild court</em>, 23 an Giblean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1528"><em>The guild summons the boatwrights of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1530"></a>**21 an Lùnastal, DE 6** — *Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell watch the guild court* (Ros dhomhain). A man sent from the dubhan works at the southern Seann Skell sits at the court of Comann nan Saor-luinge at Ros dhomhain beside a clerk of the lights, to hear what it says of engines.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0013"><em>The shipwrights' guild court</em>, 23 an Giblean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1529"><em>Sorcha nic Dhùghaill declines readmission</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1531"></a>**1 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *An Ròn Dubh laid up for the winter* (Caol fhiadhaich). The shaft-boat An Ròn Dubh is drawn up the slip at Caol fhiadhaich for the winter, and the shipwrights of the town come down one at a time to look at the bored post.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1530"><em>Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell watch the guild court</em>, 21 an Lùnastal, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1532"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *Baile ghorm's boats follow Caol fhiadhaich* (Baile ghorm). Two skippers of Baile ghorm, who had seen An Ròn Dubh come home against a south-westerly, send to the southern works for burners and to Caol fhiadhaich for a boatwright who will bore a keel.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0012"><em>The fishing boats of Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 7 an t-Sultain, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1531"><em>An Ròn Dubh laid up for the winter</em>, 1 an t-Sultain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1533"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *The pilots of Seann Warr ask for an engine boat* (Seann Warr). The pilots of the walled harbour of Seann Warr ask their maor for a pilot-boat with an engine, to meet ships in a calm; the maor answers that the town will pay for one when the shipwrights' guild allows one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0013"><em>The shipwrights' guild court</em>, 23 an Giblean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1532"><em>Baile ghorm's boats follow Caol fhiadhaich</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1534"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *The order to turn the lights read at Comhairle nan Taighean-solais* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Comhairle nan Taighean-solais sits and hears the council's order that the five lights of the coast be turned to dubhan and their coal given to the altars. Taigh-solais Baile ìseal and Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, nearest the works at Seann Skell, are to be turned first, in the summer; the keepers keep their warrants, wages and houses.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1535"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *The custodians of Tobar dhearg ask for the flame* (Tobar dhearg). The custodians of Tobar dhearg, who keep the light's log for Brìde's sake, ask the Àrd-choimheadaiche that the coal flame of their light be carried to Brìde's altar at Seann Skell and burn out there. He consents, and Comhairle nan Taighean-solais makes no objection, so long as the light is not dark a single night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0009"><em>The high custodian's letter</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1536"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, DE 6** — *Ciorstaidh nic Artair refuses a deputy for the lantern* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). Offered a clerk of the lights or a young custodian of Seann Skell to carry the flame the nine and a half miles to the altar, Ciorstaidh nic Artair, keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, writes that the flame is hers by her warrant until the burner is lit, and that she will carry it herself. The answer leaves the matter to her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1535"><em>The custodians of Tobar dhearg ask for the flame</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1537"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, DE 6** — *Taigh-solais Baile ìseal turned to dubhan* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The burner Peigi nic Ascaill tried in the yard below Taigh-solais Baile ìseal is set in the tower's lantern by order, the first of the five lights to burn dubhan. Its keeper Seonag nic Thòmais, who would not have the thing up her stair, keeps the light under it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1536"><em>Ciorstaidh nic Artair refuses a deputy for the lantern</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1538"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, DE 6** — *The tank landed at the cape of Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). A works boat from Seann Skell lands an iron tank, a burner, pipes and forty barrels of dubhan on the stones below Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg. Eight men of the village bring the tank up the landing-stones and the stair, and the barrels stand against the tower wall where the coal-sacks stood.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1537"><em>Taigh-solais Baile ìseal turned to dubhan</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1539"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, DE 6** — *The trial of the burner at Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). Peigi nic Ascaill lights the new burner in the lantern of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg for an hour beside the coal grate. The light is white and steady and throws the shadows of the lantern's bars across the cape; the boats at sea come in to ask what has happened. The grate burns on alone until the day of the carrying.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1538"><em>The tank landed at the cape of Tobar dhearg</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1540"></a>**3 an t-Samhain, DE 6** — *The last coal night at Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). On the night before the carrying the keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg burns the last of the quarter's coal, a sack and a half, as high as the grate will take it. At dawn she lights the closed lantern from the grate and lets the tower's fire go out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1539"><em>The trial of the burner at Tobar dhearg</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1541"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, DE 6** — *The walk from the cape to Seann Skell* (Tobar dhearg). Ciorstaidh nic Artair carries the lantern on foot from the cape by Baile gharbh to Seann Skell, nine and a half miles in the heat, and gives it to no one. Some thirty people of Tobar dhearg walk behind her with the three custodians of the village; at the town's edge a young custodian of the house leads her up to Brìde's house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1540"><em>The last coal night at Tobar dhearg</em>, 3 an t-Samhain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1542"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, DE 6** — *The first dubhan night at Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). On the evening of the carrying the under-keeper of Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg lights the dubhan burner at sunset, as the keeper ordered, with the keeper away at Seann Skell. The new light is seen white and steady from the quays of Seann Skell, nine miles up the coast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1541"><em>The walk from the cape to Seann Skell</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1543"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, DE 6** — *The Àrd-choimheadaiche blesses the lantern* (Seann Skell). When the coal flame of Tobar dhearg has burned out on Brìde's altar, Alasdair mac Ìomhair closes the lantern, says the words for a lamp of the vein's coal let go out, and blesses the lantern while he neither blesses nor forbids the new light. He gives the lantern back to its keeper at her asking.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0009"><em>The high custodian's letter</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1542"><em>The first dubhan night at Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1544"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, DE 6** — *The song of the last flame first sung at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). In a tavern under the quay wall at Seann Skell a skipper of Tobar dhearg makes and sings a song of the carrying on the night of it. It gathers many verses before morning, and by the summer's end every harbour of the south coast has its own; the first verse, of the flame gone out of the tower, is sung wherever it is sung.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1543"><em>The Àrd-choimheadaiche blesses the lantern</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1545"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 6** — *The bell-post on the reef below Tobar dhearg* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). The reef below Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg, where Ciorstaidh nic Artair's father drowned, carries the bell-post she had driven there; no boat goes aground on it while she keeps the light.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1544"><em>The song of the last flame first sung at Seann Skell</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1546"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 6** — *The last quarter's coal burned high* (Taigh-solais Tobar dhearg). On her last night with the coal flame Ciorstaidh nic Artair burns the last sack and a half of the quarter's coal as high as it will burn, and the boats out that night see the light burn higher than in years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1545"><em>The bell-post on the reef below Tobar dhearg</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1547"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 6** — *Brìde's house at Caol ruadh keeps its own coal* (Caol ruadh). The house of Brìde at Caol ruadh, which keeps the orthodox rite of the flame, buys two years' altar coal ahead from the last carters of the southern road and stores it in the undercroft, lest the coal fail before the rite does.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0015"><em>The last coal flame</em>, 19 an t-Iuchar, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1546"><em>The last quarter's coal burned high</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 6</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0016"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, DE 7** — *Taigh-solais Muileann bheag converted* (Taigh-solais Muileann bheag). The beacon at Muileann bheag on the Tuathaich north coast is turned to dubhan with the others. Its fuel is carted from the north; of the five lights it alone is not fed by sea from Seann Skell.
- <a id="ev-VI-0017"></a>**25 am Màrt, DE 7** — *Taigh-solais Àth dhearg converted* (Taigh-solais Àth dhearg). At Taigh-solais Àth dhearg on the north-east cape the work takes a month longer than at the others, for the stair is too narrow for the new tank. The tank is lifted to the lamp-room from outside by a crane borrowed from the rope-walk at Seann Tarr.
- <a id="ev-VI-0018"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7** — *Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted* (Taigh-solais Baile chrom). At Taigh-solais Baile chrom on the Tuathaich coast the work is done by Tuathaich fitters from Caol mhòr, for the Lighthouse Board has none of its own to send so far. The keeper's report names none of them.
- <a id="ev-VI-0019"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The lamp-makers turn* (Muileann mhin). The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin begin to make dubhan lamps and ask leave to set their guild mark on them. After a year's argument the guild court allows it. The flame over the hammer is kept.
- <a id="ev-EVII-1548"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The dubhan for Muileann bheag bought at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Peigi nic Ascaill, engineer to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais, buys the fuel for Taigh-solais Muileann bheag in the market at Caol mhòr, since no master will take a laden hull round the western capes in am Faoilleach. Twelve Tuathaich carts carry the barrels fifteen miles along the coast road to the tower. The carters are paid at the rate of the town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0016"><em>Taigh-solais Muileann bheag converted</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1549"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The coal-store at Muileann bheag locked* (Taigh-solais Muileann bheag). When Taigh-solais Muileann bheag is lit with dubhan, its keeper Calum Bàn, a Dia-thìreach of the south who has kept the light nineteen years, locks the last of its coal in the store at the tower's foot until Comhairle nan Taighean-solais shall say what is to be done with it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0016"><em>Taigh-solais Muileann bheag converted</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0014"><em>The lights turned to dubhan</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 6</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1548"><em>The dubhan for Muileann bheag bought at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1550"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The crane walked from Seann Tarr to Àth dhearg* (Seann Tarr). The rope-makers of Seann Tarr take down the crane of their rope-walk and carry it three and a half miles up the coast road to Taigh-solais Àth dhearg in pieces, on three wains. They raise it on the rock below the tower in two days and stay it to rings let into the stone. They will let no other hands touch their cables.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0017"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg converted</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <em>The rope-makers of Seann Tarr</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0182">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 53</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1549"><em>The coal-store at Muileann bheag locked</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1551"><em>The rope-makers refuse hire for the crane</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1551"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The rope-makers refuse hire for the crane* (Seann Tarr). When the tank of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg is set in its lamp-room, the rope-makers of Seann Tarr take their crane home and will take no hire for it. Their master sends word that the light owes them nothing, since their boats steer home by it. The keeper Iseabail Ruadh names the rope-walk in her daybook.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0017"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg converted</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1550"><em>The crane walked from Seann Tarr to Àth dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1552"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Caol mhòr for fitters</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1552"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Caol mhòr for fitters* (Àth dhearg). Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais that she cannot turn the light at Baile chrom before the autumn gales with the two fitters it can spare. In her own name she writes to the speaker at Caol mhòr, asking four Tuathaich fitters of the town for the work and a man named Ashby among them. She does not say who will pay them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1551"><em>The rope-makers refuse hire for the crane</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1553"><em>Four fitters of Caol mhòr walk to Baile chrom</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1553"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *Four fitters of Caol mhòr walk to Baile chrom* (Caol mhòr). Daniel Frayne, speaker of Tional nan Tuathach, sends four fitters of Caol mhòr to turn the light at Baile chrom: Joe Ashby, Will Tanner and the cousins Ned and Abel Fowler. They walk the twenty-five miles in two days of rain. The tank and fuel come round by sea from Seann Skell and are landed below the headland.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1552"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill writes to Caol mhòr for fitters</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1554"><em>The Tuathaich fitters paid by Tional nan Tuathach</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1554"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The Tuathaich fitters paid by Tional nan Tuathach* (Caol mhòr). The clerk of Tional nan Tuathach at Caol mhòr pays the four fitters who turned the light at Baile chrom from the assembly's chest, for nine days' work and four days' walking, and enters their names and the sum in its book. He writes to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais for the money, and enters the sum as owed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1553"><em>Four fitters of Caol mhòr walk to Baile chrom</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1555"><em>The keeper's report pinned at Caol mhòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1555"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The keeper's report pinned at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). The quarter-day report of Uilleam mac Dhòmhnaill, keeper of Taigh-solais Baile chrom, is copied by Comhairle nan Taighean-solais and sent round the shires. At Caol mhòr the maor pins it outside the custom-house. It says the light burns well and the town gives no trouble, and that the work was done by fitters from Caol mhòr. It names none of them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <em>The keepers of the five lights</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0075">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1554"><em>The Tuathaich fitters paid by Tional nan Tuathach</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1556"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill takes service with the works</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1556"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *Peigi nic Ascaill takes service with the works* (Seann Skell). Peigi nic Ascaill leaves the service of Comhairle nan Taighean-solais at the end of the summer and takes service as master-fitter with Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell, the shipmasters' works on the south coast, which are building a second range of retorts.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0011"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill's trial lamp</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 5</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1555"><em>The keeper's report pinned at Caol mhòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1557"><em>Joe Ashby hired at the works</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1557"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *Joe Ashby hired at the works* (Caol mhòr). Joe Ashby of Caol mhòr goes south in an t-Sultain at Peigi nic Ascaill's letter and is hired as a fitter at the shipmasters' works at Seann Skell on the south coast, with Ned and Abel Fowler. He is given a room over the forge. Will Tanner stays at Caol mhòr with his boat.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1556"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill takes service with the works</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1558"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The first dubhan pit-lamps of Muileann mhin* (Muileann mhin). The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin, working from a burner drawn by Peigi nic Ascaill, make their first twelve pit-lamps to burn dubhan. Orders come for a hundred, from the pits still worked, from the yards of Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn and from the inns of the old roads. The guild will not yet stamp them with its mark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0019"><em>The lamp-makers turn</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <em>The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0064">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 14</a>; ← Follows from <em>The coal-lamp shortage</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0213">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 63</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1559"><em>Two fitters sign the lamp-makers' petition</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1559"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *Two fitters sign the lamp-makers' petition* (Muileann mhin). At the guild's hall of Muileann mhin, Peigi nic Ascaill, master-fitter of Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell, signs the lamp-makers' petition to the guild court as the one who drew the burner, and Joe Ashby, fitter, of Caol mhòr, signs under her. The guild's master carries the petition to the court the same afternoon.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0019"><em>The lamp-makers turn</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1558"><em>The first dubhan pit-lamps of Muileann mhin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1560"><em>The Baile chrom burner mended on a smith's anvil</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1560"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The Baile chrom burner mended on a smith's anvil* (Baile chrom). A burner bent on the voyage round the western capes is straightened by Joe Ashby and the smith of Baile chrom behind a shut door; Joe pays the smith from his own pocket.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0018"><em>Taigh-solais Baile chrom converted</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1559"><em>Two fitters sign the lamp-makers' petition</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1561"><em>The harbour carts of Àth naomh blessed as before</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1561"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The harbour carts of Àth naomh blessed as before* (Àth naomh). At Àth naomh in the Cuan shean shire the harbour carts are blessed at the spring as every year, horses and all; a carter who has put a dubhan lamp on his tail-board asks whether it too is blessed, and the priest says it is on the cart.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1560"><em>The Baile chrom burner mended on a smith's anvil</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-1562"><em>The stone of Cnoc bheag scrubbed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-1562"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7** — *The stone of Cnoc bheag scrubbed* (Cnoc bheag). The town of Cnoc bheag has its carved stone scrubbed of a century's coal-smoke for the midsummer fair, and finds under the black a second band of carving no one living had seen.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-1561"><em>The harbour carts of Àth naomh blessed as before</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0020"></a>**9 am Faoilleach, DE 8** — *Daniel Frayne dies* (Muileann leathan). Daniel Frayne, speaker of the Moot, dies at Muileann leathan. The Moot chooses Martha Greaves of Doire ghlas, a mill manager, to follow him.
- <a id="ev-VI-0021"></a>**24 an Gearran, DE 8** — *The binders of Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). The Moot sends Daniel Frayne's pupils, the binders of Muileann leathan, to rebind its minute-books from the first meeting. The rebound set is kept at Caol mhòr. A second set is made and hidden, says the Moot's minute, elsewhere.
- <a id="ev-VI-0022"></a>**1 an Cèitean, DE 8** — *The coal line's first dubhan engine* (Muileann chrom). The Rail Board runs its first dubhan engine on the coal line, from the yards at Muileann chrom to Cathair dhearg. It carries no coal. It carries dubhan to the lamp-houses of the capital, and comes back empty.
- <a id="ev-VI-0023"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The eastern salt-road* (Àth bheag). For the first time salt from Àth bheag goes to the inland towns by dubhan lorry, on the drove road past Baile ìseal. Within a few years the drovers of the east coast sell their oxen.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2001"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Daniel Frayne buried at Muileann leathan* (Muileann leathan). Daniel Frayne, speaker of Tional nan Tuathach, is buried in the churchyard of Muileann leathan. His eleven binders carry the coffin through the town by turns, and each drops a length of waxed binding-thread into the grave. The schoolchildren of Doire ghlas sing the hymn of the sea road, and delegates of the fishing, mill and hill towns stand in the rain along the churchyard wall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0020"><em>Daniel Frayne dies</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>Daniel Frayne's copying school</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0168">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 48</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2002"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Martha Greaves's first sitting as speaker* (Caol mhòr). Tional nan Tuathach sits at Caol mhòr, forty-four delegates strong, and chooses Martha Greaves of Doire ghlas by show of hands; the one other name put is withdrawn. She says she is no talker. Her first business is Daniel Frayne's dying wish that his binders rebind the minute-books, and the matter is laid over for their reckoning. Her first minute is the shortest of the year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0020"><em>Daniel Frayne dies</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0008">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2001"><em>Daniel Frayne buried at Muileann leathan</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2003"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The binders' reckoning* (Muileann leathan). The binders of Muileann leathan send the speaker their reckoning for rebinding the minute-books: sixty-three books, with thread, board, hide and paste set down by weight. They charge nothing for their hands. The mills of Doire ghlas undertake to give the hide.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Doire ghlas mills</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0202">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 59</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2002"><em>Martha Greaves's first sitting as speaker</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2004"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Ellen Marsh offers her schoolroom* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh, teacher at Agnes Pike's old school in Doire ghlas, writes to Tional nan Tuathach offering her schoolroom for the rebinding of its books, since the bindery at Muileann leathan is being cleared by Daniel Frayne's kin. The children are to be taught in the church meanwhile, and the priest agrees.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>Agnes Pike's school</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0066">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2003"><em>The binders' reckoning</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2005"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The minute of the second set signed* (Caol mhòr). At the same sitting the eldest binder lays before the chair the wording of a minute: that a second set of the books is made and hidden elsewhere, and that the minute stands as all the gathering knows of it. No delegate says where. Martha Greaves has it copied as written and signs it without asking.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2004"><em>Ellen Marsh offers her schoolroom</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2006"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Peter Hale carries the books to Doire ghlas* (Caol mhòr). Peter Hale, delegate of Caol mhòr and great-grandson of Walter Hale, carries the sixty-three minute-books to Doire ghlas in three tea-chests lined with oilcloth, walking beside the cart the nine miles. The schoolchildren line up under the grey oaks to see them carried in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>Walter Hale dies</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0127">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 33</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2005"><em>The minute of the second set signed</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2007"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The bindery in Agnes Pike's school* (Doire ghlas). The binders of Muileann leathan bring their presses and sewing frames to the schoolroom at Doire ghlas and take every minute-book out of its boards before any is sewn again. The loose gatherings of seventy-seven years are laid out under weights down the length of the floor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>Agnes Pike's school</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0066">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2006"><em>Peter Hale carries the books to Doire ghlas</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2008"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Walter Hale's harbour ledger* (Doire ghlas). Unstitching the first minute-book, the binders find it to be a harbour ledger of the humans' time: Walter Hale cut out his old masters' tonnage and dues close to the fold and wrote the first day of Tional nan Tuathach on the next clean page. The speaker orders the stubs kept in the new binding.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0008">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2007"><em>The bindery in Agnes Pike's school</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2009"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The last of the sixty-three books sewn* (Doire ghlas). The binders finish the last rebound minute-book at Doire ghlas, Daniel Frayne's own, which ends in the middle of a page and is followed by the clerk's minute of his death. Each book is covered in Doire ghlas hide and lettered on the spine with its years alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0020"><em>Daniel Frayne dies</em>, 9 am Faoilleach, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2008"><em>Walter Hale's harbour ledger</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2010"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The rebound set laid in the press at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Martha Greaves lays the sixty-three rebound minute-books in the delegates' press at Caol mhòr with her own hands, in order from Walter Hale's ledger to Daniel Frayne's last book, locks it, and keeps the key on her ring with the keys of the mills. The minute records the books laid in, at the cost of the binders' thread.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0021"><em>The binders of Muileann leathan</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Moot at Caol mhòr</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0008">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 2</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2009"><em>The last of the sixty-three books sewn</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2011"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Lamp-glass dearer at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The glass-houses of Cathair dhearg raise the price of a chimney-glass by a third in the year the dubhan lamps come into the lanes, and cannot blow them fast enough.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2010"><em>The rebound set laid in the press at Caol mhòr</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2012"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The new engine hauled to Muileann chrom* (Seann Skell). An engine of the new kind, bought by Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn from the shipmasters' works at the southern Seann Skell, comes up the old road to Muileann chrom on a low wagon. Twelve horses of Òrd Mhacha draw it for two days, a priest of the order walking at their head, and at the ford below the town he stands in the water until they take it out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0008"><em>The shipmasters' works at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Gearran, DE 4</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2013"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The first dubhan tank at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's men set an iron tank on stone piers at the end of the long siding at Muileann chrom and fill it from barrels carted up from the southern Seann Skell. It is the first dubhan tank Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn owns. The families of the yard rows complain of the reek, which clings to cloth.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ○ Same place <em>The shunting yards at Muileann chrom</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0058">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2012"><em>The new engine hauled to Muileann chrom</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2014"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Eachann mac Ruairidh learns the dubhan engine* (Muileann chrom). Eachann mac Ruairidh, a driver of the yard families at Muileann chrom, alone puts his name to Comhairle nam Mèinnean's notice asking for a man to learn the new engine. Two fitters of the southern Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell teach him, one of them a Tuathach of Caol mhòr, Will Garside. In a month he drives it to An Sloc Mòr and back without them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2013"><em>The first dubhan tank at Muileann chrom</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2015"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The lamp-makers at the fence* (Muileann mhin). As the first dubhan train of Slighe a' Ghuail passes Muileann mhin on its way to Cathair dhearg, the lamp-makers of Comann nan Lòchran come out of their shops and stand along the fence of the last field in their aprons to watch it go by. One of them holds up a new dubhan lamp, unlit.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0019"><em>The lamp-makers turn</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2014"><em>Eachann mac Ruairidh learns the dubhan engine</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2016"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *An old driver will not ride* (Muileann chrom). At dusk on the day of the first dubhan train, Ruairidh mac Eachainn, who drove coal engines on the line for forty years, is asked by his son to ride the new engine to the points and back. He refuses, saying he will not ride behind a fire he cannot see into, and walks home to the yard rows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2015"><em>The lamp-makers at the fence</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2017"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *A fireman struck from the roll* (Muileann chrom). In an t-Ògmhios Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn takes a second fireman off its roll at Muileann chrom and puts no one in his place, the dubhan engine needing none and the trains from An Sloc Mòr growing fewer. The man, a fireman of nineteen years, goes down to the river landing to seek work on the boats.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2016"><em>An old driver will not ride</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2018"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *A boy of the yard rows killed* (Muileann chrom). Ailean mac Mhathain, fourteen, of the yard families at Muileann chrom, is crushed between two dubhan tank-wagons being moved by rope and pinch-bar to make room for a second tank. Comhairle nam Mèinnean's clerk enters his death in the yard book as an accident in the changeover. The rows bury him in their corner of the burial ground below the mill.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <em>The shunting yards at Muileann chrom</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0058">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2017"><em>A fireman struck from the roll</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2019"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *A salt-master of Àth bheag buys a lorry* (Àth bheag). In the autumn a salt-master of Àth bheag buys a lorry from the works at the southern Seann Skell. It comes up the coast road on its own wheels with a fitter driving and a barrel of dubhan roped behind the seat. The drovers of the east coast go down to the ford of the Abhainn dhubh to look at it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0023"><em>The eastern salt-road</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <em>Salt-pans of Àth bheag</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0124">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 32</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2018"><em>A boy of the yard rows killed</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-2020"><em>Salt of Àth bheag sent west by Slighe a' Ghuail</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2020"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *Salt of Àth bheag sent west by Slighe a' Ghuail* (Muileann chrom). The salt-master's lorry brings a second load of salt to the yard at Muileann chrom, and Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn sends it on to Cathair dhearg in a covered wagon behind the empty dubhan tanks. It is the first load the dubhan engine carries towards the capital that is not dubhan, and the first freight it pulls that pays.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0023"><em>The eastern salt-road</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2019"><em>A salt-master of Àth bheag buys a lorry</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-2021"><em>The blessing for a horse said over an engine</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2021"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8** — *The blessing for a horse said over an engine* (Muileann chrom). Before the first dubhan train leaves the yard at Muileann chrom the priest of Macha says over it the blessing for a horse setting out on a long road, since none has been made for an engine.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2020"><em>Salt of Àth bheag sent west by Slighe a' Ghuail</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0024"></a>**22 am Màrt, DE 9** — *Achadh mhòr's drovers* (Achadh mhòr). The drovers of Achadh mhòr in the south, with no oxen left to drive, buy lorries. The drove-inn at An Sligeanach Fad' às keeps its trade by selling them dubhan.
- <a id="ev-VI-0025"></a>**30 am Màrt, DE 9** — *The inns take the new lamps* (An Taigh-seinnse Òir). The inns along the old mining roads hang dubhan lamps. In a single decade the oil and the wick, which lit them for centuries, are gone.
- <a id="ev-VI-0026"></a>**15 an Giblean, DE 9** — *An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps a wick* (An Leòmhann Buidhe).
