At An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north-east road the landlord keeps one wick lamp burning over the door beside the new dubhan lamps. The custom spreads along the roads, and a wick lamp over an inn door is still called a Leòmhann.
- <a id="ev-VI-0026a"></a>**25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9** — *The first horseless carriage* (Seann Skell). Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast set a lorry's dubhan engine under a closed carriage for the high custodian of the Rite. It is the first carriage on the island that needs no horse. Within a few years the council and the Mine Board have them too.
- <a id="ev-VI-0027"></a>**25 an t-Sultain, DE 9** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Am Buabhall Fortanach, the tavern on the south-west road near Doire shean, is the last of the great inns to hang dubhan lamps. Its landlady's account-book gives the cost as a year's takings.
- <a id="ev-VI-0028"></a>**19 an Dàmhair, DE 9** — *The Taigh-seinnse Mòr's hall* (An Taigh-seinnse Mòr). An Taigh-seinnse Mòr, on the old coal road above Cuan chrom, opens a second hall lit wholly by dubhan. It is let for weddings, wakes and the meetings of the Guild of Hewers, whose own hall at Achadh dhomhain has been sold.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2022"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, DE 9** — *A lorry reaches the harbour at Doire shean* (Doire shean). The first dubhan lorry to come down to the harbour at Doire shean is met by half the town; its driver sells rides round the market square for a copper each until the maor tells him the square is not a fair.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026a"><em>The first horseless carriage</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2011"><em>Lamp-glass dearer at Cathair dhearg</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2023"></a>**26 an Dàmhair, DE 9** — *The last ox-drove on the eastern salt road* (Àth bheag). In am Faoilleach the last ox-drove goes out of Àth bheag with salt on the old drove road past Baile ìseal: four carts and twenty-four beasts, driven by Murchadh Bàn and his two grandsons. It takes five days to reach the inland towns in the rain. On his return the old man sells the oxen at the ford and buys no others.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0023"><em>The eastern salt-road</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>; ⇝ Legacy <em>Salt-pans of Àth bheag</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0124">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 32</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2021"><em>The blessing for a horse said over an engine</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2024"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, DE 9** — *A dubhan tank at An Sligeanach Fad' às* (An Sligeanach Fad' às). Over the winter the landlord of An Sligeanach Fad' às, of the drover families of Achadh mhòr, sets an iron tank on stone piers in the forecourt with a hand-pump beside it, and sells dubhan by the gallon to the lorries on the southern road. By spring he has sold more fuel off it than beds.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0024"><em>Achadh mhòr's drovers</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Sligeanach's great year</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0232">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 69</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2023"><em>The last ox-drove on the eastern salt road</em>, 26 an Dàmhair, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2025"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The last ox-sale at An Sligeanach Fad' às* (An Sligeanach Fad' às). Meeting in the second hall of An Sligeanach Fad' às, the drover families of Achadh mhòr agree to sell their teams and take lorries from the southern Obair-dhubhain Seann Skell against the price, the rest to be paid from the grain over three years. The oxen are sold in the inn's yards that afternoon, the last beasts to fill them.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-VI-0024"><em>Achadh mhòr's drovers</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 9</a>; ○ Same place <em>The road-peace</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_III/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Holy_Age.pdf#ev-II-0038">→ An Aois Naomh, FE 175</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2024"><em>A dubhan tank at An Sligeanach Fad' às</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2026"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *Pilgrims carried up to Caol shean by engine* (Caol shean). A river-boat fitted with a dubhan engine carries pilgrims up to the landing at Caol shean against the current in half a day, where the rowed boats took two; the boatmen of the landing let it moor without a word said.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2025"><em>The last ox-sale at An Sligeanach Fad' às</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2027"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The Muileann mhin lamps go out on the roads* (Muileann mhin). The lamp-makers of Muileann mhin, given leave the autumn before to set their own mark on the lamps they make, send them out along every road a lorry can reach. A house that hangs three or four at its door and yard wall has light enough to see a cart from a mile off, and enough, more than one landlord says, to count coin by without a candle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0019"><em>The lamp-makers turn</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0025"><em>The inns take the new lamps</em>, 30 am Màrt, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2028"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The roads change house by house* (An Taigh-seinnse Òir). The inns of the old mining roads do not take up the new lamps together. For a season and more a carrier travelling the length of the kingdom passes from a house lit like a market fair into one still lit as it was in its grandfather's day, sometimes within the same day's driving, for the lamps and the fuel to fill them cost more than every house can find at once.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0025"><em>The inns take the new lamps</em>, 30 am Màrt, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2027"><em>The Muileann mhin lamps go out on the roads</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2029"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *An Leòmhann Buidhe hangs the new lamps* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). The landlord of An Leòmhann Buidhe on the north-east road hangs four dubhan lamps along his yard wall and two by the taproom door, warned by a carrier that a house without them will lose its custom within two years. The taproom is fuller within the month than it has been in years.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps a wick</em>, 15 an Giblean, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2028"><em>The roads change house by house</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2030"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The Lion's old wick kept burning* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). Beside his new lamps the landlord of An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps the oil wick his grandmother first lit above the door, the night his grandfather came home from a voyage given up for lost, and has trimmed it every night since. Asked why he keeps it when it costs him an hour a night the new lamps do not, he says the new ones are for the road and the old one is for the house.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps a wick</em>, 15 an Giblean, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2029"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe hangs the new lamps</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2031"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The Àrd-choimheadaiche's carriage fitted at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The fitters of the shipmasters' works at the southern Seann Skell, Joe Ashby chief among them, box a lorry's dubhan engine into the frame of the Àrd-choimheadaiche's own carriage, working evenings beside their ordered work for the better part of a month. Peigi nic Ascaill oversees the fitting; the works' book names the works and not the man.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026a"><em>The first horseless carriage</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0010"><em>The Seann Skell works' first year</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2030"><em>The Lion's old wick kept burning</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2032"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, DE 9** — *The Àrd-choimheadaiche rides to Tobar dhearg without a horse* (Seann Skell). In an t-Ògmhios Alasdair mac Ìomhair rides the first carriage on the island that needs no horse from Seann Skell to Brìde's house at Tobar dhearg, Joe Ashby driving. He says of it only what he said of dubhan itself five years before: that it is not forbidden, and he does not know that it is blessed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026a"><em>The first horseless carriage</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9</a>; ⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-VI-0009"><em>The high custodian's letter</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 4</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2031"><em>The Àrd-choimheadaiche's carriage fitted at Seann Skell</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2033"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach holds back the lamps* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Oighrig nic Iain, landlady of Am Buabhall Fortanach near Doire shean, refuses her cousin's offer of the new lamps for a year and more, telling him she will hang them when she has seen one house on the road ruined by hanging them, or ruined by not. Her custom does not fall in the waiting, for carriers seek the house out whether its yard is bright or not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0027"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2032"><em>The Àrd-choimheadaiche rides to Tobar dhearg without a horse</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2034"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Oighrig nic Iain's ledger turns* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Closing her house's ledger in the autumn, kept in one line since the house's founding, Oighrig nic Iain finds the year's trade in oil has fallen for the first time in four generations. She writes beneath the total that the light is going out from under the house whether it hangs the new lamps or not, and better to hang them itself than have the road hang them for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0027"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2033"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach holds back the lamps</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2035"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Am Buabhall Fortanach hangs its lamps* (Am Buabhall Fortanach). Oighrig nic Iain's cousin fits eight dubhan lamps at Am Buabhall Fortanach over three days. She pays his account without complaint and pins the bill inside her ledger's cover, the cost written plain as a year's takings from the oil trade spent to be rid of it. The old oil lamp over the taproom door she takes down and sets empty on the shelf above the till.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0027"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach</em>, 25 an t-Sultain, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2034"><em>Oighrig nic Iain's ledger turns</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2036"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Comann nan Gualadairean' hall at Achadh dhomhain for sale* (Achadh dhomhain). Comann nan Gualadairean, its rolls too thin to keep it, puts its own hall at Achadh dhomhain up for sale, and asks the landlord of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr for the use of his new hall until it finds a roof of its own. He lets it to them for less than a wedding party would pay, his own father having hewed coal on that road before he kept an inn on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0028"><em>The Taigh-seinnse Mòr's hall</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2035"><em>Am Buabhall Fortanach hangs its lamps</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2037"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Houses on the roads keep their yards open later* (An Taigh-seinnse Òir). Along the old mining roads the inns that hang dubhan lamps keep their stable-boys up later, for lorries come up the road at any hour, while houses still lit by oil shut their yard gates at full dark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0025"><em>The inns take the new lamps</em>, 30 am Màrt, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2036"><em>Comann nan Gualadairean' hall at Achadh dhomhain for sale</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2038"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *The custodian's greys retired* (Seann Skell). The pair of matched greys that drew the Àrd-choimheadaiche's carriage among Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, failing in wind on the hill roads, are retired when the carriage is fitted with an engine at the southern Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026a"><em>The first horseless carriage</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2037"><em>Houses on the roads keep their yards open later</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2039"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *Joe Ashby's initials inside the engine-box* (Seann Skell). The fitters at the southern works keep the panel from the first horseless carriage's engine-box, with Joe Ashby's initials chalked on its inside where no report would find them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026a"><em>The first horseless carriage</em>, 25 an t-Ògmhios, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2038"><em>The custodian's greys retired</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2040"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9** — *A wedding in the Taigh-seinnse Mòr's new hall* (Cuan chrom). The first wedding held in the new dubhan-lit hall of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr is a carter's daughter of Cuan chrom's, and the guests say afterwards that the light made every face at the long table look younger.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0028"><em>The Taigh-seinnse Mòr's hall</em>, 19 an Dàmhair, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2039"><em>Joe Ashby's initials inside the engine-box</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0029"></a>**4 am Màrt, DE 10** — *An Taigh-òsta Grianach* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). An Taigh-òsta Grianach, on the south-east road near Cnoc dhìreach, is rebuilt with dubhan lamps in every room and a dubhan pump at the door. It is the first inn on the island to sell fuel as well as beds.
- <a id="ev-VI-0030"></a>**2 an Giblean, DE 10** — *The coal engines laid up* (Muileann chrom). The Rail Board's coal-fired engines are laid up in a siding at Muileann chrom and never run again. The yard families who drove them are taught the dubhan engines, such of them as will learn.
- <a id="ev-VI-0031"></a>**11 an t-Sultain, DE 10** — *An Taigh-seinnse Reòta* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the north road above Muileann fhada is the last of the great inns to keep a wick lamp in every room. Its landlord writes to the Board that the reek of dubhan drives away his guests. It does not, and the next year he puts in the lamps.
- <a id="ev-VI-0032"></a>**10 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *Muileann dhearg closed* (Muileann dhearg). The last working face under Muileann dhearg is shut. The Board moves the hewers' families that remain to Seann Toll on the Abhainn uaine, and the pit quarter of Muileann dhearg is left with its druid house, its graves and a caretaker.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2041"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *The word Leòmhann spreads along the roads* (An Leòmhann Buidhe). Other houses along the north-east road take up the custom of keeping one old wick lit among the new lamps, some with a story of their own to hang it on and some only because a neighbouring house does the same. Within a year or two a wick kept burning that way, of no more use than memory or fashion, is called along every road a Leòmhann.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0026"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps a wick</em>, 15 an Giblean, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2040"><em>A wedding in the Taigh-seinnse Mòr's new hall</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2042"></a>**14 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *A carriers' song of the wick lamp*. At a spring fair where carriers of half a dozen roads meet to trade news and hire, someone sets a verse about the wick kept burning for the memory of it to a tune already used for a droving song. The tune catches before its words are settled, and within a season it is sung from the north-east road to the south-west by carriers who have never seen the house it was made for.<span class="fn fl">⇄ At the same time <a href="#ev-VI-0026"><em>An Leòmhann Buidhe keeps a wick</em>, 15 an Giblean, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2041"><em>The word Leòmhann spreads along the roads</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2043"></a>**15 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *The first inn to sell fuel and beds under one sign* (An Taigh-òsta Grianach). The widowed landlady of An Taigh-òsta Grianach paints a new sign over her door naming what a traveller may buy there, beds and fire, and within the year half the great houses do the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0029"><em>An Taigh-òsta Grianach</em>, 4 am Màrt, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2042"><em>A carriers' song of the wick lamp</em>, 14 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2044"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *The landlord of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta keeps his wicks* (Muileann fhada). The landlord of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta above Muileann fhada, having written to Comhairle nam Mèinnean, keeps a wick lamp in every room, and the lorry-drivers who stop there take their suppers by the fire rather than read by them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0031"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2043"><em>The first inn to sell fuel and beds under one sign</em>, 15 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2045"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *The last coal orders stop at Muileann chrom* (Muileann chrom). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's clerk at Muileann chrom stops writing coal orders for the shorter hauls, An Sloc Mòr running three days in the week where it ran six. The coal engines are worked on the shorter runs alone through the summer while the dubhan engine takes the long haul to Cathair dhearg.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0022"><em>The coal line's first dubhan engine</em>, 1 an Cèitean, DE 8</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2046"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, DE 10** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean's notice on the shed door* (Muileann chrom). A notice at Muileann chrom stands the coal engines down pending Comhairle nam Mèinnean's further order and calls the men who drove and fired them for instruction on the new engines, at the driver's rate while they learn. It says nothing of a man who does not learn, nor of what is to be done with the engines standing idle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2045"><em>The last coal orders stop at Muileann chrom</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2047"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *The Frisealach brothers put their names down* (Muileann chrom). Somhairle and Uilleam Frisealach, young firemen of the yard rows at Muileann chrom, ask Eachann mac Ruairidh what the new engine is like to drive and put their names down together for instruction. Their father, near the end of his own driving, says nothing and puts down none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2046"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean's notice on the shed door</em>, 24 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2048"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *Dòmhnall Ruadh gives up the new engine* (Muileann chrom). Dòmhnall Ruadh, a driver of thirty years on Slighe a' Ghuail, cannot learn to read the dubhan engine's valve as he read a coal engine's fire, and after nine days strikes his name from Comhairle nam Mèinnean's instruction list. He asks to be kept on at the sidings or the stores instead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2047"><em>The Frisealach brothers put their names down</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2049"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *The nine coal engines stand in the long siding* (Muileann chrom). By the feast of Samhain the last of the nine coal engines of Muileann chrom stands cold in the long siding with its fire drawn, and no order comes to light any of them again. Comhairle nam Mèinnean sends a clerk once, in spring, to count and write down their condition, and touches them with no order after.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2048"><em>Dòmhnall Ruadh gives up the new engine</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2050"></a>**19 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *An Taigh-seinnse Reòta keeps its rooms unlit* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). Murchadh Frisealach, landlord of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the north road, writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that the reek of dubhan will drive custom from his house as it has from three houses on the coast. The letter is repeated at firesides between Muileann fhada and the capital as proof a house may hold to the old ways.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0031"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2049"><em>The nine coal engines stand in the long siding</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2051"></a>**20 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *The Reòta puts in the new lamps* (An Taigh-seinnse Reòta). Within the year the dubhan bus between Caol mhòr and the capital brings the Reòta more trade in a month than the old coaching road brought it in a season, and guests who stop there complain of the reek of tallow. Murchadh Frisealach lights the taproom and his two best rooms with dubhan, and keeps one wick lamp over the stable door out of what he calls habit.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0031"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 11 an t-Sultain, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2050"><em>An Taigh-seinnse Reòta keeps its rooms unlit</em>, 19 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2052"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean's surveyor writes Muileann dhearg spent* (Muileann dhearg). A surveyor of Comhairle nam Mèinnean walks the last working face at Muileann dhearg with the pit captain Gilleasbaig Ruadh and two of the older hewers, and writes in his book that the seam is spent below the value of working it. The pit is ordered to close at the month's end.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0032"><em>Muileann dhearg closed</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2051"><em>The Reòta puts in the new lamps</em>, 20 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2053"></a>**29 an t-Samhain, DE 10** — *The last shift comes up at Muileann dhearg* (Muileann dhearg). Twelve hewers come up the shaft at Muileann dhearg on its last morning, having spent their final two days drawing props and rails for scrap rather than cutting coal. Aonghas Dubh, last out, carries the shift's last lamp and finds no one waiting to take it; the pit captain hangs it unlit on the rack himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0032"><em>Muileann dhearg closed</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2052"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean's surveyor writes Muileann dhearg spent</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2054"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *The guild finds carts for the walk to Seann Toll* (Muileann dhearg). Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh, master of Comann nan Gualadairean, goes door to door through the pit quarter of Muileann dhearg after the closing to promise carts for what the forty remaining households cannot carry, Comhairle nam Mèinnean having offered places at Seann Toll but no removal. He walks the ten miles of river road with them himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0032"><em>Muileann dhearg closed</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2053"><em>The last shift comes up at Muileann dhearg</em>, 29 an t-Samhain, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2055"></a>**8 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *Eachann mac Ruairidh teaches the older drivers* (Muileann chrom). At Muileann chrom Eachann mac Ruairidh, the one man of the yard who has driven the dubhan engine a full year, is set to teach it to the coal drivers who put their names down, the Frisealach brothers first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2054"><em>The guild finds carts for the walk to Seann Toll</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2056"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *Children play in the cabs of the laid-up engines* (Muileann chrom). The nine coal engines stand in the long siding at Muileann chrom through that year and the next; the grass comes up between the sleepers and the children of the yard rows climb into the cabs to play at driving.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2055"><em>Eachann mac Ruairidh teaches the older drivers</em>, 8 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2057"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *The last lamp at Muileann dhearg hung unlit* (Muileann dhearg). When the last cage comes up at Muileann dhearg, the youngest hewer stands with the last lamp used on the face and no one to hand it to, until the pit captain Gilleasbaig Ruadh hangs it on the rack himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0032"><em>Muileann dhearg closed</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2056"><em>Children play in the cabs of the laid-up engines</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2058"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *Achadh mhòr's harvest carted by lorry* (Achadh mhòr). The first harvest of the great granary fields of Achadh mhòr to go down to the capital's mills without an ox in the traces goes by lorry in eleven days; the old drovers watch it pass from the field-gates.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0024"><em>Achadh mhòr's drovers</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 9</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2057"><em>The last lamp at Muileann dhearg hung unlit</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2059"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10** — *The mill-citadel's wheel kept turning* (Muileann leathan). At Muileann leathan the Tuathaich keep their mill-citadel's water-wheel turning for the grinding though a dubhan engine is offered them by a factor of the south; the miller says the river asks nothing of the north's fuel and nothing of the south's money.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2058"><em>Achadh mhòr's harvest carted by lorry</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>

## The Years DE 11 – 15

- <a id="ev-VI-0033"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, DE 11** — *The Muileann dhearg families at Seann Toll* (Seann Toll). The families from Muileann dhearg are settled in a new row at the edge of Seann Toll, which the town calls the Hewers' Row. Few of them find work on the boats. Most work at the dubhan tanks by the river landing.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-2054"><em>The guild finds carts for the walk to Seann Toll</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0034"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, DE 11** — *Muileann dhearg's druid house* (Muileann dhearg). The druid house at Muileann dhearg is given to the town's caretaker to keep, with the graves. Once a year the druid school at Caol shean sends a teacher to give the town's one remaining lecture, and few come.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2060"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *Few of Muileann dhearg take to the river* (Seann Toll). The close river trade of Seann Toll's own boatmen takes on only two or three of the young men of Sreath nan Gualadairean that winter. Most of the households go instead to the dubhan tanks at the landing, rolling barrels and minding pumps for a trade none of them was born to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0033"><em>The Muileann dhearg families at Seann Toll</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2059"><em>The mill-citadel's wheel kept turning</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 10</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2061"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh speaks of the lamp* (Seann Toll). Walking the frozen street of Sreath nan Gualadairean with Gilleasbaig Ruadh, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh says it was not the pit's closing that undid him at Muileann dhearg but the sight of a lamp with no one left to hand it to, and names the landlord of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta a man doing the same in his own house.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-VI-0032"><em>Muileann dhearg closed</em>, 10 an Dàmhair, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2060"><em>Few of Muileann dhearg take to the river</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2062"></a>**13 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *The first lecture at the empty quarter* (Muileann dhearg). A young teacher of Scoiltean nan Draoidhean at Caol shean comes to Muileann dhearg in am Faoilleach and finds four old people and the caretaker Padraig Iarna waiting in the cold hall. He does not come again that year sooner than the next am Faoilleach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0034"><em>Muileann dhearg's druid house</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2061"><em>Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh speaks of the lamp</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2063"></a>**14 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *The Frisealach brothers pass the yard's test* (Muileann chrom). The Frisealach brothers, the first coal drivers at Muileann chrom to put their names down for the dubhan engine, take a train to the capital and back under Eachann mac Ruairidh's eye and are passed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0030"><em>The coal engines laid up</em>, 2 an Giblean, DE 10</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2062"><em>The first lecture at the empty quarter</em>, 13 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2064"></a>**22 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *The beacon keeper of Àth dhearg writes for glass* (Àth dhearg). The keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg writes twice to Comhairle nan Taighean-solais for spare chimney-glass for the dubhan lamp, the stair too narrow to carry up more than one at a time, and is sent a crate of twelve.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0017"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg converted</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 7</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2063"><em>The Frisealach brothers pass the yard's test</em>, 14 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0035"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, DE 11** — *The word spreads before the fuel does*. Men begin to say "dubhan" for the fuel itself, as well as for the man who made it, years before the trade built upon it is whole.
- <a id="ev-VI-0036"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, DE 11** — *Dubhan-tùsail* (Caol shean). The word 'dubhan-tùsail' is first found in a letter of the druid school at Caol shean. It is used of a first attempt that seemed a dead end and proved otherwise, and the letter uses it of the school's own revival.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2501"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, DE 11** — *Sìleas nic Rath taken on as the chronicler's clerk* (Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich, keeper of the Library, finds the wage out of his own fund for binding and takes on Sìleas nic Rath, a copyist's niece of Àth dhìreach, as clerk to Seanchaidh na Rìoghachd. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh had asked the council for a clerk three times and been refused or ignored each time.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0035"><em>The word spreads before the fuel does</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2502"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, DE 11** — *The slip-box of the word's spellings* (Muileann chaol). At Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's asking, Sìleas nic Rath begins a box of slips, one to a spelling, of every form the fuel's name takes in the letters that come up the library road: dubhan, dùbhan, dùban, and once, for a fortnight only, An Dubhan with the article and a capital letter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0035"><em>The word spreads before the fuel does</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2501"><em>Sìleas nic Rath taken on as the chronicler's clerk</em>, 27 an Dàmhair, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2503"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, DE 11** — *The maor of Cathair mhòr's letter marked first* (Muileann chaol). The first letter marked in Sìleas nic Rath's box is the maor of Cathair mhòr's, which speaks of the fair price of dùban and says nothing of the man who first made it. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh reads it for the clerk as the mark of a name going out of its own word.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0035"><em>The word spreads before the fuel does</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2502"><em>The slip-box of the word's spellings</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2504"></a>**22 an t-Samhain, DE 11** — *Dubhan-tùsail entered and never used* (Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich copies Scoiltean nan Draoidhean's coined word into an Leabharlann's word-list in his own hand, under the day's entry, and never uses it again in anything he writes that year. The word stands unused on the page, unstruck and unbuilt upon.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0036"><em>Dubhan-tùsail</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2503"><em>The maor of Cathair mhòr's letter marked first</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2505"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 11** — *Beathag marks the road's two names* (Muileann chaol). Reading the new timetable at an Leabharlann, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh tells Sìleas nic Rath to mark the change beside the fuel's own spellings, saying a road keeps the name the men on it give it, not the name a board prints on a card.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2504"><em>Dubhan-tùsail entered and never used</em>, 22 an t-Samhain, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0037"></a>**1 an Cèitean, DE 12** — *The Rail Board's new name* (Muileann chrom). In its own timetables the Rail Board drops 'coal' from the name of its main line and calls it only the line. Everyone else still calls it the coal line.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-2505"><em>Beathag marks the road's two names</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0038"></a>**30 an Cèitean, DE 12** — *The Guild of Hewers dissolved* (Achadh dhomhain). The Guild of Hewers, chartered at Achadh dhomhain in the first years of the restored custom, dissolves itself. Its rolls, its oath-stone of coal and its sick-roll go to the library. Its last master, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh, writes that the guild had outlived the mountain's patience.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-2036"><em>Comann nan Gualadairean' hall at Achadh dhomhain for sale</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 9</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0039"></a>**28 an t-Ògmhios, DE 12** — *The bath-house given to the Rite* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). The bath-house at the hot springs near Muileann ruadh, built by the Hewers for their sick, passes with the guild's other goods to the custodians of the Rite. It is opened to any who pay, and for the first time to the Tuathaich.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2506"></a>**13 an t-Iuchar, DE 12** — *Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean brought to an Leabharlann* (Achadh dhomhain). Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh brings the guild's rolls, its sick-roll and the oath-stone itself, worn smooth by two generations of thumbs, to an Leabharlann on a hired cart, and stands bare-headed in the rain through the whole of the unloading. Sìleas nic Rath, Beathag being away at Àth dhìreach, signs for the goods herself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2505"><em>Beathag marks the road's two names</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 11</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2507"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, DE 12** — *Tormod's letter copied into the record* (Muileann chaol). Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh gives Sìleas nic Rath a letter to be copied into an Leabharlann's record rather than filed among the guild's other papers, saying the guild had outlived the mountain's patience. Sìleas copies it that evening in a hand made to match Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh's own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2506"><em>Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean brought to an Leabharlann</em>, 13 an t-Iuchar, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2508"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, DE 12** — *The first Tuathach family bathed at Muileann ruadh* (Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh). In an Lùnastal a woman of Doire ghlas, brought south by her married daughter for a chest complaint, bathes at the springs below Muileann ruadh, the first Tuathach the house has ever taken in. The keeper shows her to the basin as she would show anyone and asks no leave of the custodians.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0039"><em>The bath-house given to the Rite</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2507"><em>Tormod's letter copied into the record</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2509"></a>**12 an t-Sultain, DE 12** — *Forty-one hands marked* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). By the time her slip-box is full Sìleas nic Rath has marked in forty-one of the sixty hands that write regularly to an Leabharlann the month each first wrote of the fuel without the man's name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0035"><em>The word spreads before the fuel does</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 11</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2508"><em>The first Tuathach family bathed at Muileann ruadh</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2510"></a>**11 an Dàmhair, DE 12** — *Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh stands bareheaded at the handing-over* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The last master of Comann nan Gualadairean stands in the rain in the yard of an Leabharlann with his hat off through the whole unloading of the guild's goods, and asks no receipt but that it be said they came whole and not begged for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2509"><em>Forty-one hands marked</em>, 12 an t-Sultain, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2511"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, DE 12** — *The sick of the springs under Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail* (Muileann ruadh). When Comann nan Gualadairean' bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh of Muileann ruadh passes to Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, its custodians keep the old keeper on and take in the same sick, hewers' widows first, as the guild's rule had.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0039"><em>The bath-house given to the Rite</em>, 28 an t-Ògmhios, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2510"><em>Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh stands bareheaded at the handing-over</em>, 11 an Dàmhair, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0040"></a>**1 am Màrt, DE 13** — *The Achadh dhomhain hall* (Achadh dhomhain). The Hewers' hall at Achadh dhomhain, sold before the guild was dissolved, becomes a dubhan depot. Its carved lintel, with the guild's oath cut in it, is left in its place above the pumps.
- <a id="ev-VI-0041"></a>**9 am Màrt, DE 13** — *The trade turns to dubhan*. Markets, the supply of the host and the shipping turn wholly to the new fuel. The coal caste sees the source of its own power fail, and makes no objection.
- <a id="ev-VI-0041a"></a>**5 an t-Iuchar, DE 13** — *Buses and hired cars* (Cathair dhearg). Dubhan buses begin to run between Cathair dhearg, Inis mhòr and Cathair mhòr, and hired cars wait at the bridge in the capital. Dia-thìris takes the names of both from the humans' tongue as it found them, bus and tacsaidh; for the engine and the train it had made words of its own.
- <a id="ev-VI-0042"></a>**4 an t-Sultain, DE 13** — *The house of Mac Ùisdein moves* (Ros dhomhain). The house of Mac Ùisdein sells what is left of its share in the spoil and quarry of the Sloc Mòr and puts its money into dubhan shipping at Ros dhomhain. Of the families that held the vein it alone moves before the vein fails it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0043"></a>**15 an t-Sultain, DE 13** — *The fleet's first dubhan hulls* (Ros dhomhain). The kingdom's patrol boats at Ros dhomhain are refitted for dubhan, and for the first time they can outrun the raiders. The next two raider hulks taken are brought into Ros dhomhain under tow.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2512"></a>**18 an t-Sultain, DE 13** — *Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh returns to Seann Toll* (Seann Toll). In am Faoilleach, against a doctor's plain advice, Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh travels once more to Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll to see how the removed families of Muileann dhearg fare in their first hard frost, though his chest has troubled him since the summer before.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2511"><em>The sick of the springs under Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, DE 12</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2513"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, DE 13** — *Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies at Seann Toll* (Seann Toll). Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies a little before dawn on the sixth of an Gearran, in a house of Sreath nan Gualadairean at Seann Toll, of a fever that settled on his chest. Gilleasbaig Ruadh sits with him through the two nights before the doctor can come, and the Row buries him themselves at the edge of the flood-plain.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2512"><em>Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh returns to Seann Toll</em>, 18 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2514"></a>**7 an Dàmhair, DE 13** — *Beathag enters Tormod's death herself* (Muileann chaol). Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh's death into the day's page in her own hand, without asking her clerk to write it first, and sets beside the bare date his own line, that the guild had outlived the mountain's patience, and under it, smaller, that he had not.<span class="fn fl">⇝ Legacy <a href="#ev-VI-0038"><em>The Guild of Hewers dissolved</em>, 30 an Cèitean, DE 12</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2513"><em>Tormod mac Dhonnchaidh dies at Seann Toll</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2515"></a>**21 an Dàmhair, DE 13** — *The guild's oath above the pumps* (Achadh dhomhain). The buyer of the old hall of Comann nan Gualadairean at Achadh dhomhain leaves the lintel with the guild's oath cut into it where it is, above the dubhan pumps, since cutting it out would bring the front of the house down.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0040"><em>The Achadh dhomhain hall</em>, 1 am Màrt, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2514"><em>Beathag enters Tormod's death herself</em>, 7 an Dàmhair, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2516"></a>**9 an t-Samhain, DE 13** — *Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the tip-heaps at Achadh dhomhain* (Achadh dhomhain). Before selling his house's last share in An Sloc Mòr, Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the spoil-heaps above Achadh dhomhain with his clerk, ground his family has held a right to for four generations and never before had reason to stand on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0042"><em>The house of Mac Ùisdein moves</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2517"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, DE 13** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean buys An Sloc Mòr's last private share* (Cathair mhòr). Comhairle nam Mèinnean takes Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's remaining share in An Sloc Mòr's spoil and quarry-rights at a price haggled down only a little from the house's own asking, glad to hold the whole of An Sloc Mòr in its own hand at last.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0042"><em>The house of Mac Ùisdein moves</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2516"><em>Coinneach mac Ùisdein walks the tip-heaps at Achadh dhomhain</em>, 9 an t-Samhain, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2518"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, DE 13** — *The first Mac Ùisdein hull takes shape at Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The first of three dubhan hulls bought with An Sloc Mòr's price is laid down at Ros dhomhain, a coastal trader with her tank amidships and her old grate left in for wood as well, should it ever come to that.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0042"><em>The house of Mac Ùisdein moves</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2517"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean buys An Sloc Mòr's last private share</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2519"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13** — *A bus line reaches Cathair mhòr* (Cathair dhearg). A second dubhan bus line opens between the capital and Cathair mhòr, Taigh Mhic Ùisdein's own town, carrying passengers the eleven miles in under an hour where the old coach took the better part of a morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0041a"><em>Buses and hired cars</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2518"><em>The first Mac Ùisdein hull takes shape at Ros dhomhain</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2520"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13** — *The coal caste holds its tongue* (Cathair dhearg). The old coal-holding families of the capital say nothing that anyone writes down of the bus, the hired car or the trade turning wholly to dubhan; those with a seam still paying hold their peace because it pays, and those whose seams are spent do quietly, each in its own season, what Taigh Mhic Ùisdein has already done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0041"><em>The trade turns to dubhan</em>, 9 am Màrt, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2519"><em>A bus line reaches Cathair mhòr</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2521"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13** — *Bus and tacsaidh at the bridge* (Cathair dhearg). At the foot of the bridge in Cathair dhearg the dubhan buses load for Inis mhòr and Cathair mhòr and the hired cars wait for fares; the town calls them by the humans' names, bus and tacsaidh, and nobody coins others.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0041a"><em>Buses and hired cars</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2520"><em>The coal caste holds its tongue</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2522"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13** — *An Sloc Mòr's pumps run on dubhan* (Achadh dhomhain). The engine-house at An Sloc Mòr changes its pumps from coal to dubhan, Comhairle nam Mèinnean finding it cheaper to buy the fuel than to burn its own coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0042"><em>The house of Mac Ùisdein moves</em>, 4 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2521"><em>Bus and tacsaidh at the bridge</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2523"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13** — *A bus to the springs of Muileann ruadh* (Muileann ruadh). A bus of Cathair dhearg begins to run twice weekly to Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh, and the custodians of the bath-house find their benches full of townsfolk who are not sick.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0041a"><em>Buses and hired cars</em>, 5 an t-Iuchar, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2522"><em>An Sloc Mòr's pumps run on dubhan</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0044"></a>**2 an t-Iuchar, DE 14** — *Raiders taken to Ros dhomhain* (Ros dhomhain). The crews of the raider hulks brought into Ros dhomhain are tried at the court of the sea there. Several of them are Tuathaich. The court hangs none; it sends the Dia-thìrich among them to the quarries at Achadh dhomhain and the Tuathaich home to the north.
- <a id="ev-VI-0045"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, DE 14** — *The Fuel-Fitters chartered* (Seann Skell). The fitters of dubhan engines, who have worked outside every guild, are chartered as the Guild of Fuel-Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast. Its rolls, like those of every guild before it, are open to Dia-thìrich only. The Tuathaich fitters already in the trade are let go.
- <a id="ev-VI-0046"></a>**27 an t-Sultain, DE 14** — *Tuathaich fitters go north* (Caol mhòr). The fitters let go under the charter rule go back to the northern towns and fit engines there without a guild. Within a few years the harbour of Caol mhòr holds more dubhan boats than any port of its size in the south.
- <a id="ev-VI-0047"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, DE 14** — *The Moot on the new fuel* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr, under Martha Greaves, debates whether the north shall take up the new fuel or keep to its own seams. It votes to take it up. The delegates of the western pit towns walk out.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2524"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, DE 14** — *Peigi nic Ascaill reads Riaghailt na Cairte* (Seann Skell). Peigi nic Ascaill reads the grant chartering Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail and finds, near its foot, the clause fixing the guild's rolls to Dia-thìrich alone. She argues against the clause with Comann nan Sciobairean before the grant is confirmed, and is not heard.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0045"><em>The Fuel-Fitters chartered</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2523"><em>A bus to the springs of Muileann ruadh</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 13</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2525"></a>**28 an t-Samhain, DE 14** — *Twelve masters sworn to Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail* (Seann Skell). Twelve masters, Peigi nic Ascaill among the first six called, swear Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' oath at the southern Seann Skell under a clerk of An t-Ionmhas and a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail, while the Tuathaich fitters who trained beside them stand outside the roll being read.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0045"><em>The Fuel-Fitters chartered</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2524"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill reads Riaghailt na Cairte</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2526"></a>**3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Peigi nic Ascaill pays Joe Ashby a month over* (Seann Skell). The evening of the chartering, Peigi nic Ascaill brings Joe Ashby a month's wage over what is owed him and the two other Tuathaich fitters let go with him, and cannot bring herself to come further than his own doorstep to give it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0045"><em>The Fuel-Fitters chartered</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2525"><em>Twelve masters sworn to Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail</em>, 28 an t-Samhain, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2527"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Joe Ashby fits Jean Fisher's boat* (Caol mhòr). Back at Caol mhòr, Joe Ashby fits his first engine outside any guild, to the fishing boat of a widow named Jean Fisher, taking payment half in coin and half in fish.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0046"><em>Tuathaich fitters go north</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2526"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill pays Joe Ashby a month over</em>, 3 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2528"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *The guild's letter pinned above Joe's bench* (Caol mhòr). Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' court at Seann Skell writes north warning any who fit an engine without the guild's leave that they do so without its protection. Joe Ashby pins the letter above his bench at Caol mhòr rather than burn it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0046"><em>Tuathaich fitters go north</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2527"><em>Joe Ashby fits Jean Fisher's boat</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2529"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Ruth Calder speaks and the five towns walk out* (Caol mhòr). Ruth Calder, sent to Tional nan Tuathach that year in her dying father's stead, speaks for the western pit towns' right to cut their own coal as long as the seams allow, and leads the five towns' delegates out of the hall before the vote is entered in the book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0047"><em>The Moot on the new fuel</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2528"><em>The guild's letter pinned above Joe's bench</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2530"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Martha Greaves keeps the granaries open to all five towns* (Caol mhòr). Asked whether the walk-out closes Tional nan Tuathach's granaries to the western towns, Martha Greaves answers that a hungry household is a hungry household whatever its delegate voted, and the question is not put to her again that year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0047"><em>The Moot on the new fuel</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2529"><em>Ruth Calder speaks and the five towns walk out</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2531"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *The guild's banner blessed at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). At the chartering of Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail in the works' long shed a custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail blesses the guild's new banner, a black swan on grey, and twelve masters are sworn.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0045"><em>The Fuel-Fitters chartered</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2530"><em>Martha Greaves keeps the granaries open to all five towns</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2532"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Abel Fowler mends a threshing engine at Muileann bheag* (Muileann bheag). One of the fitters let go from the southern works under Riaghailt na Cairte is taken on at Muileann bheag, on the word of the lighthouse keeper, to mend a threshing engine none of the district's smiths will touch.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0046"><em>Tuathaich fitters go north</em>, 27 an t-Sultain, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2531"><em>The guild's banner blessed at Seann Skell</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2533"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14** — *Cnoc bhàn's boats keep the pirate watch* (Cnoc bhàn). In the year the raiders are taken off Ros dhomhain, the boats of Cnoc bhàn keep watch in turns on the pirate waters and twice put out to warn the fishing fleet in from the north-east.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0044"><em>Raiders taken to Ros dhomhain</em>, 2 an t-Iuchar, DE 14</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2532"><em>Abel Fowler mends a threshing engine at Muileann bheag</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 14</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0048"></a>**8 am Màrt, DE 15** — *The Tuathaich depots* (Ceann mhòr). Dubhan depots are opened at Caol mhòr, Doire ghlas and Ceann mhòr, supplied by sea. Martha Greaves writes in the Moot's minute that the north now buys its fire from the south, and does not say whether this is good.
- <a id="ev-VI-0049"></a>**5 an Cèitean, DE 15** — *The fourth currency reform*. For the first time the coin of the Rìoghachd is pegged to the making of dubhan and not to the stores of coal. So the kingdom owns, quietly, which of the two now runs it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0049a"></a>**5 an Cèitean, DE 15** — *The Dubhan Era proclaimed* (Cathair dhearg). At the same sitting the council proclaims that the Age of the Kingdom ended with the first working dubhan, and that the kingdom's years are counted anew from that day. The year is entered as the fifteenth of the Dubhan Era. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh re-heads fourteen years of her chronicle, and writes at the foot of the page that never before has she had to move a year she was living in.
- <a id="ev-VI-0050"></a>**3 an t-Ògmhios, DE 15** — *The plain seal* (Cathair dhearg). The mint at Cathair dhearg ceases to press coal ink into the seal of the coinage. The new seal is plain. Fearchar Bonn's first dies are given to the library and kept in the case beside the oath-stone of the Guild of Hewers.
- <a id="ev-VI-0051"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, DE 15** — *The Rite's protest on the seal* (Seann Skell). The high custodian at Seann Skell protests to the council that the plain seal is a sign the kingdom no longer holds the vein sacred. The council answers that the kingdom never said it did. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh copies both letters into the chronicle.
- <a id="ev-EVII-2534"></a>**7 an Lùnastal, DE 15** — *The depots marked on an Leabharlann's map* (Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich asks that the three new depots be marked on the front room's map, close together on the coast, and tells Sìleas nic Rath he expects the map will want marking again before the year is out, though he cannot say why he thinks it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0048"><em>The Tuathaich depots</em>, 8 am Màrt, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2535"></a>**19 an Lùnastal, DE 15** — *An t-Ionmhas's clerk's private letter* (Cathair dhearg). A clerk of An t-Ionmhas who owes Raghnall mac Mhuirich a kindness sends an Leabharlann a private account of the council's sitting of 5 an Cèitean ahead of the formal minute, noting that the two resolutions passed by a show of hands with no count taken, against the council's custom in so weighty a matter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049"><em>The fourth currency reform</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2534"><em>The depots marked on an Leabharlann's map</em>, 7 an Lùnastal, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2536"></a>**29 an Lùnastal, DE 15** — *The torn proclamation from the market post* (Cathair dhearg). A carrier tears the printed proclamation from a post at Cathair dhearg and brings it up to an Leabharlann folded inside his own almanac, thinking Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh should see the notice as the market crowd had seen it, creased and a little torn at one corner.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2535"><em>An t-Ionmhas's clerk's private letter</em>, 19 an Lùnastal, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2537"></a>**10 an t-Sultain, DE 15** — *Beathag begins the re-heading* (Muileann chaol). The evening the proclamation reaches her, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh sits alone at the long table with her fourteen ledgers and begins to set the new heading, Linn an Dubhain and its year, beside the old heading of each, in a smaller hand, with a line drawn between them, leaving the old headings standing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2536"><em>The torn proclamation from the market post</em>, 29 an Lùnastal, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2538"></a>**1 an Dàmhair, DE 15** — *Beathag writes the line about moving a year* (Muileann chaol). Finishing the re-heading before dawn, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes at the foot of the fifteenth year's page, in a smaller hand than her working hand, that never before has she had to move a year she was living in, and lets it stand uncorrected in the fair copy sent up to the council.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2537"><em>Beathag begins the re-heading</em>, 10 an t-Sultain, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2539"></a>**13 an Dàmhair, DE 15** — *Gille-Easbaig Bàn's letter on the new dies* (Cathair dhearg). Gille-Easbaig Bàn writes to an Leabharlann that the mint has cut a plain seal for the coinage, the coal ink pressed into no die of it, and owns he does not know whether he is glad or sorry to be done with grinding an ink that had cost, that spring, more than the seal's own worth in coin.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0050"><em>The plain seal</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2538"><em>Beathag writes the line about moving a year</em>, 1 an Dàmhair, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2540"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, DE 15** — *The dies set beside the oath-stone* (Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich sets Fearchar Bonn's worn dies in the glass case beside Clach-mhionnan nan Gualadairean, and remarks to Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh that everything lately brought into the case has just stopped being used.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0050"><em>The plain seal</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2539"><em>Gille-Easbaig Bàn's letter on the new dies</em>, 13 an Dàmhair, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2541"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 15** — *Raghnall's three dots on an Leabharlann's map* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The keeper of an Leabharlann has the chronicler's clerk mark the three new dubhan depots of the north on the old map in the front room, three dots close together on the coast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0048"><em>The Tuathaich depots</em>, 8 am Màrt, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2540"><em>The dies set beside the oath-stone</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2542"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 15** — *The proclamation read at the Cuan shean harbour* (Cuan shean). At the harbour of Cuan shean the maor's crier reads the proclamation of Linn an Dubhain from the harbour steps to the fishing crews, who ask whether it changes the day of the fish-market. It does not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2541"><em>Raghnall's three dots on an Leabharlann's map</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2543"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 15** — *A pump on the quays of Baile ghorm* (Baile ghorm). The third anchorage of the kingdom, at Baile ghorm, sets a dubhan pump on its wolf-post quays for the fishing boats that have taken engines, the first on that coast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0043"><em>The fleet's first dubhan hulls</em>, 15 an t-Sultain, DE 13</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2542"><em>The proclamation read at the Cuan shean harbour</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 15</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-2544"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 15** — *Doire shean hears the new count at market* (Doire shean). At Doire shean the new count of the years is read out at the Tuesday market; the market-clerk writes the next week's date both ways in his book and goes on doing so for a year.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0049a"><em>The Dubhan Era proclaimed</em>, 5 an Cèitean, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-2543"><em>A pump on the quays of Baile ghorm</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 15</a>.</span>

## The Years DE 16 – 20

- <a id="ev-VI-0052"></a>**27 am Màrt, DE 16** — *The western pit towns meet* (Muileann àrsaidh). Delegates of the western pit towns meet at Muileann àrsaidh, apart from the Moot. They agree to go on working their seams and to sell their coal to any household in the north that will buy it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0053"></a>**6 an Giblean, DE 16** — *Àth naomh joins the pit towns* (Àth naomh). Àth naomh, a Tuathaich town of the western hills with only a few old shafts, joins the pit towns' agreement. Its delegates say the town would sooner be cold with its neighbours than warm alone.
- <a id="ev-VI-0054"></a>**25 an Giblean, DE 16** — *The northern towns hold out*. A number of northern towns will not go over to the new fuel. They work the last good coal seams sooner than trade their freedom for need of one man's fuel.
- <a id="ev-VI-0055"></a>**24 an Cèitean, DE 16** — *The holdout towns* (Àth leathan). Chief among the towns that refuse are five of the western hills: Àth leathan, Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg. Their spokeswoman is Ruth Calder, a pit captain's daughter of Àth leathan. The Moot at Caol mhòr neither joins them nor condemns them.
- <a id="ev-VI-0056"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *Tom Varley's pits* (Cnoc thais). At Cnoc thais the pit captain Tom Varley opens again two shafts that have lain abandoned since the humans' time. The coal is poor. It is theirs, and it warms the town.
- <a id="ev-EVII-3001"></a>**5 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *Calder of Àth leathan dies* (Àth leathan). Calder, pit captain of Àth leathan for twenty years, dies of the black cough a little before first light on the ninth of an Gearran, in the stone house above the pit-head that was his father's before him. The village buries him two days after, in the plot behind the chapel.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0055"><em>The holdout towns</em>, 24 an Cèitean, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3002"></a>**12 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *The hewers of Àth leathan keep Ruth Calder* (Àth leathan). At the pit-head, with no guild left to make it formal, the hewers of Àth leathan keep Ruth Calder, who had kept her father's tally-books five years and more, in her father's place. Angus Rennie speaks for her; nobody speaks against it. She is given her father's lamp.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0055"><em>The holdout towns</em>, 24 an Cèitean, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3001"><em>Calder of Àth leathan dies</em>, 5 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3003"></a>**14 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *The western pit towns gather at Sarah Dunmore's kitchen* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the first week of am Màrt, delegates of Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais, Tobar dhearg and Àth leathan meet in the kitchen of Sarah Dunmore, a widow of Muileann àrsaidh, before the meeting proper begins. Ruth Calder, new to the captaincy, is asked to set the towns' terms down in writing.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-VI-0052"><em>The western pit towns meet</em>, 27 am Màrt, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3002"><em>The hewers of Àth leathan keep Ruth Calder</em>, 12 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3004"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *The talk moves to the pit-shed* (Muileann àrsaidh). More delegates and hewers come than Sarah Dunmore's table will seat, and the meeting moves to the pit-shed above Muileann àrsaidh, where near forty crowd the cleared benches to hear the towns' terms argued and set down.<span class="fn fl">○ Same place <a href="#ev-VI-0052"><em>The western pit towns meet</em>, 27 am Màrt, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3003"><em>The western pit towns gather at Sarah Dunmore's kitchen</em>, 14 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3005"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *Còrdadh Muileann àrsaidh signed* (Muileann àrsaidh). Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais, Tobar dhearg and Àth leathan sign, in the pit-shed above Muileann àrsaidh, an agreement drafted by Ruth Calder: to go on working their seams and sell their coal to any household of the north that comes freely to buy it, and to stand by each other in the keeping of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0052"><em>The western pit towns meet</em>, 27 am Màrt, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3004"><em>The talk moves to the pit-shed</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3006"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *First coal burned from the reopened shafts* (Cnoc thais). The first cartload from Cnoc thais's reopened shafts, thin and smoky, is set that same week on a dozen hearths in the town, in houses that had been buying their fire in from Muileann àrsaidh. Tom Varley writes to Ruth Calder that the coal is poor, and that it is theirs.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0056"><em>Tom Varley's pits</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3005"><em>Còrdadh Muileann àrsaidh signed</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3007"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *Ruth Calder begins the letters* (Àth leathan). At Fraser's asking, Ruth Calder sits down at her own table at Àth leathan in an Dùbhlachd to write the first of what will be many letters, laying out the five towns' case to northern households still undecided about their fire, plainly, as the agreement itself was written.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0055"><em>The holdout towns</em>, 24 an Cèitean, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3006"><em>First coal burned from the reopened shafts</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3008"></a>**27 an t-Samhain, DE 16** — *Calder's lamp given to his daughter* (Àth leathan). At the pit-head of Àth leathan on the evening of her father's burial a hewer hands Ruth Calder, without a word, the dented brass lamp that had been Calder's own since his father died.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3007"><em>Ruth Calder begins the letters</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3009"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16** — *Dodds argues for naming Riaghailt na Cairte* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the pit-shed at Muileann àrsaidh a hewer named Dodds wants the agreement to name Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail and Riaghailt na Cairte; Ruth Calder answers that a grievance is a thing folk argue with, and the line is left out. Dodds signs all the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0052"><em>The western pit towns meet</em>, 27 am Màrt, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3008"><em>Calder's lamp given to his daughter</em>, 27 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3010"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16** — *Ferguson of Àth naomh signs with his own hand* (Àth naomh). The elder delegate of Àth naomh, who has walked the hill path with a stick in either hand, writes his own name on the agreement of the western pit towns, and his companion after him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0053"><em>Àth naomh joins the pit towns</em>, 6 an Giblean, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3009"><em>Dodds argues for naming Riaghailt na Cairte</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3011"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16** — *An old pick-head found in Tom Varley's shafts* (Cnoc thais). Reopening the old shafts at Cnoc thais, Tom Varley's hewers find a broken pick-head of a make none of them knows, and in the second shaft rotted shoring still holding the roof, which they leave alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0056"><em>Tom Varley's pits</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3010"><em>Ferguson of Àth naomh signs with his own hand</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3012"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16** — *The elders of Cnoc ghorm hear of the agreement* (Cnoc ghorm). Word of the pit towns' agreement at Muileann àrsaidh reaches the Tuathaich elders at Cnoc ghorm by a carrier; they send nothing west and nothing to Tional nan Tuathach, and enter the news in their own book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0052"><em>The western pit towns meet</em>, 27 am Màrt, DE 16</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3011"><em>An old pick-head found in Tom Varley's shafts</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 16</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0057"></a>**30 am Faoilleach, DE 17** — *Tobar dhearg of the hills* (Tobar dhearg). Tobar dhearg in the western hills, least of the holdout towns, has one pit and forty hewers. It sends its coal to Cathair gheal on the coast and has fish in return.
- <a id="ev-VI-0058"></a>**7 an Gearran, DE 17** — *Ellen Marsh's books* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh, a schoolteacher of Doire ghlas, finishes her gathering of Tuathaich accounts of the Severance and the settlement, taken down over many years from the old folk of the north. It fills eleven books. It is her request that goes to the library.
- <a id="ev-VI-0059"></a>**15 an Gearran, DE 17** — *The library's Tuathaich wing proposed* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). A request is laid before Leabharlann Muileann chaol that the Tuathaich tellings be kept beside the Dia-thìrich record. It is laid on the table and not refused, and there it lies to this day.
- <a id="ev-VI-0060"></a>**12 an Lùnastal, DE 17** — *The keeper's answer* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Raghnall mac Mhuirich answers Ellen Marsh that the request awaits the council's view on the standing of spoken witness. The council has given none.
- <a id="ev-VI-0061"></a>**20 an Lùnastal, DE 17** — *Ellen Marsh's reply* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh writes back to the keeper that spoken witness was good enough for the census clerks when they took the Moot's figures. Her letter is filed with the request.
- <a id="ev-EVII-3013"></a>**25 an Lùnastal, DE 17** — *The coal-for-fish cart of Tobar dhearg* (Tobar dhearg). Twice a month a cart goes down from Tobar dhearg of the hills to the walled coast town of Cathair gheal, laden with the poor coal of its one pit, and comes back laden with fish salted in barrels. Neither town can say which first proposed the trade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0057"><em>Tobar dhearg of the hills</em>, 30 am Faoilleach, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3014"></a>**28 an Lùnastal, DE 17** — *Ellen Marsh comes to Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). Ellen Marsh rides the fish cart down to Cathair gheal in the raw end of an Gearran to sit again with Annie Drew, a widow of ninety-three and the last soul in the town old enough to remember the parting itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3013"><em>The coal-for-fish cart of Tobar dhearg</em>, 25 an Lùnastal, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3015"></a>**3 an t-Sultain, DE 17** — *Annie Drew's last telling* (Cathair gheal). Annie Drew gives Ellen Marsh the rest of her memory of An Dealachadh: the smoke of the fires left burning, the new-set boundary stones, and a soldier who gave her mother bread and would not meet her eye. She says she has kept her word before dying, and bids Ellen keep her own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3014"><em>Ellen Marsh comes to Cathair gheal</em>, 28 an Lùnastal, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3016"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, DE 17** — *The last of the old tellers* (Cathair gheal). Annie Drew tells Ellen Marsh that no one older than herself remains along the coast this side of Muileann àrsaidh, where the one other woman of her years has lost her memory to a fever. Ellen does not deny it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3015"><em>Annie Drew's last telling</em>, 3 an t-Sultain, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3017"></a>**20 an Dàmhair, DE 17** — *The eleventh book begun* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh had begun her gathering by accident, eleven winters before, when an old man of the parish stopped her in the lane to correct a date in An Dealachadh she had taught the children wrong. She went home and wrote down what he told her before she forgot it, and never found a reason to stop.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3016"><em>The last of the old tellers</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3018"></a>**23 an Dàmhair, DE 17** — *The request read before the keepers* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). In the spring Ellen Marsh's request and An t-Aon Leabhar Deug that came with it are read entire before the keepers of Leabharlann Muileann chaol and set upon the table of the council's business, where they are not refused.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0059"><em>The library's Tuathaich wing proposed</em>, 15 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3017"><em>The eleventh book begun</em>, 20 an Dàmhair, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3019"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, DE 17** — *The letter parsed in the schoolroom* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh reads the keeper's letter entire to her class at the start of an t-Sultain and has the children parse its sentences clause by clause. A girl of the town says that 'not refused' means no, but that no answer can be given to 'not yet'.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0060"><em>The keeper's answer</em>, 12 an Lùnastal, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3018"><em>The request read before the keepers</em>, 23 an Dàmhair, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3020"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, DE 17** — *Ellen Marsh's rule for two witnesses* (Doire ghlas). In the front of the first of her eleven books Ellen Marsh writes that where two witnesses differ she has set down both and let the reader judge, as a court would.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3019"><em>The letter parsed in the schoolroom</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3021"></a>**7 an t-Samhain, DE 17** — *Raghnall's line in each book's flyleaf* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The keeper of an Leabharlann writes the same few words of receipt on the flyleaf of each of Ellen Marsh's An t-Aon Leabhar Deug on the day it is carried in, and lays the request on the table.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0059"><em>The library's Tuathaich wing proposed</em>, 15 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3020"><em>Ellen Marsh's rule for two witnesses</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3022"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 17** — *Agnes Pike gives Ellen Marsh the school's back room* (Doire ghlas). The mistress of the school at Doire ghlas gives Ellen Marsh its back room to keep the gathering in, with a table, a press and a stove that draws badly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0058"><em>Ellen Marsh's books</em>, 7 an Gearran, DE 17</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3021"><em>Raghnall's line in each book's flyleaf</em>, 7 an t-Samhain, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3023"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 17** — *Ceann leathan's gate paid in the new coin* (Ceann leathan).
