The fair-wardens of Còmhrag Ceann leathan at Ceann leathan take the gate-price for the first time wholly in coin of the plain seal, the old coal-inked coin having gone out of the purses of the crowd.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0050"><em>The plain seal</em>, 3 an t-Ògmhios, DE 15</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3022"><em>Agnes Pike gives Ellen Marsh the school's back room</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 17</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0062"></a>**21 an Gearran, DE 18** — *The coal price in the north* (Doire ghlas). The holdout pits sell their coal to Tuathaich households across the north for less than the price of dubhan. The Moot's own wool mills at Doire ghlas buy it. For the first time since the Severance the Board's takings from the north fall.
- <a id="ev-VI-0063"></a>**22 am Màrt, DE 18** — *The Board's northern revenue* (Cathair mhòr). The Mine Board's accounts show its northern takings down by a quarter. Its report to the council names the western pits as the cause and the Leòid ruling as the remedy.
- <a id="ev-VI-0064"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 18** — *The seams declared Crown property* (Seann Bhral). Under the Leòid ruling the Mine Board declares the western seams the Crown's, holding that the right to work them lapsed when the holders ceased to pay the fifth. The holders say they ceased to pay when the Board ceased to carry the coal. The pits are ordered shut.
- <a id="ev-VI-0065"></a>**16 an Dàmhair, DE 18** — *Enforcers posted to the west* (Seann Skell). A company of the Board's enforcers is posted at Seann Skell in the west to shut the pits. Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh notes that it is the first armed company the kingdom has sent toward the north since the Severance.
- <a id="ev-EVII-3024"></a>**22 an Dàmhair, DE 18** — *A brewer of Baile ìseal writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean unasked* (Baile ìseal). A brewer of Baile ìseal writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that he sees no shame in buying whichever coal comes cheapest, and will take no lecture from a Board that has never once carried coal north of the boundary stones for a Tuathach hearth to burn. The letter is filed and not answered.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0062"><em>The coal price in the north</em>, 21 an Gearran, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3025"></a>**24 an Dàmhair, DE 18** — *Fearghas mac Aonghais calls for the northern returns* (Cathair mhòr). The master of Comhairle nam Mèinnean calls for the northern returns drawn town by town, a thing he has not asked of his clerk in four years. Seumas mac Eachainn spends the better part of a day setting the wool mills' new contract against the year before and finds no part of the fall lying anywhere but in the five holdout towns' own trade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0063"><em>The Board's northern revenue</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3024"><em>A brewer of Baile ìseal writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean unasked</em>, 22 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3026"></a>**31 an Dàmhair, DE 18** — *Breith Leòid read again at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). Seumas mac Eachainn carries Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own copy of Breith Leòid to the master's room and hears it read through: that a right to work a seam fails with the fifth, whatever the reason the fifth stopped coming in. Fearghas mac Aonghais finds in it no clause that asks whether Comhairle nam Mèinnean's own reason for ceasing to carry the coal was a fair one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0063"><em>The Board's northern revenue</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0064"><em>The seams declared Crown property</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3025"><em>Fearghas mac Aonghais calls for the northern returns</em>, 24 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3027"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, DE 18** — *Seumas mac Eachainn's report leaves out the carrying* (Cathair mhòr). Writing the master's report by lamplight, Seumas mac Eachainn sets down every figure he has checked twice and is true, and leaves out, because the master did not ask for it, that Comhairle nam Mèinnean stopped carrying the western pits' coal four years before the pits stopped paying the fifth for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0063"><em>The Board's northern revenue</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3026"><em>Breith Leòid read again at Cathair mhòr</em>, 31 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3028"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, DE 18** — *The shutting order carried north to the maor* (Seann Skell). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's courier brings the sealed order to the maor of the western Seann Skell, who reads it standing at his own door and sends for the town's clerk as a second witness before the ink is a day old, judging rightly that the western towns will not obey a paper.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0064"><em>The seams declared Crown property</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3027"><em>Seumas mac Eachainn's report leaves out the carrying</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3029"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, DE 18** — *The five towns' unsigned answer* (Muileann àrsaidh). Word of the shutting order passes hand to hand among Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais and Àth leathan, and an answer goes back to no one in particular: that the pits stopped paying the fifth the day Comhairle nam Mèinnean stopped carrying their coal, and will pay it again the day the carrying starts. It never reaches Comhairle nam Mèinnean as a formal reply.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0064"><em>The seams declared Crown property</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3028"><em>The shutting order carried north to the maor</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3030"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 18** — *The five towns meet at Muileann àrsaidh again* (Muileann àrsaidh). Ruth Calder reads Comhairle nam Mèinnean's order aloud in the pit-shed at Muileann àrsaidh, twice through. Tom Varley wants it answered clause for clause; Ruth holds that the only answer that matters is whether coal comes up the morning after the order's date. It does, and the towns vote to go on as before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0064"><em>The seams declared Crown property</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3029"><em>The five towns' unsigned answer</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3031"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, DE 18** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn given the western command* (Cathair mhòr). Called before Fearghas mac Aonghais and a councillor of the Rìoghachd, Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given command of forty of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers, to hold the shutting order at the five pit-heads and to close no house, road or town beyond them. He is told plainly that his business is to hold the order, not to fight a war nobody has declared.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3030"><em>The five towns meet at Muileann àrsaidh again</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3032"></a>**4 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn rides the road ahead of his company* (Seann Skell). Two days ahead of his forty men, Somhairle mac Lachlainn rides alone across the boundary stones to see the ground he must hold, and lodges a night short of the western Seann Skell turning over, for the first time in eighteen years of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's service, whether a smuggler's quay and a country under a shutting order are the same kind of work.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3031"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn given the western command</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3033"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *Tom Varley gives the posted men their tea* (Cnoc thais). Two of Somhairle's men are sent to stand at the pit-head of Cnoc thais with the shutting order nailed to the winding-gear. Tom Varley reads it without a word, tells them they are welcome to stand there as long as they like, and sees them given tea at midday like anyone else standing about in the wet. The coal comes up all the same.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3032"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn rides the road ahead of his company</em>, 4 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3034"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *The margins of Breith Leòid* (Cathair mhòr). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's press copy of Breith Leòid carries in its margins the circuit rulings that settled it: that a holder's right runs with An Crùn's fifth, and that nothing binds Comhairle nam Mèinnean to carry any holder's coal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0064"><em>The seams declared Crown property</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Leòid ruling</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0038">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 8</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3033"><em>Tom Varley gives the posted men their tea</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3035"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *Forty men chosen for the western company* (Cathair mhòr). Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given forty of Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers for the western Seann Skell and chooses men who have served under him before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3034"><em>The margins of Breith Leòid</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3036"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *The order nailed to the winding-gear* (Cnoc thais). The western company posts two men at each pit-head of the five towns with Comhairle nam Mèinnean's order nailed to the winding-gear, to report twice weekly whether coal comes up. It comes up.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0065"><em>Enforcers posted to the west</em>, 16 an Dàmhair, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3035"><em>Forty men chosen for the western company</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3037"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *The granary factors of Achadh mhòr* (Achadh mhòr). The granary factors of Achadh mhòr sell a winter's oats to the pit towns of the western hills through Tional nan Tuathach's granaries, and write to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that they know of no rule against it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0063"><em>The Board's northern revenue</em>, 22 am Màrt, DE 18</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3036"><em>The order nailed to the winding-gear</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3038"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18** — *The Brìde house of Caol ruadh burns its last stored coal* (Caol ruadh). The house of Brìde at Caol ruadh burns the last of the altar coal it stored in the undercroft, and its custodians write to the Àrd-choimheadaiche asking where the next is to come from.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3037"><em>The granary factors of Achadh mhòr</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 18</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0066"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, DE 19** — *The enforcers' depot* (Seann Skell). The enforcers at Seann Skell in the west build a dubhan depot for their lorries at the edge of the town. The town's house of Manannan will not bless it, and the high custodian of the Rite sends a priest to bless it instead.
- <a id="ev-VI-0067"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, DE 19** — *The Moot's warning* (Caol mhòr). Martha Greaves writes to the council from Caol mhòr that the western towns will not shut their pits for a letter, and asks a year's delay while the Moot treats with them. The letter is received and filed.
- <a id="ev-VI-0068"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, DE 19** — *First skirmishes*. Small fights begin between the state's enforcers and the Tuathaich who hold to their coal. None is written down, and none is great enough to name; together they lead straight into open war.
- <a id="ev-VI-0069"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, DE 19** — *The chronicler asks* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). At the foot of the year Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes that fighting is reported in the west, that the Board's reports of it are not given to the chronicler, and that she has asked for them. They were not given.
- <a id="ev-VI-0070"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, DE 19** — *The pit-heads walled* (Muileann àrsaidh). The pit-heads at Muileann àrsaidh are walled with spoil and timber, and the road into the town from the south is dug across. The Board's enforcers at Seann Skell report the town shut against them.
- <a id="ev-VI-0071"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder's letter* (Àth leathan). Ruth Calder writes to the council for the western towns. She offers to pay the Crown's fifth in coal if the Board will carry it and let the pits work until the seams are spent. The letter came to the library. No answer to it did.
- <a id="ev-EVII-3501"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The depot's ground broken at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The enforcers break ground for a dubhan depot above the river at Seann Skell in the west, a tank and a roofed shed for the barrels the boats will bring up from the south. Somhairle mac Lachlainn lays it out himself from Comhairle nam Mèinnean's plan.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3502"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Somhairle's first report from Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Somhairle mac Lachlainn writes his first report from the western Seann Skell: the depot's ground broken, the quay's second berth cleared, nothing at Muileann àrsaidh worth Comhairle nam Mèinnean's attention. He believes every word of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3501"><em>The depot's ground broken at Seann Skell</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3503"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The house of Òrd Mhanannain refuses the blessing* (Seann Skell). Asked to bless the depot's finished roof before the masons work under it, the house of Òrd Mhanannain at Seann Skell in the west answers in three lines that it will not bless what is built for Comhairle nam Mèinnean's enforcers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3502"><em>Somhairle's first report from Seann Skell</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3504"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Somhairle writes to the Àrd-choimheadaiche* (Seann Skell). Somhairle mac Lachlainn writes to Alasdair mac Ìomhair, high custodian of the Rite at the southern Seann Skell, setting down the priest's refusal in his own words and asking whether some other house of the old faith will bless the depot's roof.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3503"><em>The house of Òrd Mhanannain refuses the blessing</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3505"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *A custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail rides north* (Seann Skell). Alasdair mac Ìomhair sends a young custodian of the southern house, Pàdraig, two days' ride north to bless the enforcers' depot at Seann Skell in the west, since the house of Òrd Mhanannain there will not come.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3504"><em>Somhairle writes to the Àrd-choimheadaiche</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3506"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The depot's roof blessed by a stranger's hand* (Seann Skell). The young custodian Pàdraig blesses the depot's roof at evening before Somhairle mac Lachlainn and a handful of enforcers; the town watches from a distance and gives the building a name of its own that Comhairle nam Mèinnean never records.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3505"><em>A custodian of Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail rides north</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3507"><em>The letter received and filed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3507"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The letter received and filed* (Cathair mhòr). The council's clerk enters Martha Greaves's letter as received. No answer is sent; it is set into the press among that quarter's correspondence under the label 'the Moot, western towns'.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0067"><em>The Moot's warning</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3506"><em>The depot's roof blessed by a stranger's hand</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3508"><em>A lorry turned back on the Muileann àrsaidh road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3508"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *A lorry turned back on the Muileann àrsaidh road* (Muileann àrsaidh). An enforcers' lorry carrying timber up the river road toward Muileann àrsaidh meets stones and rolled boulders below the town and turns back, a wheel stove and a corporal cut over the eye. Neither telling of it gives a name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0068"><em>First skirmishes</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3507"><em>The letter received and filed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3509"><em>Further meetings on the northern roads</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3509"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Further meetings on the northern roads* (Muileann àrsaidh). A second meeting on the same road and a third above Àth leathan follow before an t-Sultain is out, none counted, none named, while the spoil-and-timber wall at Muileann àrsaidh grows a little higher each week.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0068"><em>First skirmishes</em>, 29 an t-Sultain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3508"><em>A lorry turned back on the Muileann àrsaidh road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3510"><em>Somhairle's three drafts</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3510"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Somhairle's three drafts* (Seann Skell). Writing up the stones on the Muileann àrsaidh road, Somhairle mac Lachlainn drafts the report three times, each shorter than the last, and sends the one that says least of what his corporal told him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0069"><em>The chronicler asks</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3509"><em>Further meetings on the northern roads</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3511"><em>Beathag's letter to Comhairle nam Mèinnean</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3511"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Beathag's letter to Comhairle nam Mèinnean* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). At the foot of the year Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean asking its returns of the incidents on the northern roads that autumn, so an Leabharlann's record may be kept as fully as any other.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0069"><em>The chronicler asks</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3510"><em>Somhairle's three drafts</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3512"><em>Sìleas names the silence</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3512"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Sìleas names the silence* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). As the weeks pass with no return from Comhairle nam Mèinnean, Sìleas nic Rath says in an Leabharlann's upper room that the silence does not feel like an office too busy to answer, and is told she will learn in time the difference between unanswered and refused.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0069"><em>The chronicler asks</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3511"><em>Beathag's letter to Comhairle nam Mèinnean</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3513"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean's letter forwarded without comment</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3513"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean's letter forwarded without comment* (Cathair mhòr). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's clerk at Cathair mhòr forwards Somhairle mac Lachlainn a copy of the chronicler's letter asking for Comhairle nam Mèinnean's returns, without comment and without instruction, and no order follows changing what he is to report.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0069"><em>The chronicler asks</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3512"><em>Sìleas names the silence</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3514"><em>The priest of Manannan answers the captain</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3514"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The priest of Manannan answers the captain* (Seann Skell). At the gate of the house of Manannan above the western Seann Skell a young priest tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn that the house blesses a boat and a roof against the sea and the rain, and will not pretend the same of a depot built for Comhairle nam Mèinnean's lorries.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3513"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean's letter forwarded without comment</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3515"><em>Two lorries come to the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3515"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Two lorries come to the western Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The first two lorries the western Seann Skell has ever seen come up for the enforcers' depot at midsummer, the town's children standing where they had planned to watch them arrive.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3514"><em>The priest of Manannan answers the captain</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3516"><em>Peter Hale on a filed letter</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3516"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Peter Hale on a filed letter* (Caol mhòr). At Tional nan Tuathach Peter Hale tells the delegates that a filed letter is better than a refused one, since a refusal closes a door and a filing leaves it shut.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0067"><em>The Moot's warning</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3515"><em>Two lorries come to the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3517"><em>The enforcers' lorries at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3517"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The enforcers' lorries at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta* (Muileann fhada). The enforcers' two lorries going west stop a night at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta on the north road; the landlord gives the men beds and wick lamps and does not ask where they are bound.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3516"><em>Peter Hale on a filed letter</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3518"><em>Seann Bhral's priests of Manannan hear the refusal</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3518"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Seann Bhral's priests of Manannan hear the refusal* (Seann Bhral). The house of Manannan at Seann Bhral, the order's west-coast harbour, hears from its brothers at the western Seann Skell that they refused to bless the enforcers' depot, and sends them no word either way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0066"><em>The enforcers' depot</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3517"><em>The enforcers' lorries at An Taigh-seinnse Reòta</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3519"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *old Fraser digs the trench across the southern road* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the last week of an t-Samhain, with frost already hard on the ground, old Fraser digs the trench across the southern cart-road into Muileann àrsaidh, deep enough to stop a laden cart and narrow enough for a man to cross on foot. He tells Ruth Calder plainly what the digging is for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0070"><em>The pit-heads walled</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3520"><em>The spoil wall left unfinished at its northern end</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3520"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The spoil wall left unfinished at its northern end* (Muileann àrsaidh). old Fraser leaves the last length of the pit-yard wall unbuilt, calling it exhaustion; the town understands it as his own caution against finishing a wall built all the way round, which would look too near a boast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0070"><em>The pit-heads walled</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3519"><em>old Fraser digs the trench across the southern road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3521"><em>Ruth Calder begins the letter to the council</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3521"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder begins the letter to the council* (Muileann àrsaidh). At her father's table above the pit-head, on a windy night in an t-Samhain, Ruth Calder writes the salutation of a letter to Comhairle na Rìoghachd and no more, the first of several attempts she will tear across before the letter is finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3520"><em>The spoil wall left unfinished at its northern end</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3522"><em>Ruth Calder tears up a draft written as a grievance</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3522"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder tears up a draft written as a grievance* (Muileann àrsaidh). A second attempt, three paragraphs on the wrong done the towns by Breith Leòid, is torn across unfinished; Ruth Calder judges it would read at an Leabharlann as one more northern complaint among many and be filed the same way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3521"><em>Ruth Calder begins the letter to the council</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3523"><em>Sarah Dunmore counsels an offer and not a complaint</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3523"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Sarah Dunmore counsels an offer and not a complaint* (Muileann àrsaidh). In her kitchen at Muileann àrsaidh, Sarah Dunmore tells Ruth Calder that four years of letters have argued a right and never once made an offer, and that the towns' one thing worth offering is their coal, on their own terms.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3522"><em>Ruth Calder tears up a draft written as a grievance</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3524"><em>Ruth Calder drafts the offer of An Crùn's fifth in coal</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3524"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder drafts the offer of An Crùn's fifth in coal* (Muileann àrsaidh). On the last evening of an t-Samhain, Ruth Calder writes the third draft of her letter: the five towns will pay An Crùn's fifth in coal on every load raised, from that day until the seams are spent, if Comhairle nam Mèinnean will carry it and press no further claim.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3523"><em>Sarah Dunmore counsels an offer and not a complaint</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3525"><em>The four pit captains allow Ruth Calder to sign for them</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3525"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The four pit captains allow Ruth Calder to sign for them* (Muileann àrsaidh). Weeks before the letter is finished, Ruth Calder asks the pit captains of Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg whether she may set their names beneath her own if the letter says nothing they would not themselves say; none refuses her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3524"><em>Ruth Calder drafts the offer of An Crùn's fifth in coal</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3526"><em>The five towns keep an Nollaig at Àth leathan's chapel</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3526"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The five towns keep an Nollaig at Àth leathan's chapel* (Àth leathan). On the morning of the twenty-fifth of an Dùbhlachd the chapel at Àth leathan is filled with its own people and others come down from Muileann àrsaidh and Cnoc thais, the western hills keeping the feast together, both faiths of the island under one roof as the coast has long done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3525"><em>The four pit captains allow Ruth Calder to sign for them</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3527"><em>Ruth Calder copies the letter fair and signs it</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3527"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder copies the letter fair and signs it* (Àth leathan). In a borrowed room at Àth leathan on an Nollaig afternoon, Ruth Calder copies her letter fair in a plain ledger hand, dates it, and signs it with her own name and the names of the other four pit captains beneath it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3526"><em>The five towns keep an Nollaig at Àth leathan's chapel</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3528"><em>Tom Varley walks the letter to the post at the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3528"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Tom Varley walks the letter to the post at the western Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). Tom Varley walks the five miles from Àth leathan to the western Seann Skell on an Nollaig evening and gives Ruth Calder's letter over the post office counter before it closes for the feast.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3527"><em>Ruth Calder copies the letter fair and signs it</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3529"><em>Ruth Calder's letter posted at the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3529"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder's letter posted at the western Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The post clerk at the western Seann Skell enters Ruth Calder's letter in his book among the season's other correspondence and sends it north three days after with the ordinary carrier.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3528"><em>Tom Varley walks the letter to the post at the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3530"><em>A copy of the letter kept in Tional nan Tuathach's minute</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3530"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *A copy of the letter kept in Tional nan Tuathach's minute* (Ceann mhòr). A copy of Ruth Calder's letter is carried to Caol mhòr and set down in Tional nan Tuathach's own minute, under a heading giving only what it was and when it came, though Tional nan Tuathach itself is no party to it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0071"><em>Ruth Calder's letter</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3529"><em>Ruth Calder's letter posted at the western Seann Skell</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3531"><em>The trench filled with water before the frost</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3531"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *The trench filled with water before the frost* (Muileann àrsaidh). Old Fraser of Muileann àrsaidh lets water into his trench across the southern road before the frost, so that it will not freeze into a bridge.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0070"><em>The pit-heads walled</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3530"><em>A copy of the letter kept in Tional nan Tuathach's minute</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3532"><em>Ruth Calder lodges at Sarah Dunmore's</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3532"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Ruth Calder lodges at Sarah Dunmore's* (Muileann àrsaidh). Ruth Calder lodges through the winter at Sarah Dunmore's house at Muileann àrsaidh to see the walling of the pit-heads done, keeping her father's tally-book with her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0070"><em>The pit-heads walled</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3531"><em>The trench filled with water before the frost</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3533"><em>Regiments spoken of at Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3533"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Regiments spoken of at Cathair dhearg* (Muileann àrsaidh). Carriers' talk reaches the western hills that regiments not called out since An Dealachadh are spoken of again at Cathair dhearg, spoken of and not yet raised.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3532"><em>Ruth Calder lodges at Sarah Dunmore's</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3534"><em>Snow closes the Muileann àrsaidh road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3534"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19** — *Snow closes the Muileann àrsaidh road* (Muileann àrsaidh). Snow closes the road from Muileann àrsaidh to the coast for nineteen days in an Faoilleach, and the enforcers' wagons stand at the western Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0070"><em>The pit-heads walled</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 19</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3533"><em>Regiments spoken of at Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 19</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0072"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, DE 20** — *The Moot stands apart* (Caol mhòr). The Moot at Caol mhòr resolves that it is no party to the quarrel of the Board and the western towns, and that it will feed any who come hungry to its towns. The resolution is carried by nine votes.
- <a id="ev-VI-0073"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, DE 20** — *The Moot's granaries* (Doire ghlas). The Moot orders its granaries at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas filled beyond the wont, paying from the takings of the wool mills. The minute gives no reason.
- <a id="ev-VI-0074"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, DE 20** — *Sìleas nic Rath* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh lays down the office, and Sìleas nic Rath, her clerk, becomes royal chronicler. Hers is the record of the war that the library afterwards seals.
- <a id="ev-VI-0075"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, DE 20** — *The regiments called up*. Regiments not called to arms since the Severance itself are formed and armed anew, openly, months before any in power will own that war is coming.
- <a id="ev-VI-0076"></a>**26 an t-Samhain, DE 20** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn* (Cathair dhearg). Command of the new-formed regiments is given to Somhairle mac Lachlainn, who rose among the Board's enforcers. The rolls of the Severance companies are brought out of the council's chests at Cathair dhearg to name the regiments, and the old names are read aloud before new men.
- <a id="ev-VI-0077"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The Moot's last petition* (Cathair dhearg). On Christmas Day Martha Greaves carries a petition of the Moot in person to the council at Cathair dhearg. It asks that the western pits be let work out their seams, which the Moot says will be spent in a few years whatever is done. It is received and filed. She is the first speaker of the Moot to enter the council chamber.
- <a id="ev-EVII-3535"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Peter Hale presses the room* (Caol mhòr). In the depth of winter Peter Hale rises before Tional nan Tuathach and says the room has sat three sittings without naming the wall at Muileann àrsaidh or the silence that answered Ruth Calder's letter, and that a gathering of the northern towns which will not say the plainest fact in the north is not doing what it was built to do.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0072"><em>The Moot stands apart</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3536"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The five empty benches* (Caol mhòr). The five benches of the western holdout towns stand chalked but empty in Tional nan Tuathach's own roll, as they have stood since the western delegates rose and left four years before. No one moves to fill them, and the room debates the wall at Muileann àrsaidh with the western towns' own voice absent from it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0072"><em>The Moot stands apart</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3535"><em>Peter Hale presses the room</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3537"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Christina Munro's question* (Caol mhòr). On the stair after the vote, a delegate of the farm towns asks Martha Greaves whether nine hands out of one-and-forty are truly the room's mind, and whether the speaker's own hand, never raised, holds the same mind as the nine. Martha answers only that the chair does not vote, and the question goes unanswered further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0072"><em>The Moot stands apart</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3536"><em>The five empty benches</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3538"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The mills' surplus reckoned* (Doire ghlas). In summer, with the spring clip in heavy and the fair price holding, Martha Greaves reckons the Doire ghlas mills' takings a whole evening in the counting-house and writes an order, at the foot of the mills' own book and not Tional nan Tuathach's, that the granaries of Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas be filled beyond the ordinary wont, paid from the mills alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0073"><em>The Moot's granaries</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3537"><em>Christina Munro's question</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3539"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Grain bought through three factors* (Doire ghlas). Through the last week of an t-Iuchar the grain for the granaries is bought quietly through three separate factors, so that no single merchant should wonder aloud why Tional nan Tuathach's towns want so much of it in a year the harvest already promises well.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0073"><em>The Moot's granaries</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3538"><em>The mills' surplus reckoned</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3540"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *"Enter the weight and the date"* (Doire ghlas). The Doire ghlas granary-keeper asks Martha Greaves whether he should set down a reason for the extra grain, since his book goes before the room's auditors each spring. She tells him to enter the weight and the date and no reason at all, and to send anyone who asks to her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0073"><em>The Moot's granaries</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3539"><em>Grain bought through three factors</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3541"><em>The autumn entry with no reason given</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3541"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The autumn entry with no reason given* (Caol mhòr). Thomas Rook's autumn entry in Tional nan Tuathach's minute records the granaries of Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas standing half again fuller than the five years' average, and gives no reason, none having been given him. Peter Hale reads the figure, looks once at Martha Greaves, and asks nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0073"><em>The Moot's granaries</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3540"><em>"Enter the weight and the date"</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3542"><em>Beathag's letter to the council</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3542"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Beathag's letter to the council* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). In spring Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes to the council, in her own hand alone, asking leave to lay down the office of royal chronicler at the close of summer, being nine-and-sixty that year, and naming her clerk of nine years, Sìleas nic Rath, to take the desk after her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3541"><em>The autumn entry with no reason given</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3543"><em>Sìleas nic Rath told over the tea</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3543"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Sìleas nic Rath told over the tea* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Sìleas nic Rath learns of Beathag's letter not from the council but from Beathag herself, over their usual tea, who tells her she has until an Lùnastal to decide whether she still wants the desk once she has heard the whole of what it costs.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3542"><em>Beathag's letter to the council</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3544"><em>The desk cleared a little at a time</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3544"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The desk cleared a little at a time* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Through the last week of an Lùnastal Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh clears her desk a little at a time, so that the room should show no single day when it stood stripped, leaving only Tormod Pinn's inkstand, the day's half-written page, and the small iron key of the sealed press.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3543"><em>Sìleas nic Rath told over the tea</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3545"><em>"Write what you are let"</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3545"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *"Write what you are let"* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Handing over the key of the sealed press, Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh tells Sìleas nic Rath to write what she is let, as fully as if no one would grudge her a word of it, and to write down what she is not let besides, where and by whom and on what day, since a chronicle that shows only its own leave is no chronicle at all.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3544"><em>The desk cleared a little at a time</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3546"><em>Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh leaves for Àth dhìreach</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3546"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh leaves for Àth dhìreach* (Muileann chaol). The morning after the handing-over, a carrier's cart takes Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh north-east to her sister's house at Àth dhìreach. Raghnall mac Mhuirich comes out to see her off, wishes her a dry ford at Àth bheag, and hands her up himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3545"><em>"Write what you are let"</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3547"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's first page</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3547"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Sìleas nic Rath's first page* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Alone at the desk, Sìleas nic Rath finishes the day's half-written entry in her own hand, smaller and more upright than Beathag's, and adds a line the office's custom does not require: that Eachdraidh na Rìoghachd now passes to a second hand, set down once so it need not be said again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0074"><em>Sìleas nic Rath</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3546"><em>Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh leaves for Àth dhìreach</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3548"><em>Five benches kept chalked in the roll</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3548"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Five benches kept chalked in the roll* (Caol mhòr). The clerk of Tional nan Tuathach keeps the five western towns' benches chalked in the roll of Tional nan Tuathach, under the towns' names, with nothing after them, five years after their delegates walked out.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0072"><em>The Moot stands apart</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3547"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's first page</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3549"><em>Travellers' talk at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3549"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Travellers' talk at An Taigh-seinnse Mòr* (Cuan chrom). In the hall of An Taigh-seinnse Mòr above Cuan chrom the carters of the north road talk through the autumn of regiments to be raised; the landlord takes down the notice of the guild meetings and puts up none in its place.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0075"><em>The regiments called up</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3548"><em>Five benches kept chalked in the roll</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3550"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn summoned to the capital* (Seann Skell). Somhairle mac Lachlainn is called down to Cathair dhearg in the first cold week of an t-Samhain, and rides Slighe a' Ghuail with a corporal and a satchel of the depot's returns that nobody troubles to ask for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3551"><em>The old drill hall opened</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3551"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The old drill hall opened* (Cathair dhearg). A long stone hall behind the council's rooms at Cathair dhearg, used in living memory for nothing grander than storing the city watch's spare pikes, is opened and swept for the reading of An Dealachadh rolls.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3550"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn summoned to the capital</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3552"><em>The rolls unsealed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3552"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The rolls unsealed* (Cathair dhearg). Ledgers of Buidhnean an Dealachaidh, kept in the council's chests some ninety years, are brought out and opened; the ink in one has gone the colour of weak tea, and a clerk works two stuck pages apart with a blunt knife.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3551"><em>The old drill hall opened</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3553"><em>The towns struck through</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3553"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The towns struck through* (Cathair dhearg). Town by town the old roll is checked against the present: some answer still and will send men gladly, others are struck through in a clerk's hand because the town that raised the company is gone, swallowed into a larger one or fallen to scattered farms with no muster-ground left standing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3552"><em>The rolls unsealed</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3554"><em>The lamps lit in the drill hall</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3554"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The lamps lit in the drill hall* (Cathair dhearg). As dark comes on, four lamps are hung along the drill hall's wall and lit with dubhan, the first flame the brackets have carried in a generation, and the reading of the old names goes on by their light into the evening.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3553"><em>The towns struck through</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3555"><em>The count of the standing companies</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3555"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The count of the standing companies* (Cathair dhearg). A clerk totals the column of towns still able to send men, once the dead towns are struck out. The figure is smaller than the roll once named ninety years before, but greater than any command Somhairle mac Lachlainn has held, and it is his from that evening to answer for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3554"><em>The lamps lit in the drill hall</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3556"><em>A corporal bidden to hear the rolls</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3556"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *A corporal bidden to hear the rolls* (Cathair dhearg). Cormac Liath, the old soldier who read the rolls aloud, tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn to bring his own corporal in to hear the old names read, since a man who hears a thing said once in a lamplit hall carries it differently to his company than a man only handed a paper.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3555"><em>The count of the standing companies</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3557"><em>Tional nan Tuathach agrees an Nollaig petition</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3557"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Tional nan Tuathach agrees an Nollaig petition* (Caol mhòr). At Caol mhòr Tional nan Tuathach sits past midnight two days before an Nollaig, turning the wording of its petition over clause by clause until it asks one thing only: that the western pits be let alone to work out seams that will be spent within a few years regardless.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3556"><em>A corporal bidden to hear the rolls</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3558"><em>Martha Greaves sets out for the capital</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3558"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Martha Greaves sets out for the capital* (Doire ghlas). Martha Greaves leaves Doire ghlas two days before an Nollaig with the petition in a leather folder, travelling south by carrier's cart, dubhan coach and at last a hired carriage, and keeps the feast on the road with a cold fowl she cannot bring herself to eat.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3557"><em>Tional nan Tuathach agrees an Nollaig petition</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3559"><em>Frost on Drochaid Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3559"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Frost on Drochaid Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). Martha Greaves comes into Cathair dhearg on an Nollaig morning, the frost lying white and unworn on the bridge's parapet because so few feet have crossed it, the Dia-thìrich keeping no feast that day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3558"><em>Martha Greaves sets out for the capital</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3560"><em>The bench in the passage</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3560"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The bench in the passage* (Cathair dhearg). Martha Greaves waits the better part of an hour on a stone bench outside the council chamber at Cathair dhearg, the petition twice taken out of its folder and twice put back unread, while the rise and fall of unheard voices carries from the room beyond.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3559"><em>Frost on Drochaid Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3561"><em>A name said the Dia-thìris way</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3561"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *A name said the Dia-thìris way* (Cathair dhearg). A clerk calls Martha Greaves into the council chamber, her surname set first and her whole name given the turn of the tongue that shapes every foreign name passing through that room, so that she does not, for a moment, know it for her own.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3560"><em>The bench in the passage</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3562"><em>Received, said the clerk</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3562"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Received, said the clerk* (Cathair dhearg). The council gives Martha Greaves's petition one word and the sound of a pen crossing paper. Nobody at the table speaks to her; the old man at its head inclines his head, and the porter is already at her elbow to show her out again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3561"><em>A name said the Dia-thìris way</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3563"><em>The road home from Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3563"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The road home from Cathair dhearg* (Doire ghlas). Martha Greaves rides the cold road north again with the folder empty on her lap, coming in sight of Doire ghlas's lit windows late on the second night after, the one word the council gave her worn down, by then, to the sound of a pen alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3562"><em>Received, said the clerk</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3564"><em>The Grey House among the old companies</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3564"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *The Grey House among the old companies* (Cathair dhearg). Among the rolls of Buidhnean an Dealachaidh read in the drill hall at Cathair dhearg is a company called only the Grey House, and no one in the room can say why.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <em>The Severance companies stood down</em> <a href="era-pdf:../age_VI/The_Diathir_Legendarium_Age_of_the_Kingdom.pdf#ev-V-0002">→ An Aois Rìoghachd, SE 1</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3563"><em>The road home from Cathair dhearg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3565"><em>Dead towns struck from the rolls</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3565"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Dead towns struck from the rolls* (Cathair dhearg). Where a company of An Dealachadh rolls answers to a town gone or swallowed into another, the clerk strikes the name through; Cormac Liath's reading grows quieter over each.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3564"><em>The Grey House among the old companies</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3566"><em>Martha Greaves keeps an Nollaig on the road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3566"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Martha Greaves keeps an Nollaig on the road* (Caol mhòr). The speaker of Tional nan Tuathach keeps an Nollaig in a hired carriage on the northern road, with Ellen Marsh's bread and cold fowl uneaten at her feet, Athchuinge Dheireannach an Tionail in Peter Hale's leather folder on her knee.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3565"><em>Dead towns struck from the rolls</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3567"><em>Anna nic Phàil's nod across the table</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3567"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *Anna nic Phàil's nod across the table* (Cathair dhearg). In the council chamber, when the speaker of Tional nan Tuathach comes in with the petition, Anna nic Phàil, councillor for Cathair dhomhain, gives her the smallest incline of the head across the width of the table.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0077"><em>The Moot's last petition</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3566"><em>Martha Greaves keeps an Nollaig on the road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-3568"><em>An Taigh-òsta Grianach full at the year's end</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-3568"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20** — *An Taigh-òsta Grianach full at the year's end* (Cnoc dhìreach). An Taigh-òsta Grianach at Cnoc dhìreach is full to the stables at the year's end with men walking to the drill hall at Cathair dhearg to hear their old companies' names.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0076"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn</em>, 26 an t-Samhain, DE 20</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-3567"><em>Anna nic Phàil's nod across the table</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 20</a>.</span>

## The Years DE 21 – 25

- <a id="ev-VI-0078"></a>**12 am Faoilleach, DE 21** — *Arms by the coal line* (Seann Bhral). The Rail Board carries arms and dubhan from Cathair dhearg to Seann Bhral on the coal line and its western branch. The yard at Muileann chrom works day and night on the trains.
- <a id="ev-VI-0079"></a>**20 am Faoilleach, DE 21** — *The hewers gather at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Hewers of the five western towns gather at Àth leathan, where the road from the south enters the hills. The Board's lists name Ruth Calder and Tom Varley among them.
- <a id="ev-VI-0080"></a>**23 am Faoilleach, DE 21** — *The regiments go west* (Seann Skell). The regiments set out from Cathair dhearg by the western road, their carts and lorries running on dubhan, to join the enforcers at Seann Skell in the west.
- <a id="ev-VI-0081"></a>**11 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Battle of Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). The first great battle of An Cogadh Fada, the Long War. The state, whose failing power already leans on Dubhan's fuel, moves against the holdouts in arms.
- <a id="ev-VI-0082"></a>**11 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The dead of Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). The open record counts the kingdom's dead at Àth leathan and not the holdouts'. The Tuathaich tellings put theirs in the hundreds. After this battle Ruth Calder's name is not found in the open record.
- <a id="ev-VI-0083"></a>**11 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Into the hills* (Muileann àrsaidh). After Àth leathan the holdouts give up the southern pits and fall back into the hills about Muileann àrsaidh and Cnoc thais. The pits at Àth leathan are taken without a fight and flooded by the Board's order.
- <a id="ev-VI-0084"></a>**11 an Giblean, DE 21** — *An seachdamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Skell). The seventh regiment is raised from the levies of the west coast and stationed at Seann Skell, the river port nearest the western hills. It holds the road behind the army and the field of Àth leathan.
- <a id="ev-VI-0085"></a>**13 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The field of Àth leathan after* (Àraich Àth leathan). The field of Àth leathan is left unploughed. The patrols of the seventh regiment pass it on the road to the western hills and report it empty.
- <a id="ev-EVII-4001"></a>**14 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The yard at Muileann chrom goes to a double shift* (Seann Bhral). The yard at Muileann chrom takes on a double shift of drivers and firemen for the arms trains west, running by night as well as by day. Eachann mac Ruairidh is given the run, and told to sign the manifest for weight and ask nothing of the goods.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4002"></a>**15 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The first sealed wagons loaded at Muileann chrom* (Seann Bhral). Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's own men load eight wagons behind tarpaulin at Muileann chrom by shuttered lamp, and take the loading out of the yard drivers' hands for the first time in the line's history.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4001"><em>The yard at Muileann chrom goes to a double shift</em>, 14 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4003"></a>**16 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The western branch runs arms by night*. Through am Faoilleach Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch, laid twenty years before for lime and slate, carries arms and dubhan west to Seann Bhral by night, at speeds the branch's rails were never built to bear.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4002"><em>The first sealed wagons loaded at Muileann chrom</em>, 15 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4004"></a>**17 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's quay at Seann Bhral*. At Seann Bhral Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's men unload the arms trains by lantern into a lorry kept always waiting, and give the driver nothing for his signature but a bare manifest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4003"><em>The western branch runs arms by night</em>, 16 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4005"></a>**18 an Giblean, DE 21** — *A company passes the arms train below the capital*. One of the new-raised companies, marching west by night under a corporal Eachann mac Ruairidh had once carried as a passenger, passes below the arms train on the branch road and is not stopped for.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0080"><em>The regiments go west</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4004"><em>Comhairle na Slighe-iarainn's quay at Seann Bhral</em>, 17 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4006"></a>**19 an Giblean, DE 21** — *A Tuathach family on the western branch*. Eachann mac Ruairidh's train passes a Tuathach family walking north along Slighe a' Ghuail's western branch before dawn, a handcart between them. He does not stop, and does not look back.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4005"><em>A company passes the arms train below the capital</em>, 18 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4007"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Cnoc thais comes to Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Tom Varley leads forty hewers and more of Cnoc thais down the ridge drove track to Àth leathan, pit-lamps lit at noon though no face waits at the path's end to work by them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4006"><em>A Tuathach family on the western branch</em>, 19 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4008"><em>Àth naomh comes to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4008"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Àth naomh comes to Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). The hewers of Àth naomh come to Àth leathan marching two abreast, keeping their own order at another town's pit-head though they have nothing there yet to defend.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4007"><em>Cnoc thais comes to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4009"><em>Muileann àrsaidh and Tobar dhearg of the hills come to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4009"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Muileann àrsaidh and Tobar dhearg of the hills come to Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Smaller parties from Muileann àrsaidh and from Tobar dhearg of the hills reach Àth leathan through a second cold dusk, among them boys of fourteen and, from two houses, whole households with none left at home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4008"><em>Àth naomh comes to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4010"><em>Ruth Calder's list begun at the pit-shed</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4010"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Ruth Calder's list begun at the pit-shed* (Àth leathan). Ruth Calder sets up a trestle table at the Àth leathan pit-shed and takes down every man's and boy's name, town by town, with a mark for those who bring their own tools.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4009"><em>Muileann àrsaidh and Tobar dhearg of the hills come to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4011"><em>Sarah Dunmore sends oatmeal to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4011"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Sarah Dunmore sends oatmeal to Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Sarah Dunmore sends two cartloads of oatmeal and a barrel of salted fish down from Muileann àrsaidh for the gathering at Àth leathan, and asks no thanks for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4010"><em>Ruth Calder's list begun at the pit-shed</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4012"><em>Ruth Calder learns Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps its own list</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4012"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Ruth Calder learns Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps its own list* (Àth leathan). Tom Varley brings word to Ruth Calder that Comhairle nam Mèinnean at Cathair mhòr keeps a list of its own, with her name and his set above every other on it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4011"><em>Sarah Dunmore sends oatmeal to Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4013"><em>The pit-sheds and byres given over at Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4013"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The pit-sheds and byres given over at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). The three pit-sheds of Àth leathan fill with sleeping men on straw, and the byres behind the chapel, their cattle turned out, hold the rest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4012"><em>Ruth Calder learns Comhairle nam Mèinnean keeps its own list</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4014"><em>The regiments camp beside the enforcers at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4014"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The regiments camp beside the enforcers at Seann Skell* (Seann Skell). The regiments from Cathair dhearg reach the western Seann Skell and camp beside the enforcers already quartered there, three years settled and waiting for exactly this company.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0080"><em>The regiments go west</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4013"><em>The pit-sheds and byres given over at Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4015"><em>Word of the march reaches Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4015"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Word of the march reaches Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). A carter carries word up from the boundary stones to Àth leathan that the regiments have gone west by the road below Cathair dhearg, their lorries running on dubhan.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0080"><em>The regiments go west</em>, 23 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4014"><em>The regiments camp beside the enforcers at Seann Skell</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4016"><em>Signed for weight and not for goods</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4016"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Signed for weight and not for goods* (Muileann chrom). The yard foreman at Muileann chrom hands Eachann mac Ruairidh a manifest giving only the weight of eight sealed wagons, and he is not to ask what is in them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0078"><em>Arms by the coal line</em>, 12 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4015"><em>Word of the march reaches Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4017"><em>Lamps lit at noon on the hill paths</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4017"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Lamps lit at noon on the hill paths* (Àth leathan). The hewers of the five towns come down to Àth leathan with their pit-lamps lit at noon, so that every farm in the western hills sees them come as pit men.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4016"><em>Signed for weight and not for goods</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4018"><em>Tobar dhearg's captain sets his lamp on the table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4018"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tobar dhearg's captain sets his lamp on the table* (Tobar dhearg). The stooped captain of Tobar dhearg of the hills sets his lamp on Ruth Calder's trestle table before he gives his own name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4017"><em>Lamps lit at noon on the hill paths</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4019"><em>Four hundred names by the sixth evening</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4019"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Four hundred names by the sixth evening* (Àth leathan). By the sixth evening of the gathering Ruth Calder's list at Àth leathan runs past four hundred men and boys of the five towns.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4018"><em>Tobar dhearg's captain sets his lamp on the table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4020"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The five towns form pit companies at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). Through am Faoilleach and an Gearran Ruth Calder and Tom Varley turn the gathering at Àth leathan into five companies, one to a town, each under its own captain and answerable to Tom Varley for the whole body.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0079"><em>The hewers gather at Àth leathan</em>, 20 am Faoilleach, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4021"><em>Blasting powder laid at the spoil-heaps</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4021"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Blasting powder laid at the spoil-heaps* (Àth leathan). Tom Varley lays four kegs of the pits' own blasting powder in the narrow ground below the spoil-heaps, on the road down from Seann Skell, to be fired at his word alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4020"><em>The five towns form pit companies at Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4022"><em>The burn comes up in spate before the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4022"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The burn comes up in spate before the battle* (Àth leathan). A fast thaw in the first week of an Giblean brings the burn below Àth leathan up in spate, closing the ford and leaving only the dry road from Seann Skell for the regiments' approach.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4021"><em>Blasting powder laid at the spoil-heaps</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4023"><em>Ruth Calder's word to the five towns' companies</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4023"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Ruth Calder's word to the five towns' companies* (Àth leathan). On the morning of the battle Ruth Calder tells Tom Varley to carry her word to the five towns' companies, that her list stands and will say who stood at Àth leathan and beside whom, whatever the day brings.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4022"><em>The burn comes up in spate before the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4024"><em>Tobar dhearg's men keep the chapel before the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4024"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tobar dhearg's men keep the chapel before the battle* (Àth leathan). Before dawn on the day of the battle, Tobar dhearg's stooped captain asks that the chapel at Àth leathan stand open, so that any of his men who wish it may go in once before the fighting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4023"><em>Ruth Calder's word to the five towns' companies</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4025"><em>The charge fired below the spoil-heaps</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4025"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The charge fired below the spoil-heaps* (Àraich Àth leathan). Tom Varley fires the blasting powder laid at the spoil-heaps as the regiments' column reaches the narrow ground, checking its head for the better part of an hour before it re-forms and comes on.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4024"><em>Tobar dhearg's men keep the chapel before the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4026"><em>The pit-heads of Àth leathan change hands</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4026"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The pit-heads of Àth leathan change hands* (Àraich Àth leathan). Through the day of the battle the pit-heads of Àth leathan pass more than once between the holdouts and the regiments before falling at last to the kingdom's side.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4025"><em>The charge fired below the spoil-heaps</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4027"><em>The five towns' companies fall back from the field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4027"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The five towns' companies fall back from the field* (Àth leathan).
