By early afternoon the five towns' companies give up the field below Àth leathan and fall back in scattered bodies along the hill paths toward Muileann àrsaidh and Cnoc thais.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4026"><em>The pit-heads of Àth leathan change hands</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4028"><em>Inis àrsaidh victuals the kingdom's host</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4028"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Inis àrsaidh victuals the kingdom's host* (Inis àrsaidh). The river town of Inis àrsaidh, nearest Àraich Àth leathan by water, supplies bread and salt fish to the kingdom's host through the campaign and the battle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4027"><em>The five towns' companies fall back from the field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4029"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn's return of the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4029"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn's return of the battle* (Seann Skell). Within the week Somhairle mac Lachlainn writes a return from Seann Skell naming the companies that fought at Àth leathan and the kingdom's dead, and no more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4028"><em>Inis àrsaidh victuals the kingdom's host</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4030"><em>Sìleas nic Rath searches the record for Ruth Calder's name</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4030"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Sìleas nic Rath searches the record for Ruth Calder's name* (Muileann chaol). Sìleas nic Rath, new to the office of royal chronicler, searches An Clàr Foscailte more than once for Ruth Calder's name after Àth leathan and does not find it, and privately judges the question not hers to press further.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4029"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn's return of the battle</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4031"><em>Doire naomh's grove takes in the field's unclaimed dead</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4031"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Doire naomh's grove takes in the field's unclaimed dead* (Doire naomh). The Dia-thìrich of Doire naomh's grove, closed to strangers, go out onto the field after the regiments pass on and carry many of the unclaimed dead of Àth leathan to their own ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4030"><em>Sìleas nic Rath searches the record for Ruth Calder's name</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4032"><em>Àth chrom's drovers carry the dead of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4032"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Àth chrom's drovers carry the dead of Àth leathan* (Àth chrom). Àth chrom's drovers take their coal and salt carts out along the road to carry the dead of Àth leathan, of both sides, without any record of whom they carried.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4031"><em>Doire naomh's grove takes in the field's unclaimed dead</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4033"><em>Baile fhiadhaich takes in the wounded of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4033"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Baile fhiadhaich takes in the wounded of Àth leathan* (Baile fhiadhaich). Baile fhiadhaich, too far off to send carriers to the field itself, takes in such wounded of Àth leathan as reach it along the west-coast harbour road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4032"><em>Àth chrom's drovers carry the dead of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4034"><em>Nine hundred at Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4034"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Nine hundred at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). By the eve of the battle the muster at Àth leathan counts near nine hundred souls with their carriers, in five companies: Muileann àrsaidh near two hundred, Cnoc thais a hundred and sixty, Àth leathan ninety, Àth naomh sixty and Tobar dhearg forty.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4033"><em>Baile fhiadhaich takes in the wounded of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4035"><em>Sixty firearms and four kegs of powder</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4035"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Sixty firearms and four kegs of powder* (Àth leathan). The five towns have among them some sixty firearms, most of them fowling pieces older than any man carrying them, a dozen rifles, picks and short axes, and four kegs of blasting powder from the pits.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4034"><em>Nine hundred at Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4036"><em>A fever in the byres of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4036"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *A fever in the byres of Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). A fever goes through the byres behind the chapel at Àth leathan in an Gearran and takes an old woman of Cnoc thais who had come down only to be near her grandsons.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4035"><em>Sixty firearms and four kegs of powder</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4037"><em>Singing in the Tobar dhearg line</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4037"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Singing in the Tobar dhearg line* (Àraich Àth leathan). In the waiting before the battle the old captain's men of Tobar dhearg sing low in An Eaglais's own words along their line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0081"><em>Battle of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4036"><em>A fever in the byres of Àth leathan</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4038"><em>Ruth Calder's account ends at the column's coming</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4038"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Ruth Calder's account ends at the column's coming* (Àraich Àth leathan). No page in Ruth Calder's hand, nor any word set down as hers by anyone who stood beside her, tells what she said or did after the regiments' column reached the ground below the spoil-heaps.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4037"><em>Singing in the Tobar dhearg line</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4039"><em>Muileann ruadh takes in wounded officers</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4039"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Muileann ruadh takes in wounded officers* (Muileann ruadh). The custodians of the bath-house at Fuarain Theth Muileann ruadh below Muileann ruadh take in two officers of the regiments wounded in the west, at the council's asking, and set them in the long room among the hewers' widows.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4038"><em>Ruth Calder's account ends at the column's coming</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4040"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tom Varley carries the wounded off the southern ground* (Àth leathan). As the light fails on the day of the battle, Tom Varley gathers hurdles and handcarts and leads the wounded of the southern pits up the ridge drove track, unlit, away from Àth leathan toward Muileann àrsaidh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0082"><em>The dead of Àth leathan</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4041"><em>The carriers pass Àth leathan in the dark</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4041"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The carriers pass Àth leathan in the dark* (Àth leathan). Tom Varley's party of carriers comes within sight of the Àth leathan pit-sheds before dawn and does not stop there, word having already reached them that the town cannot be held through the coming night.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4040"><em>Tom Varley carries the wounded off the southern ground</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4042"><em>Sarah Dunmore receives the wounded at Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4042"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Sarah Dunmore receives the wounded at Muileann àrsaidh* (Muileann àrsaidh). Sarah Dunmore and the women of Muileann àrsaidh come out along the ridge path at dawn to take the hurdles from the carriers' shoulders, and a woman who sets bones is sent for to tend the worst hurt among them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4041"><em>The carriers pass Àth leathan in the dark</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4043"><em>Tom Varley counts the wounded at the gate</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4043"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tom Varley counts the wounded at the gate* (Muileann àrsaidh). Tom Varley counts nine souls brought off the field into Muileann àrsaidh and keeps the number in his head rather than on paper, unwilling to see it set down where it might be weighed against the number that went south.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4042"><em>Sarah Dunmore receives the wounded at Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4044"><em>Tom Varley hears of the flooding at Sarah Dunmore's table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4044"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tom Varley hears of the flooding at Sarah Dunmore's table* (Muileann àrsaidh). Word of the drowned shafts reaches Tom Varley by carter and shepherd, and he and Sarah Dunmore weigh, over several evenings, what purpose the flooding serves beyond telling the hills the seams are done for good.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4043"><em>Tom Varley counts the wounded at the gate</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4045"><em>Somhairle reads the first week's patrol reports</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4045"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Somhairle reads the first week's patrol reports* (Seann Skell). Somhairle mac Lachlainn reads An seachdamh rèisimeid's first patrol reports at Seann Skell by dubhan lamp: the road clear, a cart met and let pass, a farm gate found open and shut again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0084"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4044"><em>Tom Varley hears of the flooding at Sarah Dunmore's table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4046"><em>A young officer writes of the unploughed field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4046"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *A young officer writes of the unploughed field* (Àraich Àth leathan). A patrol officer new to his rank writes into his return that the field of the battle lies as it was left and has not been ploughed, though the season for the first ploughing is well begun on every field around it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4045"><em>Somhairle reads the first week's patrol reports</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4047"><em>Somhairle sends the patrol to walk the field itself</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4047"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Somhairle sends the patrol to walk the field itself* (Àraich Àth leathan). Somhairle mac Lachlainn gives verbal, unwritten instructions for the same officer to walk Àraich Àth leathan rather than the road beside it, and receives an account he sets down in the fewest words the return will bear.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4046"><em>A young officer writes of the unploughed field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4048"><em>The maor of Seann Skell explains the seventh's short rolls</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4048"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The maor of Seann Skell explains the seventh's short rolls* (Seann Skell). The maor of the western Seann Skell tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn privately that coast boats are finding the fishing a week longer than the weather requires, rather than fill a regiment meant to stand against their own hill neighbours.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0084"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4047"><em>Somhairle sends the patrol to walk the field itself</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4049"><em>Tom Varley sends word to every hill farm</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4049"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tom Varley sends word to every hill farm* (Muileann àrsaidh). Tom Varley sends word by boys and shepherds to every hill farm within a day's walk of Muileann àrsaidh asking whether anyone has seen Ruth Calder, and gets back only that nobody has, alive or otherwise.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4048"><em>The maor of Seann Skell explains the seventh's short rolls</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4050"><em>A farm-wife's account of the field's own dead</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4050"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *A farm-wife's account of the field's own dead* (Muileann àrsaidh). A woman below the ridge sends Tom Varley word that some of the battle's dead were carried off by night in the days after by people from the hills, and might lie now in ground no list on either side will ever name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4049"><em>Tom Varley sends word to every hill farm</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4051"><em>An old woman of Àth leathan sees the field the morning after</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4051"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *An old woman of Àth leathan sees the field the morning after* (Àth leathan). An old woman who kept hens at Àth leathan tells of women from the hill farms out on the field with handcarts the morning after the battle, before the regiments came, but says she looked too little to know whose faces she saw.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4050"><em>A farm-wife's account of the field's own dead</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4052"><em>Tom Varley walks to the dyke above the field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4052"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Tom Varley walks to the dyke above the field* (Àraich Àth leathan). On the eighth day Tom Varley walks alone to a stone dyke a quarter-mile from Àraich Àth leathan and is turned back by a young sentry of An seachdamh rèisimeid before he can see more than its empty shape.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0085"><em>The field of Àth leathan after</em>, 13 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4051"><em>An old woman of Àth leathan sees the field the morning after</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4053"><em>Rab of Tobar dhearg carried up the ridge</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4053"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *Rab of Tobar dhearg carried up the ridge* (Muileann àrsaidh). A boy of Tobar dhearg named Rab, wounded in the thigh at Àth leathan, is carried up the ridge path on a handcart by Tom Varley's carriers, saying his own name over in the dark.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4052"><em>Tom Varley walks to the dyke above the field</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4054"><em>The bonesetter at Sarah Dunmore's table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4054"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The bonesetter at Sarah Dunmore's table* (Muileann àrsaidh). A bonesetter of the western hills works on the wounded of Àth leathan by lamplight at Sarah Dunmore's kitchen table at Muileann àrsaidh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0083"><em>Into the hills</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4053"><em>Rab of Tobar dhearg carried up the ridge</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4055"><em>The seventh's rolls short at the coast</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4055"></a>**20 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The seventh's rolls short at the coast* (Seann Skell). An seachdamh rèisimeid's rolls run to some four hundred and twenty men in its second week, short of the order; the maor of the western Seann Skell puts it down to boats still at sea.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0084"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 11 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4054"><em>The bonesetter at Sarah Dunmore's table</em>, 20 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0086"></a>**21 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The wartime tithe*. For the war a tax is laid, for a time, on every sale of dubhan in the kingdom. It is never lifted after the war ends.
- <a id="ev-VI-0087"></a>**29 an Giblean, DE 21** — *The tithe at the pumps* (Fèill Muileann òg). The wartime tithe is taken at the dubhan depots, where a clerk of the Treasury sits beside every pump. Within a month the fair-court at Muileann òg records the first complaint against it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0088"></a>**7 an Cèitean, DE 21** — *A' chiad rèisimeid raised* (Inis mhòr). The first regiment is raised at Inis mhòr, the river port beside the capital, from the capital's own companies. It guards the council, the mint and the bridge over the Abhainn dhomhain.
- <a id="ev-VI-0089"></a>**13 an Cèitean, DE 21** — *A' chiad chabhlach raised* (Àth gharbh). The first fleet is raised from the south-west harbours and stationed at Àth gharbh, its hulls lying in the harbour of Doire shean a short walk away. It is sent round the western cape to stop the coal going out by sea from the Tuathaich ports.
- <a id="ev-VI-0090"></a>**20 an Cèitean, DE 21** — *An ceathramh cabhlach raised* (Cuan shean). The fourth fleet is raised at Cuan shean on the west coast and joins the first off the Tuathaich shore. Between them they close Seann Skell and Cnoc bhàn in the north-west to every boat but fishing boats, and search those.
- <a id="ev-VI-0091"></a>**21 an Cèitean, DE 21** — *The siege of Muileann àrsaidh* (Muileann àrsaidh). The regiments lay siege to Muileann àrsaidh. The town holds for weeks on stored coal and potatoes, and its pit-heads are taken one by one. Sìleas nic Rath's open record gives the day it fell and nothing else.
- <a id="ev-VI-0092"></a>**5 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21** — *An treas rèisimeid raised* (Cathair mhòr). The third regiment is raised at Cathair mhòr, where the Mine Board keeps its offices in the old stone house of Mac Ùisdein. Its first muster is held under the market cross the house raised.
- <a id="ev-VI-0093"></a>**13 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21** — *An còigeamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Warr). The fifth regiment is raised at Seann Warr on the lake shore west of the capital. It is sent north to relieve the regiments before Muileann àrsaidh.
- <a id="ev-VI-0094"></a>**21 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21** — *The capital's lamp-houses rationed* (Cathair dhearg). Dubhan for the army is taken before every other use. The poorer streets of the capital go dark again, as they were before the fuel came, and the lamp-houses of Cathair dhearg ration it street by street.
- <a id="ev-VI-0095"></a>**29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21** — *Families at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Families from the western pits come into Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas with what they can carry. The Moot feeds them from its own stores, as it resolved to do. The council sends nothing and forbids nothing.
- <a id="ev-VI-0096"></a>**17 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *The Moot's granaries opened* (Caol mhòr). The Moot opens its granaries at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas to the families from the west. Its minute records how much was given and the names of the families; it is one of the few Tuathaich records of the war that the library does not hold.
- <a id="ev-VI-0097"></a>**25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *Agnes Pike's school as a shelter* (Doire ghlas). The school at Doire ghlas that Agnes Pike founded is given over to the families from the west, and its benches serve for beds. Ellen Marsh, who teaches there, takes down the families' accounts.
- <a id="ev-EVII-4501"></a>**26 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *A clerk of An t-Ionmhas is sent to Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). Cailean Ros of An t-Ionmhas comes to sit beside the fair pump at Muileann òg and mark the tithe on every gallon drawn; Ùna nic Ailein shows him the tank's own measure, which nobody in the capital had thought to teach him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0087"><em>The tithe at the pumps</em>, 29 an Giblean, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4502"></a>**27 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *The first tithe taken at Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). Ùna nic Ailein records the first gallon of dubhan sold under Deachamh a' Chogaidh at the Muileann òg pump, eleven gallons to Seumas Buidhe the smith, one part in twelve set aside before the coin changes hands.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0087"><em>The tithe at the pumps</em>, 29 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4501"><em>A clerk of An t-Ionmhas is sent to Muileann òg</em>, 26 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4503"></a>**28 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *The first complaint against the tithe* (Muileann òg). In the fifth week of the tithe, Barabal nic Rath, a weaver of Muileann òg, brings her own five weeks' reckoning of it to Cùirt na Fèille and asks that her complaint against its silence on its own ending be written into the book.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0087"><em>The tithe at the pumps</em>, 29 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4502"><em>The first tithe taken at Muileann òg</em>, 27 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4504"></a>**29 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *An ceathramh cabhlach searches the boats at Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). A hull of An ceathramh cabhlach boards and searches every boat at Caol mhòr's harbour wall for dubhan or coal carried against the closing of the coast; the engine-boats Joe Ashby has fitted are searched last and longest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0090"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach raised</em>, 20 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4503"><em>The first complaint against the tithe</em>, 28 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4505"></a>**30 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *Joe Ashby is asked to mend a fleet hull* (Caol mhòr). An unsigned letter from Caol mhòr's harbour depot asks Joe Ashby to mend an engine of An ceathramh cabhlach that the depot's own men cannot; the letter is signed with a mark, and names no fleet and no rank.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0090"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach raised</em>, 20 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4504"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach searches the boats at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4506"></a>**31 an t-Iuchar, DE 21** — *Joe Ashby refits the fleet hull* (Caol mhòr). Joe Ashby and Ned Fowler find and mend a wrongly seated valve aboard an unnamed hull of An ceathramh cabhlach at Caol mhòr's depot jetty, and are paid at the harbour's own rate, in coin, and asked no questions.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0090"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach raised</em>, 20 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4505"><em>Joe Ashby is asked to mend a fleet hull</em>, 30 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4507"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *One part in twelve* (Cathair dhearg). Deachamh a' Chogaidh is laid at one part in twelve of every sale of dubhan, taken at the point of sale by a clerk of An t-Ionmhas sitting beside the pump.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0086"><em>The wartime tithe</em>, 21 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4506"><em>Joe Ashby refits the fleet hull</em>, 31 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4508"><em>Cailean Ros given the cold corner</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4508"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Cailean Ros given the cold corner* (Muileann òg). An t-Ionmhas's young clerk at the Muileann òg pump, Cailean Ros, is given the coldest corner of the toll-house's upper room against the weather, and takes it without complaint.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0087"><em>The tithe at the pumps</em>, 29 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4507"><em>One part in twelve</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4509"><em>The lieutenant laughs at Will Tanner's locker</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4509"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The lieutenant laughs at Will Tanner's locker* (Caol mhòr). Searching the boats at Caol mhòr, An ceathramh cabhlach's lieutenant finds Will Tanner's false locker under the stern thwart with nothing in it but a jar of spirit, laughs once, and writes nothing of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0090"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach raised</em>, 20 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4508"><em>Cailean Ros given the cold corner</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4510"><em>The depot's tally names no fitter</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4510"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The depot's tally names no fitter* (Caol mhòr). The fleet depot at Caol mhòr enters the mending of a hull's engine and the sum paid out, and names no fitter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4509"><em>The lieutenant laughs at Will Tanner's locker</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4511"><em>The tithe-clerks' first returns</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4511"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The tithe-clerks' first returns* (Muileann òg). An t-Ionmhas's clerks at the pumps send in their first month's returns; the clerk at Muileann òg's is the neatest and the smallest.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0087"><em>The tithe at the pumps</em>, 29 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4510"><em>The depot's tally names no fitter</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4512"><em>Hay cleared from the barracks at Inis mhòr</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4512"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Hay cleared from the barracks at Inis mhòr* (Inis mhòr). The farmers of Seann Vell are given a week to take their hay out of the barracks at Inis mhòr when A' chiad rèisimeid is raised there; what is not taken is fed to the regiment's horses.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0088"><em>A' chiad rèisimeid raised</em>, 7 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4511"><em>The tithe-clerks' first returns</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4513"><em>The ferrymen of Àth gharbh go to A' chiad chabhlach</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4513"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The ferrymen of Àth gharbh go to A' chiad chabhlach* (Àth gharbh). Four of the ferrymen of Àth gharbh go into A' chiad chabhlach at its raising, and the ferry at the walled ford is worked through the war by the oldest of them and his daughter.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0089"><em>A' chiad chabhlach raised</em>, 13 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4512"><em>Hay cleared from the barracks at Inis mhòr</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4514"><em>The chandlers of Cuan shean</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4514"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The chandlers of Cuan shean* (Cuan shean). The chandlers of Cuan shean, An ceathramh cabhlach's harbour, sell out of rope and canvas within a month of the fleet's raising and send to Ros dhomhain for more at a price they say is war.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0090"><em>An ceathramh cabhlach raised</em>, 20 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4513"><em>The ferrymen of Àth gharbh go to A' chiad chabhlach</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4515"><em>A tithe-clerk at the pans of Caol ìseal</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4515"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *A tithe-clerk at the pans of Caol ìseal* (Caol ìseal). An t-Ionmhas's clerk for the tithe sits at the dubhan pump by the salt pans of Caol ìseal; the salt-boilers pay their part in twelve on every barrel for the pans and grumble that salt pays twice.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0086"><em>The wartime tithe</em>, 21 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4514"><em>The chandlers of Cuan shean</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4516"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The regiments break the ditch-bridge at Muileann àrsaidh* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the grey hour before dawn on 21 an Cèitean the regiments' advance breaks the ditch-bridge on the southern road and closes the gap old Fraser left unwalled the autumn before, shutting Muileann àrsaidh's ring rather than forcing it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4517"><em>The southern road is cut</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4517"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The southern road is cut* (Muileann àrsaidh). By noon of the first day a second company digs in across the southern road below Muileann àrsaidh, closing the town's last cart road and leaving only hill paths a person on foot might use.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4516"><em>The regiments break the ditch-bridge at Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4518"><em>Meikle's counting of the siege stores</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4518"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Meikle's counting of the siege stores* (Muileann àrsaidh). Muileann àrsaidh's clerk Meikle sets a weekly rationing of coal and potatoes for the town under siege, and the stores are found, by his own careful counting, to hold weeks rather than days.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4517"><em>The southern road is cut</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4519"><em>The bell rung for a pit-head</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4519"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The bell rung for a pit-head* (Muileann àrsaidh). On Meikle's proposal the chapel bell of Muileann àrsaidh is rung once for every pit-head the regiments take, so the town learns what is lost each day at a single stroke rather than piecemeal.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4518"><em>Meikle's counting of the siege stores</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4520"><em>The northern pit-head falls</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4520"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The northern pit-head falls* (Muileann àrsaidh). The northern pit-head, nearest the wall's unfinished stretch, is taken on the sixth day of the siege after an afternoon's fighting that costs the town two of its own men.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4519"><em>The bell rung for a pit-head</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4521"><em>Sarah Dunmore's kitchen serves as the town's dressing-station</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4521"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Sarah Dunmore's kitchen serves as the town's dressing-station* (Muileann àrsaidh). Sarah Dunmore's kitchen, already used for the wounded of Àth leathan that spring, tends the siege's own wounded through the weeks that follow, from stray shot to the ordinary hurts of a town crowded behind a wall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4520"><em>The northern pit-head falls</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4522"><em>Weir keeps the Sunday service through the siege</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4522"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Weir keeps the Sunday service through the siege* (Muileann àrsaidh). The priest Weir keeps Muileann àrsaidh's one weekly service without missing a Sunday through the whole siege, preaching shorter each week and reading the same psalm three Sundays running.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4521"><em>Sarah Dunmore's kitchen serves as the town's dressing-station</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4523"><em>The graves behind the chapel</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4523"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The graves behind the chapel* (Muileann àrsaidh). The dead of the siege are buried behind Muileann àrsaidh's chapel through the weeks of the siege, in the same ground the western hills have used since before An Dealachadh.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4522"><em>Weir keeps the Sunday service through the siege</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4524"><em>A picket's boast names the third and fifth regiments</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4524"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *A picket's boast names the third and fifth regiments* (Muileann àrsaidh). A picket shouts across the gap at the taken northern pit-head that a regiment has come north from Cathair mhòr under the Mac Ùisdein cross and another from Seann Warr, and the boast reaches the town before any surer word does.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0092"><em>An treas rèisimeid raised</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0093"><em>An còigeamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4523"><em>The graves behind the chapel</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4525"><em>old Fraser counts the smoke on the southern ridge</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4525"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *old Fraser counts the smoke on the southern ridge* (Muileann àrsaidh). old Fraser distrusts a picket's shouted boast but counts three mornings running of new fires on the southern ridge, and brings the count, not the boast, before the town's pit-shed.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0092"><em>An treas rèisimeid raised</em>, 5 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0093"><em>An còigeamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4524"><em>A picket's boast names the third and fifth regiments</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4526"><em>Word of the rationed capital reaches the besieged town</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4526"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Word of the rationed capital reaches the besieged town* (Muileann àrsaidh). A man briefly taken and released at the wall brings word into Muileann àrsaidh that the capital's poorer streets go dark again, the army's dubhan being served before the lamp-houses.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0094"><em>The capital's lamp-houses rationed</em>, 21 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4525"><em>old Fraser counts the smoke on the southern ridge</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4527"><em>The last pit-head's line gives way</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4527"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The last pit-head's line gives way* (Muileann àrsaidh). In the grey hour before dawn, seven weeks after the siege began, the thinned line at the last pit-head gives way without a fight anyone in the town could afterward set down in order.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4526"><em>Word of the rationed capital reaches the besieged town</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4528"><em>Tom Varley leaves for Cnoc thais</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4528"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Tom Varley leaves for Cnoc thais* (Muileann àrsaidh). As Muileann àrsaidh falls Tom Varley slips out by the hill path toward Cnoc thais, meaning to see his own shaft there fired by his own hand before any regiment comes near it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4527"><em>The last pit-head's line gives way</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4529"><em>Sarah Dunmore opens her own door</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4529"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Sarah Dunmore opens her own door* (Muileann àrsaidh). With no line left anywhere in the town to hold, Sarah Dunmore opens her own door to the soldiers before they can open it for her, and is searched and let be.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4528"><em>Tom Varley leaves for Cnoc thais</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4530"><em>Meikle's rationing</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4530"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Meikle's rationing* (Muileann àrsaidh). Through Sèist Muileann àrsaidh Meikle keeps the town's counting: a set weight of meal to a household by the week and a set weight of coal to a hearth by the day.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4529"><em>Sarah Dunmore opens her own door</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4531"><em>The children's game of the six pit-heads</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4531"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The children's game of the six pit-heads* (Muileann àrsaidh). Children of besieged Muileann àrsaidh play a game chanting the names of the six pit-heads, slapping a hand down at each as it is lost.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4530"><em>Meikle's rationing</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4532"><em>The eastern pit-head given up</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4532"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The eastern pit-head given up* (Muileann àrsaidh). On Tom Varley's counsel the besieged give up the eastern pit-head of Muileann àrsaidh without a fight, the ground about it too wide to hold without stripping the wall.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0091"><em>The siege of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 21 an Cèitean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4531"><em>The children's game of the six pit-heads</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4533"><em>An còigeamh rèisimeid musters on the harbour wall</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4533"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *An còigeamh rèisimeid musters on the harbour wall* (Seann Warr). An còigeamh rèisimeid musters on the harbour wall at Seann Warr, there being no ground inside the walls wide enough for its companies to stand in line.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0093"><em>An còigeamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 13 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4532"><em>The eastern pit-head given up</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4534"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The first family reaches Doire ghlas* (Doire ghlas). A woman, three children and her husband's father, too lame to walk the whole road, reach Ellen Marsh's own gate at Doire ghlas out of the western hills, the first of a trickle that will not stop by the year's end. They say only the town's name, Àth leathan, and no more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0095"><em>Families at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4535"><em>The eleven of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4535"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The eleven of Muileann àrsaidh* (Muileann àrsaidh). Eleven souls of three farms near Muileann àrsaidh leave together in the night before the ditch-bridge falls, judging a siege at hand and choosing the road north over the ring that is about to close. They reach Doire ghlas and Caol mhòr within the fortnight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0095"><em>Families at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4534"><em>The first family reaches Doire ghlas</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4536"><em>Àth leathan's pits given as flooded</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4536"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Àth leathan's pits given as flooded* (Àth leathan). A woman of Àth leathan tells Ellen Marsh plainly, in the humans' tongue and then in Dia-thìris, that her town's pits were flooded by the regiments' own order within a day of the fighting's end, so that nothing is left there for her household to return to.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0095"><em>Families at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4535"><em>The eleven of Muileann àrsaidh</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4537"><em>Hugh Ferris's wage-ledger</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4537"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Hugh Ferris's wage-ledger* (Doire ghlas). An old hewer of Àth leathan, forty years at the coal and ten more keeper of the pit-shed's tallies, carries away under his coat the ledger of wages owed him rather than any clothing or food, and gives it to Ellen Marsh to keep beside her own books.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0095"><em>Families at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4536"><em>Àth leathan's pits given as flooded</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4538"><em>Martha Greaves writes to an Leabharlann</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4538"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Martha Greaves writes to an Leabharlann* (Caol mhòr). Martha Greaves writes to Sìleas nic Rath at Muileann chaol, not to ask anything of an Leabharlann but to set down, outside her own kitchen table, that Tional nan Tuathach has fed the west's hungry while the council has sent nothing north and forbidden nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0096"><em>The Moot's granaries opened</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4537"><em>Hugh Ferris's wage-ledger</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4539"><em>Thomas Rook's register begun</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4539"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Thomas Rook's register begun* (Caol mhòr). Thomas Rook rules a plain ledger into columns, name, town of origin, family and taken in, and keeps it from the first week of the families' coming. By the end of an Cèitean he counts three hundred and forty souls taken in at Caol mhòr and Doire ghlas together.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0096"><em>The Moot's granaries opened</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4538"><em>Martha Greaves writes to an Leabharlann</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4540"><em>William Reid questions the promise's floor</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4540"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *William Reid questions the promise's floor* (Caol mhòr). At a sitting called out of the calendar, the eastern delegate William Reid asks the room whether it has considered that a promise to feed the west's people indefinitely was made without knowing how long the feeding would be needed. Martha Greaves answers that the not knowing excuses nothing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0096"><em>The Moot's granaries opened</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4539"><em>Thomas Rook's register begun</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4541"><em>Ellen Marsh's twelfth book begun</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4541"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Ellen Marsh's twelfth book begun* (Doire ghlas). Ellen Marsh begins, without quite deciding to begin it, a twelfth book, kept in Dia-thìris as her eleven before it, of what the war's families tell her in the school's hall of an evening: not a life's telling saved up, but the sharp particular things a mind cannot help keeping.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4540"><em>William Reid questions the promise's floor</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4542"><em>The families name the war-book</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4542"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *The families name the war-book* (Doire ghlas). The families sheltered under Agnes Pike's roof come, within the first month, to call Ellen Marsh's new book the war-book among themselves, and bring things to it the way a thing is brought to be weighed, whether or not she ever asked them for a telling.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4541"><em>Ellen Marsh's twelfth book begun</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4543"><em>Hugh Ferris's account of the pit-shed</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4543"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Hugh Ferris's account of the pit-shed* (Doire ghlas). The old hewer of Àth leathan gives Ellen Marsh, for the war-book, an exact accounting of the pit-shed where Ruth Calder once read out the agreement of the five towns, believing it flooded or fallen, and wishing it set down once more before it goes under.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4542"><em>The families name the war-book</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4544"><em>A child gives Ruth Calder's name</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4544"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *A child gives Ruth Calder's name* (Doire ghlas). A girl of the Muileann àrsaidh eleven asks Ellen Marsh to set Ruth Calder's name in the war-book, though she has, by her own word, nothing true to give beside it: only what her mother says of a name dropped from every list the kingdom keeps since the spring.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4543"><em>Hugh Ferris's account of the pit-shed</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4545"><em>Nell Forbes's dresser</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4545"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Nell Forbes's dresser* (Doire ghlas). A woman of Àth leathan sheltering at Doire ghlas tells Ellen Marsh that she thinks more often of the kitchen dresser she left with the plates on it than of the house itself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4544"><em>A child gives Ruth Calder's name</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4546"><em>A harbour boy's word on beggaring</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4546"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *A harbour boy's word on beggaring* (Caol mhòr). A harbourmaster's boy of Caol mhòr tells the speaker of Tional nan Tuathach, repeating his father, that Tional nan Tuathach will beggar itself feeding the western hills and serve the council right.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0096"><em>The Moot's granaries opened</em>, 17 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4545"><em>Nell Forbes's dresser</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4547"><em>Seed-corn sent west from Caol mhòr</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4547"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Seed-corn sent west from Caol mhòr* (Caol mhòr). Tional nan Tuathach sends seed-corn from the stores at Caol mhòr to the farms of the western hills that fed the column's families, entered in the roll as a loan with no term.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0095"><em>Families at Caol mhòr</em>, 29 an t-Ògmhios, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4546"><em>A harbour boy's word on beggaring</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4548"><em>Meal from Cnoc ghorm for Doire ghlas</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4548"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Meal from Cnoc ghorm for Doire ghlas* (Cnoc ghorm). The Tuathaich of Cnoc ghorm send three carts of meal down to Doire ghlas for the western families in Agnes Pike's school, the carters asking no receipt.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0097"><em>Agnes Pike's school as a shelter</em>, 25 an t-Iuchar, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4547"><em>Seed-corn sent west from Caol mhòr</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-4549"><em>Doire shean's market-clerk counts the tithe</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-4549"></a>**1 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Doire shean's market-clerk counts the tithe* (Doire shean). At Doire shean the market-clerk, who keeps the new count and the old side by side, keeps a third column now for the tithe paid at the harbour pump.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0086"><em>The wartime tithe</em>, 21 an Giblean, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-4548"><em>Meal from Cnoc ghorm for Doire ghlas</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0098"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Cnoc thais taken* (Cnoc thais). Cnoc thais is taken after the regiments cut the road to its pits. Tom Varley's two shafts are fired and sealed. The open record gives the number of holdouts taken, and not the number who went on into the hills.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-4528"><em>Tom Varley leaves for Cnoc thais</em>, 1 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0098a"></a>**10 an Lùnastal, DE 21** — *Onto the windy coast* (Cnoc thais). Some of the holdouts of Cnoc thais go on beyond the hills and out onto the windy coast of the far north-west. The regiments follow them to the edge of the shire of Seann Vell and no farther. The open record names them, as it names every foe of the war, only as those 'of no shire'.
- <a id="ev-VI-0099"></a>**23 an t-Sultain, DE 21** — *An dàrna cabhlach raised* (Seann Skell). The second fleet is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast, to keep the eastern and southern waters while the first and fourth are in the north-west.
- <a id="ev-VI-0100"></a>**2 an Dàmhair, DE 21** — *Raiders take the salt-boats* (Spùinneadairean-mara). With the fleets drawn to the north-west, raiders from the eastern waters take two salt-boats off Àth bheag and burn a third. The second fleet runs down one of the raiders off Baile ìseal.
- <a id="ev-VI-0101"></a>**17 an Dàmhair, DE 21** — *An siathamh rèisimeid raised* (Cnoc bheag). The sixth regiment is raised at Cnoc bheag, the great river port of the Hawk houses in the north-central country. It holds the northern road between the Tuathaich shires and the middle of the island, and the Hawk houses bless its colours by their own rite.
- <a id="ev-VI-0102"></a>**25 an Dàmhair, DE 21** — *An dàrna rèisimeid raised* (Àth dhìreach). The second regiment is raised at Àth dhìreach in the east and set to guard the coal line and the library road. Its camp is the first soldiery the town of Muileann chaol has seen.
- <a id="ev-VI-0103"></a>**2 an t-Samhain, DE 21** — *An ceathramh rèisimeid raised* (Caol bheag). The fourth regiment is raised at Caol bheag in the north-east. It goes down the Abhainn ghorm to Ros chiar, is shipped west round the north coast in hired dubhan hulls, and is landed at Ceann mhòr in the Tuathaich north.
- <a id="ev-VI-0104"></a>**10 an t-Samhain, DE 21** — *The regiments at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). The fourth regiment is quartered at Ceann mhòr, in the old human magistrate's house that the maor has kept since the shires were drawn. The Moot protests the quartering. The protest is received.
- <a id="ev-VI-0105"></a>**15 an t-Samhain, DE 21** — *The fishermen of Cathair gheal* (Cathair gheal). The fleets off the north-west search the fishing boats of Cathair gheal on every day they put out. The fishermen petition the Moot, and the Moot petitions the council. The searching goes on.
- <a id="ev-VI-0106"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, DE 21** — *An t-ochdamh rèisimeid raised* (Inis uaine). The eighth regiment is raised at Inis uaine on the Abhainn chaol in the east, to guard the dubhan depots and tanks of the eastern ports, which the council fears the holdouts may fire.
- <a id="ev-VI-0107"></a>**1 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *An treas cabhlach raised* (Baile ghorm). The third fleet is raised at Baile ghorm on the south-west coast, and carries the army's dubhan up the west coast in tank-hulls to the regiments in the hills.
- <a id="ev-VI-0108"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The Baile chrom vigil* (Baile chrom). The Grey Night sect at Baile chrom keeps its vigil as always. The regiments quartered along the coast report a night when the whole town was dark and silent; they search it, and find nothing.
- <a id="ev-VI-0109"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg* (Àth naomh). The last two western towns, Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg, open their roads to the regiments without a siege. Their pits are flooded. The open record names no holdouts taken at either.
- <a id="ev-EVII-5001"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Tom Varley reckons the powder for his own shafts* (Cnoc thais). In the last week of an Cèitean, with the road below Cnoc thais already cut, Tom Varley and Angus Rennie's cousin work out by lamplight how much powder will bring the lower galleries down clean and how much less would only crack the timbering.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5002"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *A shepherd's path left unwatched* (Cnoc thais). The regiment below Cnoc thais spends the better part of a month digging and drilling before it finds a shepherd's path along the northern ridge too steep for anything but goats, which the town's own watchers had judged not worth the watching.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5001"><em>Tom Varley reckons the powder for his own shafts</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5003"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Tom Varley fires his own two shafts* (Cnoc thais). Tom Varley goes down each shaft alone in the grey hour and fires the charges himself, refusing another man's offer to do it, and stands at the shaft-head afterward watching the smoke come up thin against a low sky.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5002"><em>A shepherd's path left unwatched</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5004"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Forty-one taken at Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). The regiment's muster gives forty-one holdouts marched south as prisoners from Cnoc thais; it gives no figure for those already gone up into the hills by paths the shepherd had not shown the soldiers.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5003"><em>Tom Varley fires his own two shafts</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5005"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Tom Varley takes the rabbit path* (Cnoc thais). Tom Varley leaves the falling town by a path he last walked as a boy after rabbits, with five other hewers who choose, each in his own time, to take it rather than stand and be taken.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5004"><em>Forty-one taken at Cnoc thais</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5006"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *A warning at the shielings*. On the second night out, sitting at a small fire among the summer shielings, one of Tom Varley's party argues that the near hills will not be let stand a season longer, and the others find no better guess to set against him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5005"><em>Tom Varley takes the rabbit path</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5007"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Seven parties on an Oirthir Ghaothach*. Word passes between separate handfuls out of Cnoc thais, the last of Muileann àrsaidh's scattered folk and one party out of Àth naomh, until seven parties in all, somewhat short of two hundred souls, sit on the same stretch of unclaimed ground.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5006"><em>A warning at the shielings</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5008"><em>Cairstine's coast path</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5008"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Cairstine's coast path*. A trader named Cairstine, who has walked the coast path with salt and needles twice a year since before the war had a name, carries the season's word up to the fisherfolk and the seven parties both.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0099"><em>An dàrna cabhlach raised</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5007"><em>Seven parties on an Oirthir Ghaothach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5009"><em>An dàrna cabhlach's raising told on an Oirthir Ghaothach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5009"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *An dàrna cabhlach's raising told on an Oirthir Ghaothach* (Seann Skell). Cairstine tells Tom Varley's fire that An dàrna cabhlach was raised that season at the southern Seann Skell out of the harbour towns and Deas-ghnàth a' Ghuail's own boatmen, to hold water that had stood quiet a generation.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0099"><em>An dàrna cabhlach raised</em>, 23 an t-Sultain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5008"><em>Cairstine's coast path</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5010"><em>The burned boat's crew put ashore</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5010"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The burned boat's crew put ashore* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The crew of the salt-boat burned off Àth bheag are put ashore some days after at the light of Baile ìseal, with nothing left of a season's work but the clothes they stand up in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0100"><em>Raiders take the salt-boats</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5009"><em>An dàrna cabhlach's raising told on an Oirthir Ghaothach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5011"><em>A fisherman's word on the door left open</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5011"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *A fisherman's word on the door left open* (Baile ìseal). A fisherman of Baile ìseal tells Cairstine that a kingdom which shuts a door on nothing much will find another door, one it did not think to watch, standing open behind it, and she carries the saying north with the rest of the season's news.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0100"><em>Raiders take the salt-boats</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5010"><em>The burned boat's crew put ashore</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5012"><em>Tom Varley's private tally</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5012"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Tom Varley's private tally*. Through the autumn Tom Varley keeps, unwritten, a tally in his own head of the men who came out of Cnoc thais with him, the men the regiment marched south, and a field left unploughed below Àth leathan he cannot yet set down as finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5011"><em>A fisherman's word on the door left open</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5013"><em>The first evening at the edge of the sea</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5013"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The first evening at the edge of the sea*. In the last clear evening before the hard weather turns, Tom Varley stands on a strand of black shingle at the edge of an Oirthir Ghaothach and watches the light go out of the sky without any sunset to mark the day's end.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5012"><em>Tom Varley's private tally</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5014"><em>Mary Kessock's two ends</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5014"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Mary Kessock's two ends* (Cnoc thais). At the council of Cnoc thais in the chapel room an old widow, Mary Kessock, says a town threatened by soldiers it cannot fight may be taken whole or leave the takers nothing and go. The room begins to make ready to leave.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5013"><em>The first evening at the edge of the sea</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5015"><em>Mary Kessock stays at her door</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5015"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Mary Kessock stays at her door* (Cnoc thais). When Cnoc thais falls, the old widow Mary Kessock stays at her own door and raises a hand to Tom Varley as he goes up the rabbit path.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098"><em>Cnoc thais taken</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5014"><em>Mary Kessock's two ends</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5016"><em>A hind brought down on an Oirthir Ghaothach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5016"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *A hind brought down on an Oirthir Ghaothach* (Cnoc thais). On the walk to an Oirthir Ghaothach a man of Àth naomh brings down a hind with a single cast of the spear he had carried from his own town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5015"><em>Mary Kessock stays at her door</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5017"><em>Calum Odhar's byre</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5017"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Calum Odhar's byre* (Cnoc thais). A widower of an Oirthir Ghaothach, Calum Odhar, who fishes a two-man boat out of a cove with no name, gives the byre behind his house to the six men of Cnoc thais and asks only whether they can mend a net.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0098a"><em>Onto the windy coast</em>, 10 an Lùnastal, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5016"><em>A hind brought down on an Oirthir Ghaothach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5018"><em>Cnoc bhàn's harbour shut to strangers</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5018"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Cnoc bhàn's harbour shut to strangers* (Cnoc bhàn). The Tuathaich of Cnoc bhàn shut their harbour to boats they do not know through the autumn, fearing raiders with the fleets drawn to the north-west, and turn away a Dia-thìreach trader with a load of salt.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0100"><em>Raiders take the salt-boats</em>, 2 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5017"><em>Calum Odhar's byre</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5019"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh watches the camp from her garden wall* (Àth dhìreach). Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh, retired at Àth dhìreach, watches An dàrna rèisimeid's camp rise from her own garden wall and is asked by its young captain whether the wall marks ground his picket line needs; it does not. She notes the town gives the company no trouble and is given none.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0102"><em>An dàrna rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5020"><em>Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes to Sìleas nic Rath of the camp</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5020"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes to Sìleas nic Rath of the camp* (Àth dhìreach). Beathag writes to Sìleas nic Rath that she trusts her own eyes on a garden wall better than she ever let herself trust the reports that once reached her desk from towns she had never stood in. The line is struck through once and left to stand, the ink thin enough to read beneath it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0102"><em>An dàrna rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5019"><em>Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh watches the camp from her garden wall</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5021"><em>The fourth marches down to the river</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5021"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The fourth marches down to the river* (Caol bheag). An ceathramh rèisimeid marches from Caol bheag to the river on a frosted morning, the whole town turned out along the road. Corporal Dùghall mac Iain's own mother stands at the mill corner and says nothing at all as he passes, which he takes, without either of them saying it, for the greater kindness.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5020"><em>Beathag nic Fhionnlaigh writes to Sìleas nic Rath of the camp</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5022"><em>The fourth's voyage down the Abhainn ghorm</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5022"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The fourth's voyage down the Abhainn ghorm* (Caol bheag). An ceathramh rèisimeid goes down the Abhainn ghorm to Ros chiar in refitted coal barges, the two days' journey the maps had promised done in a day and a half on the autumn spate, the barge-men steering more than rowing, the men passing the crossing in games, arguments and a harvest song none of them had thought to sing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5021"><em>The fourth marches down to the river</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5023"><em>The hired hulls put out from Ros chiar</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5023"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The hired hulls put out from Ros chiar* (Ros chiar). An ceathramh rèisimeid's hired dubhan hulls put out from Ros chiar into a turning sea, five days round the north cape with the tanks below decks giving off a smell that does not leave the men's kit for weeks. A boy of the second company goes overboard reaching for a loosed line and is hauled back half-drowned.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5022"><em>The fourth's voyage down the Abhainn ghorm</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5024"><em>One hull parts company off the north cape</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5024"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *One hull parts company off the north cape* (Ceann mhòr). In the worst of the second night's weather one of An ceathramh rèisimeid's hired hulls is separated from the rest, puts into a cove on the far side of the north cape, and loses two days finding the others again, reaching Ceann mhòr three days behind the rest with crew and cargo whole.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5023"><em>The hired hulls put out from Ros chiar</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5025"><em>The maor of Ceann mhòr gives up his house</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5025"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The maor of Ceann mhòr gives up his house* (Ceann mhòr). The maor of Ceann mhòr gives up the greater part of the old human magistrate's house to An ceathramh rèisimeid without complaint, moving his own household into its two upper rooms, and takes afterwards to walking their narrow gallery of an evening remarking to whichever officer passes below that the army has undone in a fortnight what forty winters of sea air had not.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5024"><em>One hull parts company off the north cape</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5026"><em>The maor's clerk keeps the two tongues apart</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5026"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The maor's clerk keeps the two tongues apart* (Ceann mhòr). The maor of Ceann mhòr's clerk, a Tuathaich woman of long service, addresses An ceathramh rèisimeid's captain in Dia-thìris without a stumble and her own townsfolk, on the office's business, in the humans' tongue alone, the two tongues kept, in her own ordering of things, for two entirely different kinds of transaction.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5025"><em>The maor of Ceann mhòr gives up his house</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5027"><em>Martha Greaves's letter reaches the magistrate's house</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5027"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Martha Greaves's letter reaches the magistrate's house* (Ceann mhòr). Martha Greaves's single sheet asking that An ceathramh rèisimeid be lodged at its own charge and not the town's is carried up the coast road and read aloud by the fourth's own captain to his assembled company. It is received and forwarded; Comhairle nam Mèinnean's late reply says only that the arrangement stands until the campaign's needs change it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5026"><em>The maor's clerk keeps the two tongues apart</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5028"><em>The Cathair gheal petition folded into a barrel of cod</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5028"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The Cathair gheal petition folded into a barrel of cod* (Cathair gheal). The fishermen of Cathair gheal draw up their petition on the quay before the boats go out, setting down only the days the searching has run and the hours a boat is commonly held, and send it to Caol mhòr folded inside a barrel of salt cod consigned, quite genuinely, to Tional nan Tuathach's own stores.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0105"><em>The fishermen of Cathair gheal</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5027"><em>Martha Greaves's letter reaches the magistrate's house</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5029"><em>Dùghall hears the petition told as a soldier's tale</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5029"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Dùghall hears the petition told as a soldier's tale* (Ceann mhòr). A corporal of An dàrna cabhlach, billeted a night at Ceann mhòr, tells Dùghall mac Iain the tale of the fish-barrel petition over their shared supper as dry entertainment and nothing graver, a story a searching soldier keeps by him for its comedy rather than its weight.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0105"><em>The fishermen of Cathair gheal</em>, 15 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5028"><em>The Cathair gheal petition folded into a barrel of cod</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5030"><em>Dùghall billeted on Barbara Keir of Ceann mhòr</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5030"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Dùghall billeted on Barbara Keir of Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). Once the magistrate's house is full past stretching, the maor's clerk billets Corporal Dùghall mac Iain on a widow of the town named Barbara Keir, who keeps a loom in the room behind her kitchen; she opens her door to him with no more welcome than the clerk's own list had shown in its writing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5029"><em>Dùghall hears the petition told as a soldier's tale</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5031"><em>The tongue Barbara Keir will not give him</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5031"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The tongue Barbara Keir will not give him* (Ceann mhòr). Barbara answers Corporal Dùghall mac Iain readily in Dia-thìris on the house's own business, but gives him, try as he may, not one word of the humans' tongue, though he hears her speak it easily across the yard wall to a neighbour; he comes to understand it a door shut on him alone.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5030"><em>Dùghall billeted on Barbara Keir of Ceann mhòr</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5032"><em>The barges of the Abhainn ghorm</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5032"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The barges of the Abhainn ghorm* (Caol bheag). An ceathramh rèisimeid goes down the Abhainn ghorm from Caol bheag to Ros chiar in old coal barges fitted with plank benches, the river high with rain, in a day and a half.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5031"><em>The tongue Barbara Keir will not give him</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5033"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach on the quartering</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5033"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach on the quartering* (Ceann mhòr).
