Near the year's end Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach's protest against the quartering at Ceann mhòr that the arrangement stands until the campaign's needs change it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0104"><em>The regiments at Ceann mhòr</em>, 10 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5032"><em>The barges of the Abhainn ghorm</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5034"><em>An siathamh rèisimeid drills by the carved stone</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5034"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *An siathamh rèisimeid drills by the carved stone* (Cnoc bheag). An siathamh rèisimeid, raised at Cnoc bheag, drills in the square beside the carved stone, and the town's children learn the words of command before the recruits do.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0101"><em>An siathamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 17 an Dàmhair, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5033"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers Tional nan Tuathach on the quartering</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5035"><em>Baile ghorm's quays given to An treas cabhlach</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5035"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Baile ghorm's quays given to An treas cabhlach* (Baile ghorm). At its raising An treas cabhlach takes the wolf-post quays of Baile ghorm for its own; the fishing boats are moved to the old beach and their pump with them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0107"><em>An treas cabhlach raised</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5034"><em>An siathamh rèisimeid drills by the carved stone</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5036"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *An treas cabhlach's first tank-hull reaches Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). A week after its raising at Baile ghorm An treas cabhlach's first tank-hull, her number chalked on her bow for want of a name, comes into Ceann mhòr with the army's dubhan. Her master, Griogair, a fisherman of Baile ghorm forty years, talks with Corporal Dùghall mac Iain on the quay through the unloading.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0107"><em>An treas cabhlach raised</em>, 1 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5037"><em>Dùghall billeted on Barbara</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5037"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Dùghall billeted on Barbara* (Ceann mhòr). At Ceann mhòr Dùghall mac Iain is billeted on a Tuathaich widow named Barbara, who feeds him at her own table and answers him only in Dia-thìris, though he hears her, of an evening, singing at her loom in the humans' tongue she will not use to speak to him directly.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0103"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid raised</em>, 2 an t-Samhain, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5036"><em>An treas cabhlach's first tank-hull reaches Ceann mhòr</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5038"><em>A file sent north to Baile chrom</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5038"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *A file sent north to Baile chrom* (Ceann mhòr). An ceathramh rèisimeid sends Corporal Dùghall mac Iain and six men on the two days' coast road to Baile chrom, a bent headland town no patrol of the regiment has yet troubled to search, with orders to look for arms and for men of the western hills and to bring back a report.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5037"><em>Dùghall billeted on Barbara</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5039"><em>The watched mill on the coast road</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5039"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The watched mill on the coast road*. On the march north the file passes a mill and two farms whose people watch them from their doorways and say nothing, a silence the soldier Cailean judges more telling, in its own way, than any shout a Dia-thìreach farm on the same road would have raised.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5038"><em>A file sent north to Baile chrom</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5040"><em>The town found dark and silent</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5040"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The town found dark and silent* (Baile chrom). Dùghall mac Iain's file comes into Baile chrom after dark on the eve of Oidhche Glaise to find no lamp lit, no dog loosed and every door unlatched; house after house holds a family sitting hands folded round a cold hearth, answering nothing but a single slow headshake.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5039"><em>The watched mill on the coast road</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5041"><em>Margaret Crane keeps the vigil alone</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5041"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Margaret Crane keeps the vigil alone* (Baile chrom). In the house nearest the lighthouse road an old woman named Margaret Crane sits alone keeping Oidhche Glaise as she has kept it since before the war, gives Dùghall mac Iain her name and leave to search, and tells him nothing more; a soldier of his own file sets his lamp down outside her door rather than carry its light past her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5040"><em>The town found dark and silent</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5042"><em>The regimental clerk's question</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5042"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The regimental clerk's question*. Copying Dùghall mac Iain's report fair at the bothy, the file's young clerk asks whether there is more to the night than its three written lines; Dùghall tells him there is not, and keeps the headshakes and the cold hearths out of the regiment's own returns.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5041"><em>Margaret Crane keeps the vigil alone</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5043"><em>Barbara on the flooded pits</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5043"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Barbara on the flooded pits* (Ceann mhòr). Dùghall mac Iain mentions the flooding of Àth naomh's pits to Barbara over her evening table; she answers only, in Dia-thìris, that a pit flooded is a pit flooded whichever order floods it, and takes up her mending again in the silence he has learned by then not to press.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0109"><em>Àth naomh and Tobar dhearg</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5042"><em>The regimental clerk's question</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5044"><em>Dùghall's sleepless winter</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5044"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Dùghall's sleepless winter* (Ceann mhòr). Through the short days that follow, Dùghall mac Iain wakes most nights with the sea-sound of the Baile chrom headland in his ears, unable in either tongue he carries to find words for a stillness that asked nothing of him and gave him nothing to answer with.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5043"><em>Barbara on the flooded pits</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5045"><em>The file sent round by the headland farms</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5045"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The file sent round by the headland farms* (Baile chrom). Corporal Dùghall mac Iain's file of six is sent to Baile chrom by way of the headland farms, sleeping a night in an empty drover's bothy on the way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5044"><em>Dùghall's sleepless winter</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5046"><em>Cailean says the house searched him back</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5046"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *Cailean says the house searched him back* (Baile chrom). Marching back from Baile chrom, a soldier named Cailean says he has never come away from a search feeling the house had searched him back, and would not go north again.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0108"><em>The Baile chrom vigil</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5045"><em>The file sent round by the headland farms</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5047"><em>The ninth's raising read at Ceann mhòr</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5047"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *The ninth's raising read at Ceann mhòr* (Ceann mhòr). Two days after an Nollaig the raising of An naoidheamh rèisimeid at the southern Seann Skell is read out in An ceathramh rèisimeid's guardroom at Ceann mhòr.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5046"><em>Cailean says the house searched him back</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0110"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21** — *An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised* (Seann Skell). The ninth regiment is raised at Seann Skell on the southern coast, the second town of that name in the regimental list, to guard the dubhan works the shipmasters built there. The regimental clerks tell the two apart by river and coast.<span class="fn fl">→ Caused by <a href="#ev-EVII-5047"><em>The ninth's raising read at Ceann mhòr</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0111"></a>**29 an Dàmhair, DE 22** — *The column goes south* (Muileann mhin). A column of holdouts, some hundreds strong, leaves the western hills and marches south-east through the middle of the island toward the capital. Why it did so is in the sealed archive. The Tuathaich tellings name its leader Owen Barrow. The open record gives no name.
- <a id="ev-VI-0112"></a>**24 an t-Samhain, DE 22** — *The column's road* (Àth bheag). The column's road south-east runs by Àth bheag in the west, Muileann mhin and the edge of the capital's country. The towns it passes report it, and the open record copies their reports and not the regiments'.
- <a id="ev-VI-0113"></a>**6 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The camp by Muileann ghlas* (Muileann ghlas). The column passes Muileann òg and camps on the fields by Muileann ghlas, a day's walk from Cathair dhearg. The first and third regiments are brought down the fair road to meet it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0114"></a>**9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The fair-ground emptied* (Fèill Muileann òg). The fair-ground at Muileann òg is cleared of its standing booths to give the first and third regiments room to camp. The books of its court for that year end with no closing entry.
- <a id="ev-VI-0115"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Battle of Muileann ghlas* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The second great battle of the war, and the last. In two summers of fighting the Tuathaich holdouts are broken: children of the humans once driven to the island's edge, driven back again, and this time by a fuel that one of their own devised.
- <a id="ev-VI-0116"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The field at Muileann ghlas* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The open record lists the first and third regiments on the field at Muileann ghlas and gives no count of the column's dead. The regiments' own dead are named on a stone at Cathair mhòr, set up the next year.
- <a id="ev-VI-0117"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The last pits give up* (Àraich Àth leathan). Word of Muileann ghlas reaches the hills, and the holdouts still there come down to the posts of the seventh regiment on the Àth leathan road. They are disarmed and sent home. The open record counts their weapons.
- <a id="ev-VI-0118"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *An Cogadh Fada ends*. The Long War ends. Nine regiments and four fleets were raised in it, each named for the town where it is stationed, and all of them stand to this day.
- <a id="ev-VI-0119"></a>**10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Fadachadh* (Caol mhòr). Among Tuathaich speakers 'chaidh am fadachadh', they got long-warred, begins to be said of the defeat in the west, and then of any defeat after holding out too long. It is said as a jest, and those who say it do not laugh.
- <a id="ev-EVII-5501"></a>**11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The pass at the Caol mhòr steps* (Caol mhòr). Comhairle nam Mèinnean's office begins issuing a small paper against a name, a face and a stated errand for anyone at Caol mhòr who means to leave the harbour road; the town takes to calling it simply the pass, and Martha Greaves comes to show her own to the same soldier three times that spring on Moot business.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5502"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Joe Ashby's boats searched again* (Caol mhòr). A patrol captain boards every hull at Caol mhòr's harbour wall in the last week of an Cèitean, the engine-boats last and most carefully; Joe Ashby, watching from his shed door, tells him plainly that no guild in the harbour would give him leave to fit them, and the captain writes it down without comment.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5501"><em>The pass at the Caol mhòr steps</em>, 11 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5503"></a>**13 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Joe Ashby fits a fleet hull again* (Caol mhòr). Before the summer is out the depot's own men send for Joe Ashby a second time, for a hull no guild-trained fitter at Seann Skell could put right; he mends it, takes his coin at the harbour's own rate, and asks no more of the matter than the coin requires.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5502"><em>Joe Ashby's boats searched again</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5504"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Tional nan Tuathach's register adds the names of Àth leathan* (Caol mhòr). Peter Hale brings Martha Greaves a list gathered from the western towns under the disarming; she enters the dead and maimed of Àth leathan into Tional nan Tuathach's register column by column, and finds Ruth Calder's own name on none of its three columns.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5503"><em>Joe Ashby fits a fleet hull again</em>, 13 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5505"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Easter kept under watch* (Doire ghlas). Martha Greaves stands at the back of Eaglais nan Tuathach's own Easter service at the chapel above Doire ghlas and finds a single soldier of the regiments posted at the door the whole length of it, writing nothing in his book, the service passing between door and altar without a word exchanged.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5504"><em>Tional nan Tuathach's register adds the names of Àth leathan</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5506"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Ellen Marsh takes down the Cnoc thais women* (Doire ghlas). In the schoolroom given over the autumn before, Ellen Marsh takes down the accounts of the women of Cnoc thais bench by bench for her twelfth book, among them Peggy Innes's telling of a farm that bakes a second loaf every night and leaves it on the sill for a coming and going the disarming never ended.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5505"><em>Easter kept under watch</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5507"></a>**17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A hill farm burned above Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). A patrol of the regiments finds a farm above Cnoc thais with a barn half full of grain no ration book can account for and burns the house and byre, turning the family into their own yard first; no one is killed, and Ellen Marsh sets the telling down in the same flat voice the women themselves use for it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5506"><em>Ellen Marsh takes down the Cnoc thais women</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5508"></a>**18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Ellen Marsh finishes her twelfth book* (Doire ghlas). In the first week of an Dàmhair Ellen Marsh closes the twelfth of her books of Tuathaich accounts, the one that gathers the war her first eleven never spoke of, and writes on its last leaf that she does not know which of her twelve a reader two generations off will find the harder to believe.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5507"><em>A hill farm burned above Cnoc thais</em>, 17 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5509"></a>**19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *An ceathramh rèisimeid's year of patrols on the Ceann mhòr road* (Ceann mhòr). Through the whole quartered year An ceathramh rèisimeid keeps its patrols on the Ceann mhòr road, a file out at first light and in at dusk; no arms and no unaccounted man are found, and the regiment's returns settle into the same three words that closed every report of the autumn before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5508"><em>Ellen Marsh finishes her twelfth book</em>, 18 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5510"></a>**20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Dùghall hears the hymn through the wall* (Ceann mhòr). Of an evening in an t-Sultain, Dùghall mac Iain hears through the wall of Barbara's house a hymn sung low in the humans' tongue, heavier than her shuttle-song of the autumn before; by an Dàmhair he can carry its whole shape in his head without meaning to have learned it, and catches himself humming it on the road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5509"><em>An ceathramh rèisimeid's year of patrols on the Ceann mhòr road</em>, 19 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5511"></a>**21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Cailean's own grandmother's tune* (Ceann mhòr). Dùghall mac Iain hums two bars of the learned hymn to the soldier Cailean over a cold supper; Cailean says his own grandmother kept a tune very like it, that he never asked its words either, and that a man billeted long enough on a house not his own generally carries some piece of it home in him.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5510"><em>Dùghall hears the hymn through the wall</em>, 20 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5512"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A rumour that will not run to ground*. Across the quartered year a single rumour passes from the Cnoc thais hill paths to the Doire ghlas schoolroom to the Ceann mhòr road, that something gathers in the western hills the disarming never reached; no regiment's patrol and no clerk's report ever explains it, and it never twice is told the same way.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5511"><em>Cailean's own grandmother's tune</em>, 21 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5513"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Word reaches Caol mhòr that the hills are moving* (Caol mhòr). In the last week of an Dàmhair a Board carrier rides two days without pausing to bring Caol mhòr word that some hundreds have come down out of the western hills and turned south-east across the middle of the island; Martha Greaves reads the note beside her register's own closed column on the names of Àth leathan.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0110"><em>An naoidheamh rèisimeid raised</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 21</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5512"><em>A rumour that will not run to ground</em>, 22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5514"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A burial walked to on a pass* (Caol mhòr). A carter of Caol mhòr shows his pass at the harbour steps in his mourning black to walk to his father's burial two roads inland, the office having made no separate provision for burials.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5513"><em>Word reaches Caol mhòr that the hills are moving</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5515"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A byre-boy's raised hand* (Ceann mhòr). On the Ceann mhòr road a boy of ten driving three cows begins, in the second season of the patrols, to lift a hand to An ceathramh rèisimeid's file as it passes.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5514"><em>A burial walked to on a pass</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5516"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Bread left on a sill above Cnoc thais* (Cnoc thais). A farm two ridges back from ruined Cnoc thais bakes twice what its household can eat and leaves the second baking on the sill overnight; the loaves are gone by morning and the sill is never watched.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5515"><em>A byre-boy's raised hand</em>, 25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5517"></a>**27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Goods carried out before the thatch was fired* (Cnoc thais). Marion Kenny tells Ellen Marsh that the family of the burned farm above Cnoc thais were given time by the patrol to carry out a chest, a loom and the year's meal before the thatch was fired.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5516"><em>Bread left on a sill above Cnoc thais</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5518"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean counts night traffic on the hill paths* (Cnoc thais). A clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean stationed at Cnoc thais writes to Tional nan Tuathach that the hill paths above the town carry more foot-traffic by night than any patrol's daylight count can explain.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5517"><em>Goods carried out before the thatch was fired</em>, 27 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5519"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The passes printed at Cathair dhearg* (Cathair dhearg). The passes of the northern office are printed at Cathair dhearg on grey card, ten thousand at a time, with a space for a name and none for a trade.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5518"><em>A clerk of Comhairle nam Mèinnean counts night traffic on the hill paths</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5520"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A pass-office at Cnoc ghorm* (Cnoc ghorm). The northern office sets a clerk with his grey passes in the old wool-hall at Cnoc ghorm; the Tuathaich come to him one household at a time, and the elders have their own names written first.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0119"><em>Fadachadh</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5519"><em>The passes printed at Cathair dhearg</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5521"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The regiments' lorries at Muileann fhada* (Muileann fhada). The regiments' lorries on the north road take on fuel at a pump set up in the yard of An Taigh-seinnse Reòta above Muileann fhada, the landlord renting the yard to Comhairle nam Mèinnean and keeping his wicks inside.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5520"><em>A pass-office at Cnoc ghorm</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5522"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Àth bheag's report of the ford* (Àth bheag). The maor of Àth bheag writes the fullest report of the column's road: some four hundred men forded the water below the bridge at dawn, in order, without banner or drum, and went on south without stopping.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5523"><em>Sìleas nic Rath keeps a file of the column's road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5523"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Sìleas nic Rath keeps a file of the column's road*. Seanchaidh na Rìoghachd asks every town on the column's line for its account and is given leave to keep them, a freedom the war itself never allowed her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5522"><em>Àth bheag's report of the ford</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5524"><em>Bread bought and paid for at Muileann mhin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5524"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Bread bought and paid for at Muileann mhin* (Muileann mhin). Two men of the column buy the widow Mòrag nic Fhearghais's whole morning's baking at Muileann mhin and pay in full before the company passes, taking nothing else from the town.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5523"><em>Sìleas nic Rath keeps a file of the column's road</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5525"><em>Muileann mhin's miller reports no loss</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5525"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Muileann mhin's miller reports no loss* (Muileann mhin). The miller of Muileann mhin under the western hills writes to Comhairle nam Mèinnean that the town's takings showed no loss by the column's passing, the bread having been paid for at a fair price and nobody's stock troubled beyond it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5524"><em>Bread bought and paid for at Muileann mhin</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5526"><em>A night's lodging paid at a barn on the capital's edge</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5526"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A night's lodging paid at a barn on the capital's edge*. A party of the column sleeps a night in Aonghas mac Cuinn's barn and leaves coin and a note under a stone, thanking him and asking nothing more.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5525"><em>Muileann mhin's miller reports no loss</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5527"><em>The column keeps wide of the towns of the fair country</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5527"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The column keeps wide of the towns of the fair country*. Crossing the open country toward the capital's fields, the column holds a road that passes no town of any size, and the small farms it crosses report only a quiet passing.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5526"><em>A night's lodging paid at a barn on the capital's edge</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5528"><em>The fair-ground at Muileann òg ordered for the regiments</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5528"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The fair-ground at Muileann òg ordered for the regiments* (Muileann òg). A' chiad rèisimeid's quartermaster requires the fair-ground, its booths and its cleared ground for the first and third regiments, over Cùirt na Fèille's own market set for the ninth.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5527"><em>The column keeps wide of the towns of the fair country</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5529"><em>Fionnlagh Dubh numbers his stall's timbers</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5529"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Fionnlagh Dubh numbers his stall's timbers* (Muileann òg). An ironmonger of thirty years' standing at Muileann òg's fair chalks numbers on his stall's poles before stacking them, against a spring market neither he nor the clerk much believes will come.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5528"><em>The fair-ground at Muileann òg ordered for the regiments</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5530"><em>An treas rèisimeid camps on the cleared fair-ground</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5530"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *An treas rèisimeid camps on the cleared fair-ground* (Muileann òg). An treas rèisimeid pitches its tents where the ironmonger's stall and the cheese-sellers' row stood the day before, the ground cleared from the toll-house arch to the river bend.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0113"><em>The camp by Muileann ghlas</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5529"><em>Fionnlagh Dubh numbers his stall's timbers</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5531"><em>A' chiad rèisimeid fills Muileann òg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5531"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A' chiad rèisimeid fills Muileann òg* (Muileann òg). A' chiad rèisimeid comes down the same evening as the third and fills the fair-ground, the water-meadow and the lanes above the mill, so that Muileann òg holds more soldiers under canvas than people.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0113"><em>The camp by Muileann ghlas</em>, 6 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5530"><em>An treas rèisimeid camps on the cleared fair-ground</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5532"><em>Cùirt na Fèille keeps its small business through the camp</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5532"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Cùirt na Fèille keeps its small business through the camp* (Muileann òg). Ùna nic Ailein keeps Cùirt na Fèille open through the regiments' camp, hearing a strayed cow and a firewood complaint while the road to Muileann ghlas fills and empties below her window.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5531"><em>A' chiad rèisimeid fills Muileann òg</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5533"><em>Ùna nic Ailein's book closes with no entry</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5533"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Ùna nic Ailein's book closes with no entry* (Muileann òg). Unable to set a sum against a market that never ran, Ùna rules the line the court's form requires, leaves it blank, and closes the year the desk with no closing entry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5532"><em>Cùirt na Fèille keeps its small business through the camp</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5534"><em>The maor of Àth bheag watches from the bank</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5534"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The maor of Àth bheag watches from the bank* (Àth bheag). Cailean mac Griogair, maor of Àth bheag, woken by the smith's boy, stands at the field's edge in a borrowed coat watching the column ford the water and does not go down to ask where it is bound.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0111"><em>The column goes south</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5533"><em>Ùna nic Ailein's book closes with no entry</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5535"><em>No banner and no drum</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5535"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *No banner and no drum* (Àth bheag). The miller's wife of Àth bheag, watching the column cross from the mill loft, says she saw no banner among them and no drum, only a man at the head whom the rest left the whole width of the road.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0111"><em>The column goes south</em>, 29 an Dàmhair, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5534"><em>The maor of Àth bheag watches from the bank</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5536"><em>The note under the stone</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5536"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The note under the stone*. Aonghas mac Cuinn finds under a stone on his barn floor coin for a week's rent and a note in Dia-thìris: for the barn, and thanks; we have asked nothing else. It is the only writing in an Leabharlann's file that can be set to a hand inside the column.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0112"><em>The column's road</em>, 24 an t-Samhain, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5535"><em>No banner and no drum</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5537"><em>The eel-woman's tub carried off the fair-ground</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5537"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The eel-woman's tub carried off the fair-ground* (Muileann òg). Clearing the fair-ground at Muileann òg for the regiments, two soldiers lift the heavier end of the eel-woman's tub onto her handcart for her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5536"><em>The note under the stone</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5538"><em>Caol ruadh's boats carry the regiments' bread</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5538"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Caol ruadh's boats carry the regiments' bread* (Caol ruadh). The boats of the red strait at Caol ruadh are hired to carry the regiments' bread along the coast in the autumn, paid by the day, with a soldier aboard each to count the loaves.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0114"><em>The fair-ground emptied</em>, 9 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5537"><em>The eel-woman's tub carried off the fair-ground</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5539"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The column sings through its last night in the open* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). On the bank and in the thorn below Muileann ghlas the column keeps its last night before the battle by singing low, company after company, in part for what courage it lends and in part because there are children on the field with nowhere else on the island to be left.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5540"><em>Owen Barrow walks the line before first light</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5540"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Owen Barrow walks the line before first light* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). In the last hour of dark Owen Barrow goes the length of the column's line, speaking to each company and to many of the column by name; he is remembered in the north to have said that the hills lie behind them now and cannot be walked back to before the guns find them either way. An Clàr Foscailte names him nowhere.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5539"><em>The column sings through its last night in the open</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5541"><em>The guns find the thorn stand</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5541"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The guns find the thorn stand* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). An treas rèisimeid's four field pieces, hauled the last two miles by hand through ground too soft for the horses, find the column's thorn-stand line within the first half-hour of the fighting; what holds after that holds along the bank itself, hand to hand, through most of the short forenoon.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5540"><em>Owen Barrow walks the line before first light</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5542"><em>The corporal's list at the mill</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5542"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The corporal's list at the mill* (Muileann ghlas). A corporal of An treas rèisimeid draws up the regiments' dead of the day at a trestle table in the mill at Muileann ghlas, the miller's own ledger turned backward for want of other paper: three-and-twenty names, each with a town and, where known, an age.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0116"><em>The field at Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5541"><em>The guns find the thorn stand</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5543"><em>A requisition for lime</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5543"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *A requisition for lime* (Muileann ghlas). The regiments' burial parties ask the quartermaster for a good deal more lime than three-and-twenty graves would need. The requisition survives where no count of the column's own dead does, and is the nearest thing An Clàr Foscailte holds to one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0116"><em>The field at Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5542"><em>The corporal's list at the mill</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5544"><em>The miller's wife keeps her kitchen through the battle</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5544"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The miller's wife keeps her kitchen through the battle* (Muileann ghlas). As the mill at Muileann ghlas changes hands twice before noon, the miller's wife will not leave her own kitchen for either army, and is remembered by the regiments' surgeon to have gone on moving her pots and sacks from whichever corner the fighting had just left.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5543"><em>A requisition for lime</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5545"><em>The colonel's report</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5545"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The colonel's report* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). A' chiad rèisimeid's colonel writes that the column held the bank at Muileann ghlas longer than any force he had faced in two years of war, and sets it down, he says, only so his council should have the field's truth and not a prettier account of it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0116"><em>The field at Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5544"><em>The miller's wife keeps her kitchen through the battle</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5546"><em>The taken ground remembered</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5546"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The taken ground remembered* (Muileann ghlas). An old man of Muileann ghlas, brought before the regiments' officers to answer for a store of grain, tells them the field carries an older name, the taken ground, from a battle of Cogadh nam Bràithrean fought on the same ground two centuries before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5545"><em>The colonel's report</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5547"><em>The sixty come out of the byres</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5547"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The sixty come out of the byres* (Muileann ghlas). After dark, some sixty of the column still holding the mill and its byres come out under a promise, carried by a Tuathach prisoner on a white cloth, that any man unarmed will be marched and not shot; they are counted, searched and held overnight on the mill floor.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5546"><em>The taken ground remembered</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5548"><em>The regiments' surgeon treats both sides alike</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5548"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The regiments' surgeon treats both sides alike* (Muileann ghlas). The regiments' own surgeon, two years out of his training, tends the wounded of both the regiments and the column through the night at Muileann ghlas by two lanterns and a banked fire, and An Clàr Foscailte notes that he made no distinction between them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0115"><em>Battle of Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5547"><em>The sixty come out of the byres</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5549"><em>The old man of Cnoc thais brings down his cow</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5549"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The old man of Cnoc thais brings down his cow* (Cnoc thais). A lame old man of Cnoc thais comes down to An seachdamh rèisimeid's northernmost post on the Àth leathan road carrying no weapon, leading on a rope halter the one cow his family kept through two summers of war, and is let through with it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0117"><em>The last pits give up</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5548"><em>The regiments' surgeon treats both sides alike</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5550"><em>The sergeant judges the counting done</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5550"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *The sergeant judges the counting done* (Àth leathan). At An seachdamh rèisimeid's northernmost post the sergeant keeping the list of the hills' people notes, when no one more has come down the road by noon, that he takes the empty road to mean the counting is finished.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0117"><em>The last pits give up</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5549"><em>The old man of Cnoc thais brings down his cow</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5551"><em>Somhairle hears the guns are done</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5551"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Somhairle hears the guns are done* (Cathair dhearg). Somhairle mac Lachlainn hears at the capital, from a clerk who comes into his room without knocking, that the fighting at Muileann ghlas is over; he says afterward that his first thought was for Slighe a' Ghuail's timetable and the wounded's carriage north.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0118"><em>An Cogadh Fada ends</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5550"><em>The sergeant judges the counting done</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5552"><em>Somhairle checks the wounded trains twice over</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5552"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Somhairle checks the wounded trains twice over* (Cathair dhearg). In the first weeks of the peace Somhairle mac Lachlainn has Slighe a' Ghuail's schedule for the war's wounded checked twice against the surgeons' own returns, to be sure no man carried north that winter rode on a train meant for other cargo.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0118"><em>An Cogadh Fada ends</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5551"><em>Somhairle hears the guns are done</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5553"><em>Near ninety of the column's wounded brought in</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5553"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Near ninety of the column's wounded brought in* (Muileann ghlas). The regiments' surgeon's tally for the night after Muileann ghlas stands at twenty-three of the regiments buried or dying and near ninety of the column's wounded brought in.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0116"><em>The field at Muileann ghlas</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5552"><em>Somhairle checks the wounded trains twice over</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-5554"><em>Taigh-solais Àth dhearg sees no fleet</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-5554"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22** — *Taigh-solais Àth dhearg sees no fleet* (Àth dhearg). The keeper of Taigh-solais Àth dhearg on the north-east cape writes in his log through the autumn that no ship of the fleets has passed the cape in three months.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-5553"><em>Near ninety of the column's wounded brought in</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0120"></a>**13 am Faoilleach, DE 23** — *The regiments stay on their stations* (Cathair dhearg). The nine regiments and four fleets are not stood down. The council keeps each at the town where it was raised and pays them from the wartime tithe.
- <a id="ev-VI-0120a"></a>**26 am Faoilleach, DE 23** — *The market charter of Caol ruadh* (Caol ruadh). Caol ruadh, whose harbour victualled the garrisons and the second fleet through the war, is granted a market right for the southern strait. It is the sixteenth market town, and the last chartered.
- <a id="ev-VI-0121"></a>**11 an Gearran, DE 23** — *Dubhan's fuel over all the island*. With the last ordered resistance gone, Dubhan's fuel is in all but law compelled upon the whole trade of the island.
- <a id="ev-VI-0122"></a>**24 an Gearran, DE 23** — *The western seams flooded* (Àth leathan). By the Board's order the last western seams are flooded and their shafts capped with concrete. The seventh regiment stands by at every capping. After this no coal is dug on the island outside the Board's own works.
- <a id="ev-VI-0123"></a>**4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23** — *The prisoners sent home* (Caol mhòr). The holdouts held since Muileann ghlas are let out of the capital's gaol and sent north under guard of the first regiment as far as the boundary stones. The Moot's register adds their names, in a column of their own, to the dead and maimed it has kept since the Severance.
- <a id="ev-VI-0124"></a>**31 an Lùnastal, DE 23** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn seated* (Cathair dhearg). Somhairle mac Lachlainn is given a seat on the council, the first soldier to sit there since the captains of the Severance war.
- <a id="ev-VI-0125"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, DE 23** — *The seventh regiment at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). The seventh regiment builds a post on the road below Àth leathan and keeps a company there. In the regimental lists it is called the Àth leathan post, and in the town something else.
- <a id="ev-VI-0126"></a>**15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The stone at Cathair mhòr* (Cathair mhòr). A stone is set up at Cathair mhòr bearing the names of the regiments' dead from Àth leathan and Muileann ghlas. It stands beside the market cross of the house of Mac Ùisdein.
- <a id="ev-VI-0127"></a>**28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The Muileann ghlas field* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). The field at Muileann ghlas where the column camped is sown again. For years the farmer who holds it finds weapons in the furrows and hands them to the first regiment, which keeps a list.
- <a id="ev-EVII-6001"></a>**29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The first capping at Àth leathan* (Àth leathan). In am Màrt An seachdamh rèisimeid pours the first concrete over a flooded shaft at Àth leathan while Somhairle mac Lachlainn watches from the pit-head; the mix lies still in a way the seam itself, even flooded, had never once lain before.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0122"><em>The western seams flooded</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6002"></a>**30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Sergeant Iain Mòr counts the cappings* (Muileann àrsaidh). A sergeant of An seachdamh rèisimeid tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn this is the fourth capping his company has stood by that month, at Muileann àrsaidh, Cnoc thais and a nameless working near Àth naomh, and wonders aloud what the regiment will be set to guard once Tobar dhearg of the hills is done.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0122"><em>The western seams flooded</em>, 24 an Gearran, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6001"><em>The first capping at Àth leathan</em>, 29 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6003"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Comhairle nam Mèinnean ends the coal trade outside An Sloc Mòr* (Cathair mhòr). Fearghas mac Aonghais's office notes that the trade in coal-fuel is at an end on the island outside what Comhairle nam Mèinnean still cuts for its own account at An Sloc Mòr: not forbidden by any law, but ended by there being, at last, nowhere left to sell it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0121"><em>Dubhan's fuel over all the island</em>, 11 an Gearran, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6002"><em>Sergeant Iain Mòr counts the cappings</em>, 30 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6004"><em>Aonghas mac Phàdraig's plough finds the first iron</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6004"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Aonghas mac Phàdraig's plough finds the first iron* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). Turning his field at Muileann ghlas in am Màrt as he has every spring of his life, Aonghas mac Phàdraig's share brings up a rusted bayonet lying whole across it; he finishes the furrow before he carries it home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0127"><em>The Muileann ghlas field</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6003"><em>Comhairle nam Mèinnean ends the coal trade outside An Sloc Mòr</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6005"><em>A' chiad rèisimeid's corporal begins a list</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6005"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *A' chiad rèisimeid's corporal begins a list* (Àraich Muileann ghlas). A corporal of A' chiad rèisimeid collecting rents in the district takes Aonghas mac Phàdraig's bayonet and enters it on a list kept for such finds, not knowing whether it is a record of the dead or only of the field giving back what two armies left in it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0127"><em>The Muileann ghlas field</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6004"><em>Aonghas mac Phàdraig's plough finds the first iron</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6006"><em>The letter from the capital's gaol</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6006"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The letter from the capital's gaol* (Ceann mhòr). Martha Greaves receives word from the council's office that the holdouts taken at Muileann ghlas are to be released in an t-Iuchar and marched north to the boundary stones, with no word of who is to feed them on the road or what their flooded towns will make of their return.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6005"><em>A' chiad rèisimeid's corporal begins a list</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6007"><em>Martha Greaves and Peter Hale ride to the stones</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6007"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Martha Greaves and Peter Hale ride to the stones* (Caol mhòr). Martha Greaves and Peter Hale take the last carriage Slighe a' Ghuail runs toward the boundary stones, Peter carrying a register freshly ruled with a new column by his own hand for want of any other paper the party trusted.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6006"><em>The letter from the capital's gaol</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6008"><em>A mother writes four words beside her son's name</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6008"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *A mother writes four words beside her son's name* (Caol mhòr). A woman of Cnoc thais gives Martha Greaves her son's name for the register and, unbidden, the words he is not among these; Martha sets both down, judging the register poorer without them.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6007"><em>Martha Greaves and Peter Hale ride to the stones</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6009"><em>A man refuses his name for a town that no longer stands</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6009"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *A man refuses his name for a town that no longer stands* (Caol mhòr). An older prisoner at the boundary stones will not give his name at first, saying it would mean nothing written beside Muileann àrsaidh's ruin; Martha Greaves promises the town will stand again in whatever shape its people build it, and he gives his name.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6008"><em>A mother writes four words beside her son's name</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6010"><em>Peter Hale keeps a name of his own</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6010"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Peter Hale keeps a name of his own* (Caol mhòr). Among the released Peter Hale recognises a man once apprenticed to the same binder at Muileann leathan whose pupils rebound Tional nan Tuathach's minute-books; the man gives no sign of knowing him, and Peter does not ask which it is, silence or forgetting.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6009"><em>A man refuses his name for a town that no longer stands</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6011"><em>Anna nic Phàil speaks to Somhairle at the chamber door</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6011"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Anna nic Phàil speaks to Somhairle at the chamber door* (Cathair dhearg). At the close of his first sitting Anna nic Phàil tells Somhairle mac Lachlainn she stood on the bench in the passage an Nollaig Martha Greaves carried Athchuinge Dheireannach an Tionail in, and means to go on voting every mercy the council's business allows her.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0124"><em>Somhairle mac Lachlainn seated</em>, 31 an Lùnastal, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6010"><em>Peter Hale keeps a name of his own</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6012"><em>Somhairle reads the one-and-sixty names</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6012"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Somhairle reads the one-and-sixty names* (Cathair mhòr). At the stone's unveiling at Cathair mhòr, Somhairle mac Lachlainn reads aloud the one-and-sixty names of the regiments' dead from Àth leathan and Muileann ghlas to a silent square, and finds the town's silence harder to bear than any noise it might have made instead.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0126"><em>The stone at Cathair mhòr</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6011"><em>Anna nic Phàil speaks to Somhairle at the chamber door</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6013"><em>Somhairle thinks of the names the stone does not carry</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6013"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Somhairle thinks of the names the stone does not carry* (Cathair mhòr). Standing alone at the stone after the crowd disperses, Somhairle mac Lachlainn counts over the column's uncounted dead, the sixty from the byres, and a mother's son who was not among the released, and finds that number, cut nowhere, stays with him longer than the one that is.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0126"><em>The stone at Cathair mhòr</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6012"><em>Somhairle reads the one-and-sixty names</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6014"><em>Four score released at the boundary stones</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6014"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Four score released at the boundary stones* (Caol mhòr). Some four score holdouts taken at Muileann ghlas are handed to Tional nan Tuathach at the boundary stones; Martha Greaves writes their names in a column Peter Hale ruled that morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0123"><em>The prisoners sent home</em>, 4 an t-Iuchar, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6013"><em>Somhairle thinks of the names the stone does not carry</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6015"><em>The heading on Clach nan Rèisimeidean</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6015"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The heading on Clach nan Rèisimeidean* (Cathair mhòr). Clach nan Rèisimeidean is cut in two columns under a single heading, the regiments' dead, giving neither battle nor date.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0126"><em>The stone at Cathair mhòr</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6014"><em>Four score released at the boundary stones</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6016"><em>Two brothers of Seann Bhral on the stone</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6016"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *Two brothers of Seann Bhral on the stone* (Cathair mhòr). Among the names read at the stone's unveiling are two brothers of Seann Bhral who enlisted together and died within the same hour of the same morning.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0126"><em>The stone at Cathair mhòr</em>, 15 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6015"><em>The heading on Clach nan Rèisimeidean</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6017"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6017"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post* (Freiceadan Àth leathan). An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post by Àth leathan is spent roofing it; the men buy their slates at the western Seann Skell.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0125"><em>The seventh regiment at Àth leathan</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6016"><em>Two brothers of Seann Bhral on the stone</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6018"><em>The first market under the Caol ruadh charter</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6018"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *The first market under the Caol ruadh charter* (Caol ruadh). The first market held under Caol ruadh's new charter is held in the rain on the quay; the market-due is taken by a clerk of An t-Ionmhas under a sailcloth awning, and the fishwives sell out before noon.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0120a"><em>The market charter of Caol ruadh</em>, 26 am Faoilleach, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6017"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid's first winter at the post</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Leads to <a href="#ev-EVII-6019"><em>A plough-share of Muileann ghlas</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6019"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23** — *A plough-share of Muileann ghlas* (Muileann ghlas). The farmer of the sown field at Muileann ghlas brings the first blade turned up by his plough to the regiments' post, and the corporal enters it in a book kept for the purpose.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0127"><em>The Muileann ghlas field</em>, 28 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6018"><em>The first market under the Caol ruadh charter</em>, 31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 23</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0128"></a>**14 am Faoilleach, DE 24** — *The library's war archive sealed* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The whole record of the Long War at Leabharlann Muileann chaol is sealed against all readers for fifty years. No other archive in the kingdom's history has been sealed.
- <a id="ev-VI-0129"></a>**25 am Màrt, DE 24** — *Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Of the royal chronicle for the war years there stays open only Sìleas nic Rath's list of places, the regiments present and the counts she was allowed. Her full record went into the sealed archive with the rest.
- <a id="ev-VI-0130"></a>**6 an Giblean, DE 24** — *The cairn at Àth leathan* (Àraich Àth leathan). Tuathaich families build a cairn on the field of Àth leathan without leave. The patrols of the seventh regiment leave it standing, and every time they pass it has grown by a stone or two.
- <a id="ev-VI-0131"></a>**27 an Giblean, DE 24** — *The tithe carried forward* (Cathair dhearg). The Treasury's accounts carry the wartime tithe forward as a standing line under the regiments' pay. No minute of the council records a choice to keep it.
- <a id="ev-VI-0131a"></a>**22 an Cèitean, DE 24** — *The market-due fixed* (Cathair dhearg). The Treasury fixes the market-due at seventeen in the hundred on every sale a town makes into its market and on every sale between markets. A clerk of the Treasury is set in each of the sixteen market towns to take it and keep the market roll. The wartime tithe on dubhan stays at the pumps, on its own line.
- <a id="ev-VI-0132"></a>**26 an Cèitean, DE 24** — *The Fuel-Fitters and the regiments* (Seann Skell). The Guild of Fuel-Fitters at Seann Skell on the southern coast is given the contract for the regiments' engines and the fleets' hulls, and doubles its rolls. The charter rule holds, and all its new fitters are Dia-thìrich.
- <a id="ev-VI-0132a"></a>**20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 24** — *The regiments' arms contracts* (Àth naomh). The forges of Àth naomh in the west and Caol ìseal on the north coast, which smelt the bog-iron of their districts, take the Crown's contract for the regiments' small arms and field-guns. The forge-towns of the old vein country follow. Arms become the dearest common goods in every market of the kingdom.
- <a id="ev-VI-0133"></a>**2 an Lùnastal, DE 24** — *The second fleet off Baile ìseal* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). The second fleet runs down off Baile ìseal the raiders who took the salt-boats in the war, and brings their hulls into Seann Skell. The lighthouse log at Baile ìseal records the chase from the lamp-room.
- <a id="ev-VI-0134"></a>**29 an t-Sultain, DE 24** — *The fourth fleet in the north-west* (Spùinneadairean-mara). The fourth fleet, kept on the Tuathaich coast after the war, searches the raiders' bays off Cathair gheal and finds them empty. The fishermen of Cathair gheal say the raiders left when the fleets came and will return when they go.
- <a id="ev-VI-0135"></a>**28 an Dàmhair, DE 24** — *The third fleet's tank-hulls* (Baile ghorm). The third fleet at Baile ghorm keeps its tank-hulls after the war and runs dubhan up the west coast to the Tuathaich depots on the council's contract. The Moot pays the freight.
- <a id="ev-EVII-6020"></a>**30 an Dàmhair, DE 24** — *The council's order reaches Muileann chaol* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). A rider who has changed horses three times brings the council's four-line order to Raghnall mac Mhuirich on the doorstep of the old building: the whole record of An Cogadh Fada is to be shut against every reader for fifty years, and the keeper alone is to hold the key.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0128"><em>The library's war archive sealed</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6021"></a>**1 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *Raghnall has a room built for the seal* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Raghnall clears an old storeroom at the end of the new wing's gallery and has a mason and a smith fit it, through a fortnight of hard weather, with an oak door two inches thick and a lock made new to no other key in the kingdom, standing over the last morning's fitting himself.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0128"><em>The library's war archive sealed</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6020"><em>The council's order reaches Muileann chaol</em>, 30 an Dàmhair, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6022"></a>**4 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *Sìleas carries her full record to the door* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Over two days Sìleas nic Rath carries her own four boxes of the war's full record up from her room and sets them inside the new door herself, letting no clerk touch them: the movements, counts and letters she was never let publish alongside the open chronicle.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0128"><em>The library's war archive sealed</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0129"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6021"><em>Raghnall has a room built for the seal</em>, 1 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6023"></a>**6 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *The key turns once* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Raghnall turns the new lock himself with the mason and smith gone, and hangs the key on a cord under his own shirt, where he is seen for years after to lay his hand against his chest before he blows out the reading-room's last lamp.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0128"><em>The library's war archive sealed</em>, 14 am Faoilleach, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6022"><em>Sìleas carries her full record to the door</em>, 4 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6024"></a>**11 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *Sìleas's promise at the head of the open list* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). Sìleas writes, unasked, a line at the head of the war's open list saying plainly that the fuller record exists, is kept, and will be given to any honest reader when the fifty years end; Raghnall reads it and lets it stand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0129"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6023"><em>The key turns once</em>, 6 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6025"></a>**16 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *An seachdamh rèisimeid's captain lets the cairn stand* (Àraich Àth leathan). Asked whether to clear the cairn the Tuathaich have raised on Àraich Àth leathan, Comhairle nam Mèinnean answers that its captain may use his own judgment; he tells his patrols to walk past it and count the stones if they wish, and report only what is found beneath one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0130"><em>The cairn at Àth leathan</em>, 6 an Giblean, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6024"><em>Sìleas's promise at the head of the open list</em>, 11 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6026"></a>**18 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *A woman of Àth leathan carries a stone each morning* (Àraich Àth leathan). A woman of the town who lost a brother in the fighting there, and will not say which side he died fighting for, is seen to walk out alone before the patrol each morning, set one stone on the cairn, and stand a while with her hand flat against it before going home.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0130"><em>The cairn at Àth leathan</em>, 6 an Giblean, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6025"><em>An seachdamh rèisimeid's captain lets the cairn stand</em>, 16 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6027"></a>**23 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *Peigi nic Ascaill signs the regiments' contract* (Cathair dhearg). Peigi nic Ascaill signs Comann nan Goibhnean-ceangail' contract for the regiments' engines and the fleets' hulls at Cathair dhearg with a clerk on either hand to witness it, and tells her under-fitter afterward that no paper she has signed will put more Dia-thìrich fitters to the trade than this one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0132"><em>The Fuel-Fitters and the regiments</em>, 26 an Cèitean, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6026"><em>A woman of Àth leathan carries a stone each morning</em>, 18 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6028"></a>**25 an t-Samhain, DE 24** — *A smith of Àth naomh counts his musket-stocks* (Àth naomh). Writing to his brother at Cathair dhearg, a smith of Àth naomh says he has turned out more musket-stocks that winter than ploughshares in the six years before the war, and cannot decide whether to call it his own good fortune or the kingdom's bad one.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0132a"><em>The regiments' arms contracts</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6027"><em>Peigi nic Ascaill signs the regiments' contract</em>, 23 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6029"></a>**5 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *The forge at Caol ìseal takes on new hands* (Caol ìseal). The woman who masters the forge at Caol ìseal, left her by a father with no son to leave it to, takes on four boys and a girl under the arms contract and tells Comhairle nam Mèinnean's inspector she means to keep them past the contract's term, war or no war.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0132a"><em>The regiments' arms contracts</em>, 20 an t-Ògmhios, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6028"><em>A smith of Àth naomh counts his musket-stocks</em>, 25 an t-Samhain, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6030"></a>**7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *Seonag nic Thòmais lights the second lamp* (Taigh-solais Baile ìseal). Keeper of the trial lamp at Baile ìseal, Seonag nic Thòmais sees the salt-boat raiders' sail two hours before An dàrna cabhlach's own lookout and lights, on her own judgment, the warning lamp kept unlit in ordinary weather; the fleet's captain copies her log whole into his return.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0133"><em>The second fleet off Baile ìseal</em>, 2 an Lùnastal, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6029"><em>The forge at Caol ìseal takes on new hands</em>, 5 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6031"></a>**12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *Sìleas opens the next day's page as any other* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The morning after the lock is turned, Sìleas sets the day's date and the weather at the top of her page and writes only of a mill's copying fee, exactly as on any working morning of the thirteen years before, and says nothing there of the sealed room.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0129"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6030"><em>Seonag nic Thòmais lights the second lamp</em>, 7 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6032"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *Some forty places on the open list* (Leabharlann Muileann chaol). The open list of the war years at an Leabharlann runs to some forty places, each with its regiments and the counts allowed before the sealing, and a blank where the column's dead would stand.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0129"><em>Sìleas nic Rath's open chronicle</em>, 25 am Màrt, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6031"><em>Sìleas opens the next day's page as any other</em>, 12 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6033"></a>**16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *The quays of Baile ghorm lengthened* (Baile ghorm). For An treas cabhlach's tank-hulls the quays of Baile ghorm are lengthened by forty paces into the anchorage, the stone carted from the old wolf-posts' quarry.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0135"><em>The third fleet's tank-hulls</em>, 28 an Dàmhair, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6032"><em>Some forty places on the open list</em>, 14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6034"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *Doire shean pays the market-due* (Doire shean). At Doire shean the fixed market-due is taken for the first time; Am Buabhall Fortanach, which sells no goods at market, is found to owe it on its buffalo.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0131a"><em>The market-due fixed</em>, 22 an Cèitean, DE 24</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6033"><em>The quays of Baile ghorm lengthened</em>, 16 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6035"></a>**31 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24** — *Còmhrag Ceann leathan of Ceann leathan after the war* (Ceann leathan). At the first Còmhrag at Ceann leathan after the last pits gave up, the fair-wardens count more fighters from the shires of the middle country than in any year before, and none from the western hills.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0117"><em>The last pits give up</em>, 10 an Dùbhlachd, DE 22</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6034"><em>Doire shean pays the market-due</em>, 26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 24</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-VI-0136"></a>**23 an Giblean, DE 25** — *The creature off the cape again* (Uilebheist na Mara). The fourth fleet's log for the year records a thing longer than a patrol boat off the north-west cape, where the Tuathaich fishermen reported one in Gormshuil nic Dhùghaill's day. The log calls it a whale.
- <a id="ev-VI-0137"></a>**2 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25** — *Anna nic Phàil's motion* (Cathair dhomhain). The motion to make amends to the Tuathaich is brought into the council by Anna nic Phàil, councillor for Cathair dhomhain, on a petition of the Moot under Martha Greaves. She speaks for it once.
- <a id="ev-VI-0138"></a>**10 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25** — *The motion for amends* (Cathair dhearg). In the capital it is proposed to pay the Tuathaich for their losses in the war. The motion is let die quietly, and no vote is taken.
- <a id="ev-VI-0139"></a>**18 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25** — *The Moot's minute on the amends* (Caol mhòr). The Moot's minute on the motion for amends runs to one line: 'Allowed to die.' That same year Martha Greaves lays down the chair. The Moot chooses Peter Hale, a great-grandson of its first speaker, to follow her.
- <a id="ev-VI-0140"></a>**27 an Dàmhair, DE 25** — *The fifth regiment's barracks* (Seann Warr). The fifth regiment builds stone barracks at Seann Warr, the first lasting quarters any of the nine regiments has had. The town gives the land and takes the regiment's custom.
- <a id="ev-VI-0141"></a>**14 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *The eighth regiment at Inis uaine* (Inis uaine). The eighth regiment's guard on the eastern dubhan tanks at Inis uaine is made lasting. Its officers take houses in the town, and the Seann Spioradan house of Inis uaine adds the regiment to its prayers.
- <a id="ev-VI-0142"></a>**22 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *The fourth regiment leaves Ceann mhòr* (Caol bheag). The fourth regiment leaves the old magistrate's house at Ceann mhòr and goes home to Caol bheag. The Moot asks that the house be given to the town. It is given to the maor.
- <a id="ev-EVII-6036"></a>**23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *Anna nic Phàil cuts a page of figures from her own draft* (Cathair dhomhain). Writing her motion at her own table through the early months of the year, Anna nic Phàil cuts a whole page of named costs, granaries and flooded pit-heads and Clach nan Rèisimeidean, judging that a council grows deaf to a column of figures faster than to almost anything else brought before it.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0137"><em>Anna nic Phàil's motion</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6037"></a>**24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *The master of An t-Ionmhas asks a figure of the motion* (Cathair dhearg). Uisdean Dubh, master of An t-Ionmhas, asks Anna nic Phàil's Tagradh na h-Èirig whether its sum has been costed against the year's roll; she answers that the reckoning is the room's own trade, and asks only that the principle be granted.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0137"><em>Anna nic Phàil's motion</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6036"><em>Anna nic Phàil cuts a page of figures from her own draft</em>, 23 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6038"></a>**25 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *The motion held over, morning after morning* (Cathair dhearg). For eight sittings running the council's clerk carries Tagradh na h-Èirig forward on the day's business-paper under the same two words, held over, without any member speaking against it or any vote being called.<span class="fn fl">← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0137"><em>Anna nic Phàil's motion</em>, 2 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-VI-0138"><em>The motion for amends</em>, 10 an t-Ògmhios, DE 25</a>; ← Follows from <a href="#ev-EVII-6037"><em>The master of An t-Ionmhas asks a figure of the motion</em>, 24 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25</a>.</span>
- <a id="ev-EVII-6039"></a>**26 an Dùbhlachd, DE 25** — *Somhairle mac Lachlainn is asked whether the sum is too great* (Cathair dhearg).
